News.title: Frontman of indie-rock band charged with unlawful acts on a child under the age of 10 just days before festival gig
News.content:
'SERIOUS & DISTURBING' Frontman of indie-rock band charged with unlawful acts on a child under the age of 10 just days before festival gig







Next

A POPULAR indie-rock band’s frontman has been charged with unlawful acts involving a child under the age of 10 just days before a huge festival gig.

Mauricio “Mauri” Tapia, 26, lead singer of Los Retros, was hit with four shocking charges at an LA court on Monday – just months after performing at Coachella.



Tapia is the focus of several disturbing allegations, including claims that he took advantage of the vulnerable young victim from a position of trust.

He faces four criminal charges regarding unlawful acts with a child younger than 10 years old.



The sickening charges came just days before Los Retros were set to perform at the Stones Throw 30 music festival on Friday in the City of Angels.

The organiser later withdrew the band from the event due to “unforeseen circumstances”.



Los Retros’ label, Stones Throw Records, have subsequently distanced itself from Tapia and issued a public statement on the matter.

In a statement, they said: “Yesterday we learned of extremely serious and disturbing allegations against Mauri Tapia, professionally known as Los Retros.

“We had previously announced the cancellation of his scheduled performance at Stones Throw 30 before we were aware of these circumstances.

“In light of this information, we are taking steps to disassociate ourselves from Tapia and his work.



“We take these allegations extremely seriously and will continue to assess the situation as more information becomes available.”

The lead singer was arrested on October 8 and reportedly booked with a bail set at $3m, according to the LA Times.

He is due to appear in court on Thursday.

The singer is yet to enter a plea.

Tapia founded Los Retros in 2016 after which they became an influential act in a wave of Latino bands.



The band has more than 2.7 million monthly listeners on Spotify, with one song, “Someone to Spend Time With,” boasting more than 271 million listens.

They have released a total of three albums since 2017.

Tapia and his band played at Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in Indio this year.

News.title: Italy descends into chaos as hooded teens smash up & loot shops with PM blaming ‘hooligans’ as Europe battles more riots
News.content:
Next

ITALY has been plunged into chaos as hooded teens rampage through the streets and smash up shops in Brit holiday hotspots.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has slammed the youths as “gangs of hooligans” as waves of violent riots sweep across Europe.



Vandals smashed windows, set fires and hurled hunks of debris at riot police, transforming Milan‘s central piazza into a battleground.

Horrifying videos show balaclava-clad boys trampling on cars while taking selfies and using bins as battering rams on shopfronts.





What started as a peaceful march of around 5,000 people on Saturday over the high cost of living quickly spiralled into fiery chaos and carnage.

Gangs of youths – many of them masked – ransacked properties, looted shops and set rubbish bins on fire.

Terrified tourists fled the usually packed square – overlooked by the gleaming white duomo – to escape the violent rioters.

The mayor of Milan, Giuseppe Sala, said that he had witnessed “smashed shop windows, looted stores, and frightened citizens”.



“What happened here is what we are seeing in many cities around the world,” he told Ansa.

He added: “I’m very worried because it’s a new phenomenon, which also originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself.”

Around 70 people have been detained across the weekend of riot hell, according to news outlet Ansa.



Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni slammed the vandals as “thugs who exploit demonstrations to spread chaos, attack those who guarantee security, and hold entire cities hostage”.

She thanked police officers for protecting citizens, business owners and workers “who have the right to live in their city without fear and without seeing it ravaged by gangs of hooligans.”

“To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not” she wrote on X.

Police battled the crowds on Sunday by firing water cannons and unleashing tear gas before charging into the luxury shopping arcade of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II where some rioters had gathered.

Police said 104 cops were injured in Milan and a total of 72 suspects – many of them minors – had been dragged to the city’s police station.



Damage from the violent unrest is estimated to cost taxpayers around half a million euros, according to Marco Barbieri, general secretary of the Confcommercio business association.

Violence also broke out in Rome, Turin and Bologna with a total of 197 suspects identified or detained over the clashes.

Rocks and eggs were pelted at police in Turin while firecrackers and small homemade bombs were launched at the education ministry’s HQ in Rome.

Bologna’s railway station was engulfed by thugs with rioters hurling bottles and barricading roads with rubbish bins.

An emergency meeting to tackle the rioting has been scheduled for Monday, PM Meloni announced.



Students are clashing with law enforcement in unprecedented scenes of unrest across Europe.

In France, Macron has blasted “far-left extremists” for ravaging the country by burning down buildings and looting shops with abandon.

More than half a million people took to the streets on Saturday over the cost of living – but the marches again erupted into chaos with one protestor losing his life in the apocalyptic destruction.

Hundreds of anti-fascist protestors also clashed with police in Brussels, Belgium on Saturday.

And in Lisbon, Portugal tens of thousands marched against soaring living costs and an escalating housing crisis.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Protests continued into their sixth day in Albania with furious citizens demanding the resignation of prime minister Edi Rama over allegations of corruption.

Rama has denied the accusations and said he will remain in post.

News.title: Killer cop to be executed for burning man alive in ‘most heinous and cruel murder’ sparked by bitter love triangle
News.content:
DEATH SENTENCE Killer cop to be executed for burning man alive in ‘most heinous and cruel murder’ sparked by bitter love triangle







Next

A KILLER police officer has been sentenced to death for a horrifying murder sparked by twisted jealousy.

Otto Lenke, 67, was handed the death sentence in St. Lucie County, Florida, on Wednesday for the murder of mechanic Richard Benson, 57, on February 17, 2021.



The jury heard how Lenke drove 40 minutes to Fast Frank’s Cycle Concepts and waited a further 20 minutes before walking in and shooting Benson in the back three times at point blank range.

Lenke then poured two containers of denatured alcohol over Benson and lit him on fire while he was still alive.



He also dragged Benson back as he had tried to crawl helplessly to the door to escape.

The entire attack, including the preparation, was captured on surveillance footage that left detectives speechless.

read more on news RESCUE MISSION Horror as sharks attack survivors of capsized boat with 11 still missing

“‘I remember being in a room with the Indian River County Sheriff’s detectives, probably with over 100 years of combined experience, and their jaws dropped when they saw this video because it was probably one of the most heinous things we’ve ever seen,” Assistant State Attorney Brandon White told Treasure Coast News.

Circuit Court Judge Michael Linn described the murder as “one of the most heinous, atrocious, and cruel ways imaginable”.

Linn said that Lenke had “executed a cold and calculated plan” to commit kill Benson after a love triangle turned deadly.



Benson was dating a woman Lenke had previously been in a relationship with and prosecutors argued that Lenke’s main motive for the killing was jealousy.

Lisa Diggs, Lenke’s former girlfriend, helped identify him in surveillance tapes thanks to his “particular walk”, among other things.

Harrowing surveillance footage from the scene showed Lenke removing his license plate tag before carrying out the brutal attack.

Lenke, who had known Diggs for a decade at the time of the murder, had been in contact with her months before the murder.

On January 19, he delivered a handmade wooden boat to his former lover, at which point he asked “why she did not love him and asked if it was because she was seeing someone.”



Prosecutors say it was this interaction that sparked his jealousy to the point of murder.

He was jailed two days later and a jury made up of seven women and five men convicted him of first-degree murder in May.

Despite the death sentence ruling, his case will still need to be reviewed by the state Supreme Court, per Florida law.

News.title: Attacks on waiters, shock tactics & even stealing with KIDS… Britain’s dine & dash plague driving restaurants to brink
News.content:
Next

BRAZEN dine and dashers are plaguing Britain’s restaurants – and poor staff say they’re left helpless.

Waiters and managers have been forced to face off with a plauge of opportunistic criminals and some have been left battered and bruised from run-ins with violent dine and dashers.



New stats obtained by The Sun reveal Britain is awash with dine and dash heists.

The cuisine thieves order huge feasts before legging it and ditching the bill, costing restaurants thousands.





UKHospitality – a trade body – told us that a third of members have experienced a dine and dash incident and almost half of those reckon there’s been an increase.

We spoke to restaurant owners at their wits end with the situation.



We have reported on a waiter being left in A&E by a suspected dine & dasher, entire families with kids brazenly stealing, and tactics such as getaway cars and even picking out their own hairs to avoid paying the bill.

Earlier this year The Sun exclusively shared CCTV footage showing a couple necking 14 Baby Guinness shots before apparently running out on their £230 bill at The Halfway House, Essex.

General manager Deanne Perkins, 45, said the restaurant has been targeted twice this year alone



She told us: “That’s all I see on our social media, it seems to be happening everywhere. It’s crazy.

“It has a big impact. We’re a small family-run business so obviously it hits us hard. We’re not a big chain or anything.

“Every loss is a real kick in the teeth. And obviously it really upsets the staff because they’re on minimum wage, they work really hard. And then you get people walking out.

“It just makes obviously staff on edge a little bit because we’re a table service restaurant. But it shouldn’t be like that.

“You’re trying to give good customer service, not trying to think ‘oh, are they going to run out after eating?’



“It’s just extremely frustrating and disappointing. If you can’t afford to eat out, don’t do it.”

Earlier this year cops were called to La Delizia, in Hastings after a group legged it without paying their £146 bill.

The culprits devoured their entire meal before claiming there was a issue with the food and refusing to pay.

Their owner, Franco Esposito told The Sun: “We’ve had trouble at La Delizia but even more issues at our other restaurant down the road.

“After one incident I called the police but they never came so I had to deal with everything myself.



“No one looks after us when we’re in trouble, I have to sort it out myself.”

The Sun also heard from Relentless – Steak and Lobster House in Portsmouth.

The owner, Scott Mathews, reckons the problem is getting worse and has resorted to charging customers before their meal to crackdown on the incidents.

In February 2026 two customers legged it without paying for their £170 bill after feasting on oysters and booze.

On another occasion fleeing visitors dodged an £800 bill.



He said: “It’s a frustration when the police turn up and they can’t do anything, the law needs to change.

“We had £800 worth of losses from a dine and dash, that’s two and a half people’s wages at the time.

“Dine and dashers should be prosecuted across the board and not dealt with as a petty crime.

“It’s on the rise massively, everyone’s after something for nothing so we’ve got cameras above every table now.

“Alcohol is the only thing police can make them pay for by law, so they order tap water to get around it.



“They come out for a slap up meal and it’s become a bit of a game for them.”

In Manchester, a young waitress was rushed to A&E after she was allegedly attacked by a “violent man” after she confronted a group over an unpaid bill at Noodle Alley.

It’s the second time in two months the restaurant has been targeted, previously revealing footage of a man in flip flops who fled without paying.

Over in Wales, a couple were jailed for fleeing restaurant bills amounting to over £1,000 in 2024.

Bernard McDonagh, 41, and his wife Ann McDonagh, 39, were caught on camera striking at a string of five eateries across Wales.



The duo were sent to the slammer for 20 months after pleading guilty to five counts of fraud at Swansea Magistrates’ Court.

Dine and dasher Johnny Delaney was caught on camera leaving Stubbs, a steak and seafood eatery in Ashford, Kent, last November, without paying a penny of his £250 bill.

He was then sentenced to a 12-month community order, and a combined bill of £1,996.82.

UKHospitality CEO Allen Simpson: “Any customers walking out of restaurants without paying is simply unacceptable and shows a complete lack of respect towards businesses and teams that work incredibly hard to provide guests with good service, good food and good experiences.

“Deliberately leaving without paying is a criminal offence, and businesses should not be left out of pocket because of this kind of behaviour.



“We would encourage any operators who experience walkouts to report it to the police.”

A National Police Chiefs’ Council spokesperson said: “We know that theft can have a significant impact on individuals, businesses and communities, which is why policing is committed to tackling all forms of this criminality.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Dine and dash type offences are largely opportunistic in nature and we would encourage all business owners and staff to make sure that when they do happen, they are reported so their local force can take action.

“While policing will always follow all possible lines of enquiry to identify and pursue offenders, any tools like CCTV can greatly assist with this.”

News.title: Frustrated locals make life-size knitted traffic officers in bid to catch out reckless drivers speeding through village
News.content:
STITCH 'EM UP Frustrated locals make life-size knitted traffic officers in bid to catch out reckless drivers speeding through village







Next

FRUSTRATED locals have turned to unusual methods to tackle speeding in their area, creating knitted mannequins to deter reckless motorists.

Members of the Knit and Natter group in Fillongley, Warwickshire, have scattered the lifesize figures around the village to slow drivers down.



Woollen children carrying road safety messages and an RAF figure pointing a speed gun are among the creations.

Elsewhere, knitted zebras line a key crossing in the town while a woollen tortoise encourages drivers to check their speed.



The displays come amid rising concerns about road safety, particularly on busy crossroads including the village’s main junction on Nuneaton Road.

Residents were frustrated by the length of time it was taking for a permanent solution to rampant speeding in the area.

According to Warwickshire County Council, 11 road accidents have been recorded at the junction over the past four years.

Ecologist Tom Docker, who has lived in the village for a year, says the figures have been a triumph.



“I think it’s a really good initiative,” said the 42-year-old.

“It speaks to the creativity of the local community, it’s really good that they’ve turned their attention to problems in the village.

“Speeding is an issue and we’ve had quite a lot of accidents here in recent years.

“We have a primary school just off the junction and there isn’t a crossing point for them, and that lack of crossing is going to end in tears one day I think.”

But while the mannequins have amused many, the striking RAF character has now vanished in a disappointing turn of events.



Heather Badham, parish clerk and a member of the knitting group, said she was saddened by the news.

“Someone’s stolen it between 7.10am and 8.05am and I’m gutted for the ladies that knitted that, because of the amount of work that went into it,” she said.

“This is a piece of village heritage and it’s just been taken by somebody.”

The blue-uniformed figure was originally used in a D-Day celebration, representing the dads of one of the knitters.

She added that silly as they might be, the figures were in fact having an effect on drivers, who were seen braking as they approached the knitted speed gun.



“They think it’s an actual speed camera and they slow down,” she said.

Traffic lights at the crossroads were approved by the council earlier this year, but some locals have pushed for speed cameras instead.

The authority said it was mulling over a range of safety measures at the critical junction.

Warwickshire Police and Crime Commissioner Philip Seccombe said Fillongley remained one of the county’s collision hotspots and acknowledged concerns about road safety in the village.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile, members of knitting group have reported the missing figure to police and are considering creating a replacement.

News.title: ‘How can French people do this to France?’ Macron blasts rioters as he warns violence to be met with severe consequences
News.content:
Next

EMMANUEL Macron has blasted rioters who “ravaged” France in violent protests as he warned serious consequences will be handed out.

The French president denounced the “far-left” hooligans who looted and burned down buildings, questioning how French people could do so much damage to their own country.



In an address to the nation Macron said: “Public buildings, shops and town halls were attacked and in some cases destroyed.

“Many hundreds of police officers were injured. When we saw the images, we all thought, what was in their heads? How can French people do this to France?



“We are all feeling anger and shame tonight. To see the cities, the streets of our cities, ransacked like this is unbearable.”

He blamed “agitators from far-Left fringe groups, joined by numerous criminals” for plunging his country into “unbridled violence.”



He said there is “nothing that justifies” the riots and damage caused.

But as Mr Macron’s speech continued, rioters and looters returned to the streets of central Paris to continue their battle with police.

Gangs of youths in balaclavas, on Sunday evening, could be heard chanting “everyone hates the police” as they set up barricades on major roads, such as the Rue de Rivoli.

One person who asked to remain anonymous said: “We are here because we want Macron to resign.”



They said the police are out to wound them, if not kill them, but they will continue to fight back.

In his speech Macron said the hooligans “will answer for what they have done”.

He said: “Those who destroyed must pay, those who looted must reimburse.”

Macron explained that the aim of the meeting is to “mobilise support for all who are going through difficult times”.



He continued: “Right now, we need to be very clear-minded.

“We need to look at what was expressed in the country.

“Several hundreds of thousands of our compatriots demonstrated with legitimate claims.



“We should never confuse the demonstrators with those who broke things and rioted and looted.”

Macron said he was particularly devastated at Limoges City Hall being burnt, along with a tourist office in Lyon.

He said the storming of Marseille city hall, and the attack on the Prefect’s Residence in Bordeaux can never be repeated.



The president concluded his address with a call for “calm and respect”.

French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu is due to chair a crisis meeting on Monday to discuss the next steps and recovery measures.

More than half a million people took to the streets across the country on Saturday as furious demonstrations over the cost of living descended into more chaos today.

One person died and more than 2,000 had been arrested across France, according to the Minister of the Interior, Laurent Nuñez.

Nuñez said 600 police, firefighters and paramedics have also been injured.



French police admitted they “lost control” of major cities during the weekend of “apocalyptic rioting”.

A high-ranking officer told Sunday’s Le Parisien newspaper: “‘Law enforcement was unable to contain the multitude of simultaneous attacks occurring across the country, and was quickly overwhelmed by determined protesters.”

He said there simply was not enough personnel or ammunition to tackle the threat.

Prime minister Sebastian Lecornu shared Marcon’s disdain and last night said: “Peaceful demonstrations have a rightful place in our Republic. Arson, looting, and attacks do not.

“Today, far-Left groups orchestrated violence in several French cities – criminals joined in to loot and destroy.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Left-wing politicians deny stirring up any trouble and blamed paramilitary police units for provoking the crowds.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of France Unbowed (FLI) said too many tear gas canisters had been fired at peaceful demonstrators.

News.title: Man dead after being hit by car during police chase over ‘dangerous driving’ on major motorway as one arrested
News.content:
FATAL CRASH Man dead after being hit by car during police chase over ‘dangerous driving’ on major motorway as one arrested







Next

A MOTORCYCLIST has died after he was hit by a car as he tried to flee on foot during a police chase across a major motorway.

The pursuit began on the M60 near Stockport as officers made “tactical contact” with the biker after he was caught driving recklessly.

Officers in Manchester had originally followed the motorbike because it was driving in a “dangerous manner” around 7:30pm.

The chase continued until the driver of the motorbike “made off on foot across the motorway”, where he was then hit by a car.





The driver was pronounced dead at the scene.

Another man involved in the crash has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by careless driving when under the influence, and causing death by driving uninsured.

The motorway was shut for about 12 hours after the death and re-opened this morning, with some motorists stuck on the road for several hours.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct has launched an investigation due to “police contact” prior to the fatality.

Tactical contact is a legal police strategy used to stop fleeing drivers by purposely bumping or forcing their vehicle.

In a statement, Greater Manchester Police said: “Shortly before 7.30pm on Saturday 17 October 2026, officers on patrol observed a red coloured motorbike being driven in a dangerous manner on the M60 clockwise around Stockport Pyramid.

“Officers then began following the vehicle, which was posing a significant risk to members of the public using the motorway.

“A pursuit commenced and continued onto the M56.



“During the pursuit, tactical contact was made with the motorcycle at low speed on the hard shoulder near Junction 5.

“After the motorcycle was brought to a stop between junctions 3 and 4 of the M56, the driver made off on foot across the motorway and was subsequently involved in a collision with another vehicle.

“North West Ambulance Service attended the scene, and the driver of the motorbike, a man, received emergency medical treatment.

“Despite the best efforts of medical professionals, he was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.

“A man involved in a collision, but who was not involved in the initial pursuit, was arrested at the scene on suspicion of causing death by careless driving when under the influence of drink or drugs and causing death by driving uninsured.



“In-line with standard procedure following a fatality after police contact, Greater Manchester Police has referred the matter to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) and they have decided an independent investigation is required, to establish the full circumstances of the incident.

“We await the conclusion of their investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Officers from our Serious Collisions Investigation Unit are now appealing for information regarding the incident to assist with our investigation.

“Anyone with information, Dash Cam, or CCTV footage is urged to contact Greater Manchester Police on 101 and quote log 2974-17/10/26. Reports can also be made via the LiveChat function at gmp.police.uk.”

News.title: Sick nude pictures of dead college student, 19, ‘sent in texts by man who drugged and raped her’ instead of calling 911
News.content:
Next

HORRIFYING new details have emerged about the death of a fashion student who was allegedly drugged and raped in her dorm room.

Annabel Richter, 19, from Brazil, was studying at the Fashion Institute of Technology in New York when she fell into a coma and died following the alleged attack.



Moises Freire, 19, has now been charged with distributing fentanyl disguised as cocaine with the intent to commit rape following the March 18 incident.

Federal prosecutors say the Bronx teen, who was not a student at the college, tricked Richter and her friend into taking the deadly drug by claiming it was pure cocaine from Mexico.



The pair both immediately lost consciousness inside their dorm room and Freire then raped Richter who died in hospital three days later, according to the Manhattan US Attorney’s Office.

As her family pay tribute to the “bright and beautiful young woman,” officials say Freire texted nude pictures of his victims to pals rather than call 911.

Images allegedly sent during this sickening 45-minute delay before calling for campus security include a picture of Richter naked from the waist down, newly unsealed court docs state.

Prosecutors claimed Freire lied to campus security saying that both women drank too much and lost consciousness.



They further claim he told security that he failed to realize Richter had passed out until after he finished having sex with her.

“It is truly hard to believe that the defendant, who seemed entirely coherent and sober at the time, who didn’t have any of the substance, who is captured on the security guard’s body-worn camera seeming coherent and sober, didn’t know what was going on when he was having sex with the victim who was completely unconscious,” prosecutor Ariana Bloom said at hearing in April.

Both women were given Narcan by emergency services before being rushed to hospital.

“Annabel was full of life,” her mom Flavia Rocha, told The New York Post.

“She knew loads about music and art and had a contagious laughter. Her presence filled the room.



“For us, her family and her friends, she was and always will be, our beloved Bel.”

Despite her parents’ mad dash to get to New York after learning what happened, they never got to say goodbye to their daughter, one student told the Daily Mail.

Her surviving roommate has withdrawn from the fashion college and has not been identified.

Brian Peralta Cabrera, 18, of Queens, has also been charged with conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance resulting in death and serious bodily injury after allegedly helping supply Freire with the drugs.

Court documents allege he told Cabrera that he wanted substances that “would last the entire night”.



The pair were initially arrested in March and pleaded not guilty to earlier charges that did not include the rape allegation against Freire.

Freire is due back in court on October 28 for arraignment on the upgraded charge of distributing a controlled substance with the intent to commit rape.

He is being held without bail pending a March 2027 trial.

His attorney, Mitchell Schwartz, previously described Richter’s death as a tragedy but disputed suggestions that his client had deliberately drugged the students.

He argued that the events leading up to the overdoses amounted to “a story of teenagers doing what I would call ‘dumb teenager things.’”



His attorney previously told the court that he and Richter had a consensual “sexual relationship” in the year before she died.

New York Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch branded the defendants’ alleged actions “truly unconscionable.”

“As alleged in the indictment, the two defendants supplied the fentanyl that killed one young woman and nearly killed another,” Tisch said.

“Rather than immediately seek help, Freire allegedly first raped the incapacitated victim who died and then lied to first responders.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“These actions are as sick and twisted as they come.”



If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call RAINN (Rape, Abuse, & Incest National Network) at 800-656-HOPE (4673).

News.title: Polanski says he will not overturn Green Party's 'Zionism is racism' motion
News.content:
Zack Polanski has said he will not overturn a motion passed by Green Party members that declared Zionism a form of racism.

The Green leader told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, it would be party policy until 2028.

The motion, passed at the party's conference earlier this month, described Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".

It divided the party and sparked a major backlash from MPs, Jewish campaigners, the government and the European Green movement, with the equality watchdog writing to the party for more information on it.

The fallout from the motion overshadowed the final days of Polanski's campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, in which he came second to Labour, and threatened his leadership.

He came under criticism for not voting on the motion which was passed by 1,022 votes to 813 - a small fraction of the party's 230,000 members - in Brighton earlier this month.

The motion also asserted the party's backing for "a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine", a full arms embargo on Israel and a commitment to Palestinian liberation.

Asked if he would now step in as leader to overturn it, Polanski said: "I'm not going to try to overturn it.

"At the first available opportunity, I do want to amend it - I want to move away from one state, towards saying that Israelis and Palestinians should decide that future for themselves."

He said this would not be until 2028 as "you can't [amend it] within the rules, so when you vote on something in our party conference that's then policy for two years".

Kuenssberg asked if he would therefore change the rules as leader, but Polanski said: "I think if members have made a decision, then I respect the democratic will of our members."

Former Green Party co-leader and current MP Adrian Ramsay responded by calling for action to be taken sooner.

"I don't think it's tenable for us to continue the next two years with this policy that's been adopted given the huge political distraction that it's been for our councillors across the country," he told the BBC News Channel.

"One way forward could be to have a ballot of all party members to establish very clearly where does the party as a whole stand - my view is we would see a different answer."

Polanski had previously said he would not have voted for the motion without two amendments.

The first of these would have avoided "determining there was a single democratic state", and the other would have specified that the motion should not be used to discipline Jewish Green members who attend synagogues that consider themselves Zionist.

Both of these amendments were voted down by members at the party's conference.

Green MPs, including Ellie Chowns, have called for the party's member-led decision-making procedures to be reviewed given how few people took part in the vote.

News.title: Watch: Police hunt for synthetic drugs in Chicago jail
News.content:
Chicago's largest jail, and the largest single use jail in America, is Cook County.

In 2023 it saw a spike in overdose deaths. The facility, which averages one or two overdose deaths a year, lost eight inmates that year to fatal seizures. Security footage shows prisoners spasming and collapsing.

Traditional drugs were usually brought into the jail in body cavities, so the jail had the same body scanners you find at airports to prevent that happening. However, a new way of drugs entering the prison was uncovered. Drugs were being mailed into the jail soaked in the paper of the pages of books and in letters.

The BBC's Quentin Sommerville joined corrections officers at Cook County as they prepared for an early morning raid on the jail's high security D block.

To understand the challenge that authorities face in tackling the problem the BBC interviewed a former inmate and dealer, who explained how synthetic drugs can be made in the US using household ingredients and how this could change the demand for drugs from outside of the country.

News.title: Ending corridor care in hospitals for children a priority, says health secretary
News.content:
The health secretary has asked the NHS to draw up urgent plans to speed up ending hospital "corridor care" for children.

Yvette Cooper told the BBC there would be new standards for caring for children in A&E in England, with figures collected on corridor care by age for the first time.

She was speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg where the programme highlighted the case of two-year-old Finlay Roberts who died in 2024 after spending hours in a hospital corridor before being discharged.

The health secretary has announced Â£140m to improve urgent care in England ahead of what she said would be a "more difficult" winter than usual.

The government has already pledged to end corridor care for all patients by the end of this parliament, and now Cooper has said eradicating it for children would be prioritised.

Corridor care refers to patients receiving treatment or waiting in corridors, waiting rooms or other hospital areas due to a lack of appropriate space.

The health secretary was also asked if the government would meet a key manifesto pledge that 92% of patients would start treatment within 18 weeks of booking a hospital appointment by 2029.

"That remains our manifesto commitment and of course we're going to keep working towards it," Cooper said.

Pushed further on whether the target was achievable, she replied: "The whole point about having the targets is about having something stretching that we work towards."

The 18-week target has consistently not been met for more than a decade.

Cooper said that the NHS was dealing with a number of challenges after record A&E admissions following heatwaves over the summer.

According to the latest figures for England, an estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.

On the programme the story of Finlay Roberts, was highlighted. He died after being discharged from hospital in 2024 following hours spent in an A&E corridor in north London.

Finlay's father David told the BBC the situation was a "terrible mess", with the family moved into a room with a bed before being moved back into the corridor.

"He just clung to me, as we now know, slowly dying," he said.

Liz Roberts, Finlay's mother, said corridor care "robs people of their dignity when they are at their most vulnerable". She recalled being told to administer a suppository to her son in the corridor.

Cooper apologised to Finlay's parents on behalf of the NHS, saying: "No child should be treated in a corridor. No patient should be treated in a corridor."

News.title: Suspects hunted after police officer injured in shooting
News.content:
Detectives are searching for two suspects who fled after a police officer was shot in Nottingham city centre.

Nottinghamshire Police said the officer had approached two suspects in Angel Row shortly before 04:50 BST on Sunday.

The officer is in a stable condition in hospital, where he is receiving treatment for a wound to his foot, the force added.

Detectives said a man and a woman had fled the scene and that a firearm, which could be seen within the cordon, had been found.

Angel Row remained closed by a large police scene until Sunday evening.

Police cars were parked along the road, which is lined by fast food stores and shops, and orange traffic cones had been laid out alongside items left on the road.

The cordon had also been extended to St James's Street, where an officer is standing guard.

The force said there would be a heightened police presence as the investigation continued.

News.title: Man, 80, who died in light aircraft crash near Loch Lomond named
News.content:
An 80-year-old man who died in a light aircraft crash is understood to be flying instructor Ian Haggis.

He and a 16-year-old boy died when their plane came down near Loch Lomond. The teenager's identity has not been released.

The pair had flown out from Glasgow Airport at 16:17 and stopped transmitting at 16:37, a few miles north east of the village of Drymen near Stirling.

Emergency services were called to the crash at about 16:45 on Friday.

Both of them were pronounced dead at the scene.

Temporary airspace restrictions are currently in place over the area while the Air Accidents Investigation Branch (AAIB) carries out its inquiries.

Old Drymen Road, near the scene of the crash, remains closed with vehicles being turned around and hillwalkers rerouted.

News.title: Watch: Pope thanks well-wishers in first event after cancer surgery
News.content:
Pope Leo XIV held his first public engagement since his lung cancer surgery on Sunday, as he recited the Angelus prayer from the window of Vatican's Apostolic Palace.

The surgery had taken place just a few days before, after Pope Leo had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.

After the prayer, he thanked the people who have prayed for him in recent days and said he appreciated the support. He added he will now gradually return to his commitments as he recovers.

Read more about the Pope's cancer diagnosis.

News.title: Photos show luxury boat with 50m pool and water slides near Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
News.content:
An 80m (263ft) luxury vessel has been repeatedly spotted in satellite images off North Korea's Wonsan coast from July to mid-October this year.

What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end.

After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula.

This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family.

It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC.

The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size.

News.title: NHS data breaches a disgrace, health secretary says
News.content:
NHS staff accessing the medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims and possible breaches over a man killed by a tiger is a "disgrace", the health secretary has said.

Speaking to the BBC, Yvette Cooper said she expected action to be taken against staff who had breached NHS data and privacy standards.

Her comments came after Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had sacked a total of 15 members of staff and Yorkshire Ambulance Service said William Chapman's medical records may have been accessed illegitimately.

Dr Manjeet Shehmar, NUH medical director, previously said there was "simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason".

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Cooper said "there's got to be proper respect for patients" from NHS staff.

"Let me be really clear about this," she said. "There are proper data and privacy standards across the NHS."

Students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020.

NUH said in May that it had sacked 11 members of staff for inappropriately accessing the victims' medical records, and had informed the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) and Nottinghamshire Police of the investigation.

At the time, the ICO told the BBC it would "assess any evidence provided by the trust in due course and consider our next steps", while police said there was "no criminal investigation".

In its update about further dismissals on Friday, NUH said it had taken action against "doctors, nurses, registered healthcare professionals and other staff", and that independent regulators such as the Nursing and Midwifery Council and General Medical Council, the ICO and Nottinghamshire Police had been informed.

NUH added a new system, currently under testing, was being implemented to protect patient records in future and alert the trust to potential breaches.

News.title: Boy, 14, stabbed in shopping centre attack
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy has been stabbed in a car park at Manchester's Arndale Centre shopping mall.

Greater Manchester Police said the boy was injured on the ninth floor of the Arndale Centre car park just after 15:00 BST on Saturday.

The force said his injuries were not believed to be life threatening or life changing. The Arndale was closed for several hours after the stabbing.

Det Insp Sam Jones said: "This is believed to be an isolated incident with no risk to the wider public."

News.title: West Midlands Police officer who accessed police records 2,000 times sacked
News.content:
An officer who inappropriately accessed police records more than 2,000 times has been sacked for gross misconduct.

A West Midlands Police misconduct hearing acknowledged PC Shannon Parsons felt "isolated and disconnected" due to working part-time and returning from maternity leave, but had breached standards of professional behaviour.

Parsons had claimed there was a policing purpose to her searches, the panel said, and was seeking to "keep herself up to date, informed and was often in a position to support and assist other colleagues in operational matters".

However, chair of the panel Debra Tedds concluded the searches were carried out for the officer's "own personal benefit".

As a result, Parsons was dismissed without notice and barred from future work in policing.

The searches took part over a period of about five years, the panel heard, and many included incidents near her home address.

Parsons had an otherwise unblemished career in policing in the West Midlands, lasting 13 years, but was said to show no insight or remorse "as to the potential harm that has been caused by accessing the amount of information over a significant time period," according to the panel's report.

News.title: BBC pauses civil service secondment scheme
News.content:
The BBC says it will pause secondments of government statisticians to its fact checking service, BBC Verify, and review their roles.

Since 2018 the BBC has offered six-month secondment opportunities for up to two civil servant statisticians to work for BBC News's head of statistics.

A BBC spokesperson said: "All BBC journalism and editorial decisions are made by BBC journalists and editors, in line with the BBC's editorial guidelines, so the statisticians never make editorial decisions."

Those currently on secondment would not be involved in the publication of news or content during the review and the current round of recruitment will be paused while the role is reviewed, the corporation added.

The decision follows a report in The Telegraph which said embedded civil servants had been engaging in editorial tasks and raised questions about a breach of impartiality rules.

The spokesperson added that the BBC "takes independence and transparency incredibly seriously, and we must ensure we are meeting the highest standards".

They said although statisticians' work had sometimes been recognised with their names on the BBC website, "they never made editorial decisions".

According to The Telegraph, external, a job advert for the 2027 secondment said a successful candidate would have "the ability to influence decision making, working with credibility and proactively with customers to share knowledge and information".

A now-removed blog post written by one civil servant about their placements showed a secondee describing how they had drafted copy for the news website.

Under the scheme, it is understood that statisticians explain data in writing that can be incorporated into stories, but they do not write the copy itself.

Secondees' contributions can be incorporated into journalism that scrutinises the current government, as well as all political parties.

The seconded statisticians also have to adhere to the Civil Service Code of Practice for Statistics. It requires them to present and use data and statistics objectively and not to withhold or misrepresent data due to political or commercial influence.

News.title: Man arrested after boy, 16, dies in crash
News.content:
A man has been arrested after a 16-year-old boy was killed in a crash in Birmingham.

Police said the teenager was in a white Seat Ibiza which was understood to have hit railings on Shaftmoor Lane at about 20:30 BST on Saturday.

A second passenger, a boy in his teens, was taken to hospital with a serious arm injury.

A 19-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of causing death and serious injury by dangerous driving and failing to provide a breath specimen, West Midlands Police said.

The force stated the 16-year-old boy who lost his life was pronounced dead at the scene, in the Acocks Green area, despite the best efforts of paramedics.

It appealed for information, adding specialist officers from the serious collision investigation unit were asking anyone who had dashcam footage from around the time of the crash to get in touch.

News.title: 'Learning to read in my 80s has changed my life'
News.content:
An 86-year-old man said learning to read has enabled him to read his and his wife's anniversary cards for the first time in 65 years.

Alan Hannay, from Dibden Purlieu, learned to read through the charity Read Easy, which helps adults across the country who struggle with the skill many of us take for granted.

Hannay told BBC Radio Solent: "It's changed my whole life, my confidence, changed my family life and everything around me.

"It's one of the best experiences I've ever had in my life."

Hannay said he now reads every morning for about an hour and a half and goes to the class twice a week.

"I enjoy it so much now," he said.

The charity said Hannay is an "inspiring example of determination and courage".

It said he asked his local library in Hythe, Southampton, about learning to read, which led him to the charity and his reading coach, Angie.

During his working life as a professional chauffeur, he relied on his memory to drive his clients around London, and at the age of 70 he attended evening classes to improve his reading.

However, he found the group situation difficult.

News.title: House that looks like boulders to be built on moor
News.content:
Plans for a house designed to look like rocks on a famous Yorkshire moor have been approved.

The contemporary structure, which has large irregular-shaped windows and a natural outdoor pool, looks similar to the landmark Cow and Calf Rocks in Ilkley, West Yorkshire.

The house will be built on green belt land which is the garden of a home off Heber's Ghyll Drive, and will be eco-friendly, to an ultra-low energy standard called Passivhaus.

Harrogate-based architects Shaw & Jagger said the scheme was eventually passed by HM Planning Inspectorate through the country house clause, which allows development on green belt for buildings of "exceptional quality".

The architect Matt Masserella-Gill was commissioned to design the home by the landowner David Rasche.

He said the design was "arguably the most complex country house application ever made in this country".

The house has been named Fomorian - meaning a supernatural race of giants in Irish mythology - taking inspiration from the mythical giant Rombald who is told to have lived on Ilkley Moor.

Masserella-Gill said: "The design approach was to propose a scheme that is intrinsically linked to the spirit of its place. Fomorian is of its place, part of the moors, its geology and its spirit.

"We took cues from local folklore, the surrounding rocks; ancient carvings, standing stones and escarpments that are synonymous with the landscape."

News.title: Three officers injured after lorry crashes into police vehicle
News.content:
Three police officers have been injured in County Down after a lorry they were pursuing drove on the wrong side of the road and collided with their vehicle at speed.

A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of driving while unfit through drink or drugs, driving while disqualified and dangerous driving.

A police vehicle was extensively damaged but the officers injuries are thought not to be serious at this time.

The incident began following a report of a blue articulated lorry swerving on Moygannon Road in the Warrenpoint area shortly before 23:30 BST.

"Officers responded and located a lorry matching the description on the Derryleckagh Road, Newry," said Ch Insp Will Brown.

When signalled to stop, the lorry then made off "at speed and on the wrong side of the road", before smashing into a police vehicle and continuing towards Rostrevor.

Brown continued: "The lorry later came to a stop in the Water Street area of Rostrevor where the driver, aged 36, made off on foot but was detained by officers following a short foot chase."

He remains in custody.

Brown said: "Our officers put themselves on the front line to help keep people safe. Thankfully, no one sustained more serious injuries during this incident, including officers and other road users."

News.title: The ‘absurd’ part of this Arsenal team that can help champions defend their Premier League crown
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Modern football is a game of two parts: the first hour or so, dictated by carefully curated gameplans and training ground patterns; and the final half-hour when a flurry of substitutes come on, rigid structures fade away and a match opens at the seams. Arsenal were dire for most of this game at the City Ground, shut out by Nottingham Forest’s red wall. But yet again the power of Mikel Arteta’s “finishers” decided a match.

Noni Madueke was sent on at half-time for Eberechi Eze, who had been statuesque at his station on the left touchline, which, in fairness, is not his position. With the clock ticking towards 80 minutes, Madueke did what Eze hadn’t and drove at Forest’s defence before unleashing a shot, which took a fortunate deflection off Jair Cunha on its way past the helpless Matz Sels. It went down as Arsenal’s only shot on target, and in truth it might have been curling wide.

This was the third game in a row in which Arteta rang the changes in the second half as his team struggled to click, after Leeds last weekend and Lille in midweek. Once again he made a triple substitution on 65 minutes, sending on Jurrien Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyokeres, and once again a stubborn defence was worn down in the final stages. No Premier League side has generated more goals and assists from the bench since the start of last season.

open image in gallery Noni Madueke scored the only goal of the game ( Reuters )

Forest were excellent in their determination to blunt Arsenal’s attack. Like Eze, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka had little joy, and Oliver Glasner took positives from a performance of cohesion and spirit. Liam Delap was a brilliant nuisance in attack and could have equalised in the final minutes but for Ezri Konsa’s last-ditch block. Murillo nearly scored the goal of the season, dribbling in from the left touchline before curling just over the bar with one of the last kicks. But Forest remain third from bottom after a third successive defeat, and their wait for a first home goal of the season goes on.

Arsenal, meanwhile, stay second, three points behind Manchester City and two ahead of Brighton. Second might be enough for first when City are eventually sanctioned. And even if Arsenal endure more struggles like they did for the majority of this game, strength in depth may prove the difference between the champions and the rest.

“If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench, it’s absurd,” said Madueke, after a game in which fellow substitutes Max Dowman, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly weren’t needed. “We know that we’re going to start some [games] and finish some, and for me it’s the same mentality every time: I just want to create or score.

“All 20-something players are elite and of the highest level. It’s great to have that type of competition, you know on the bench you’re ready to have an impact.”

Arteta added: “Some of them played three days ago and some of them will start the next game, and they know that everyone has to be at it. If you are needed after 60 minutes, 45 minutes and sometimes two minutes, we have a squad now that can deliver in moments and we have to use that.”

open image in gallery Mikel Arteta applauds the Arsenal fans at full-time ( Reuters )

It had been a desperate game. For those who rail against the hegemony of positional football, who say it’s shackling ingenuity and entertainment, this first half was exhibit A. Arsenal had 74% possession and no shots on target. Gabriel would pass the ball out to Eze on the touchline who would recycle it back into the middle, rinse and repeat.

“Arsenal have been the better team,” said Roy Keane at half-time, and he was right, in the sense that they are literally the better team. But better at what, exactly? Better at keeping the ball away from opposition’s prying toes, perhaps, better at that square pass Declan Rice makes to a centre-back after deciding against a forward ball.

With 331 passes at a completion rate of 91%, Arsenal were certainly better at fluffing their own statistics, although Forest didn’t help themselves: during one of many lulls, Ivorian centre-back Ousmane Diomande passed the ball straight off the pitch, chest high, nowhere near anybody, with the conviction of a man executing a plan only he knew existed.

But when it came to the nuts and bolts of the game, to tackling, to running, to winning duels, it was hard to tell the two sides apart. After 45 stultifying minutes in which neither goalkeeper made a save, it was actually Forest who had taken five of the game’s eight shots.

Rice was particularly impotent playing as the six at the base of midfield. It is a role which showcases very little of his greatest trait, his athleticism, but with Lewis-Skelly on the bench, Guimaraes was given licence to rove forwards with Martin Odegaard. The pair occasionally injected brief moments of speed into Arsenal’s game but no one else found their wavelength. It wasn’t a great surprise to see Eze replaced by Madueke at half-time, but Arsenal met the same problems.

open image in gallery Liam Delap couldn't breach Arsenal's defence ( Reuters )

Then came Arteta’s triple change: Merino for Guimaraes, Timber for Ben White, Gyokeres for Havertz. Forest dropped deeper and on 71 minutes, Arsenal produced their best move of the match when Saka played a short pass inside to Odegaard, who slipped in Timber running around the back of the Forest defence. Timber teed up Rice, who slashed a shot over the bar from 12 yards.

But Madueke rode to the rescue, dribbling inside to score after Merino had first forced back Forest’s centre-backs with a dangerous run.

“He’s a special character,” Arteta added of Madueke. “He’s someone who everyone loves in and around the dressing room with the way he connects and talks to people. I think I saw an interview where they were asking our players, ‘Who would you call if you have a problem?’ and some of them said, ‘Noni’, which I was surprised at. But I think it’s a massive credit and explains the kind of character that he is.

“We knew today we wouldn’t score in the first 20, 30 minutes. We were going to face a different Forest because they are extremely well coached, they put like a Christmas tree [formation], there is no space to play. You have to be so neat and tidy. You have to generate a lot of chaos in the box, whether that is an open play or with set-pieces.

“At the end I had the belief that the physical level [of Forest] was going to drop, the spaces will be a little bit bigger, more time to be more efficient. And the finishers delivered.”

News.title: Britain’s biggest warship sets sail for the Arctic in latest NATO show of strength
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Britain’s biggest warship, HMS Prince of Wales, has departed Portsmouth Naval Base in Hampshire to lead the UK Carrier Strike Group on a deployment to the Arctic and North Atlantic.

The aircraft carrier left on Sunday, with dozens of people gathering to wave and take pictures as the warship made its way out of the harbour.

The deployment marks the second phase of Operation Firecrest, which will focus on operational readiness, training, and strengthening Nato interoperability.

The Royal Navy said stealth fighter jets would return to the skies in the High North.

It said deployment of the flagship aircraft carrier alongside Nato allies “is a powerful shield for the nation, ensuring that the critical energy, trade, and communication links we all rely on every day in the region remain secure”.

open image in gallery Crew wave, as HMS Prince of Wales leaves Portsmouth Naval Base to lead The UK Carrier Strike Group on deployment to the Arctic and North Atlantic, on Operation Firecrest ( PA )

HMS Prince of Wales is accompanied by Type-45 destroyer HMS Dauntless.

The carrier has embarked with an air group comprising fifth-generation F-35 Jets, Merlin Mk4 Commando and Mk2 Anti-submarine helicopters, Wildcat helicopters and Malloy drones, the Royal Navy said.

More than 1,200 British personnel are deployed as part of the Carrier Strike Group.

They are working closely with allies including Norway, Denmark and Germany on operations designed to test and strengthen Nato interoperability, the Royal Navy added.

HMS Prince of Wales will be joined by HMS Dauntless and the staff of UK Carrier Strike Group, commanded by Commodore Richard Hewitt.

He said: “I am delighted to return to the Arctic and North Atlantic as we build on the successes of the first phase of Operation Firecrest.

“Led by the UK Flagship HMS Prince of Wales, the strike group will bring together a range of assets and capabilities, while taking every opportunity to train, operate and integrate with our Nato allies and partners.”

As part of the deployment, HMS Prince of Wales will host gatherings of military and political leaders in Oslo focused on the collective security of Northern Europe.

open image in gallery Crowds gather, as HMS Prince of Wales leaves Portsmouth Naval Base to lead The UK Carrier Strike Group on deployment to the Arctic and North Atlantic, on Operation Firecrest, which will focus on operational readiness, training, and strengthening NATO interoperability ( PA )

The Atlantic Future Forum and the International Sea Power Conference will bring together defence leaders, industry and policymakers to discuss the future of Euro-Atlantic security.

Earlier this year, former chief of the Royal Navy Lord West of Spithead told the Press Association news agency: “The bottom line is the Navy’s in a more parlous state than at any stage in the 60 years I’ve been on the active list.

“It’s too small, it’s not been looked after properly, there’s been insufficient (funds) spent on it, and I’m afraid it doesn’t deliver what the nation needs.”

Armed forces minister Louise Sandher-Jones said: “The deployment of the HMS Prince of Wales and her air wing to the High North and the North Atlantic, operating under Nato leadership, is a clear demonstration of the UK’s commitment to the alliance and contribution to the enduring security and stability of the North Atlantic.”

The focus of phase 2 of Operation Firecrest is “maintaining operational readiness, strengthening interoperability and ensuring the Carrier Strike Group are prepared to respond to the challenges of an increasingly important region”, the Royal Navy said.

News.title: During anti-Trump protests, No Kings’ Instagram page got pulled. Platform says oops
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Meta disabled the primary Instagram account belonging to the No Kings Coalition on Saturday, briefly shutting down access to the page during nationwide demonstrations against President Donald Trump.

The suspension came as nearly 3,000 events were taking place across all 50 states and Washington, D.C., as part of the group’s early-voting push ahead of the November midterms.

The social media giant attributed the disruption to an automated safety filter.

“When accounts post, share or comment at very high frequencies, it can trigger automated systems,” Meta communications officer Andy Stone wrote on X. “That’s what happened with the No Kings IG account in the lead-up to today’s day of action. Unfortunately, that automated action was clearly taken in error. Everything is now working as it should, and we sincerely apologize.”

The temporary outage occurred during the fourth series of No Kings demonstrations held across the United States since President Trump took office in early 2025. The coalition, organized by Indivisible, emerged after the president returned to the White House following a movement focused on ensuring political power remained with the people rather than Washington leadership.

Meta temporarily disabled the primary Instagram page for the No Kings Coalition on Saturday in what the company described as an automated system error, shutting off account access during nationwide demonstrations against President Donald Trump ( Getty )

Organizers reported that administrative access was cut off around 1:30 p.m. Eastern Standard Time, leaving leaders unable to update supporters at a critical point during the day's actions. Even after the page became public again, organizers said they remained locked out of the account’s backend for roughly four hours.

“In the middle of that joyful experience at the protest locally, I got word from my team that Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta had suspended the Instagram account for the No Kings Coalition,” organizer Ezra Levin told MeidasTouch. “They suspended it. We didn’t have access to it.

“We couldn’t post to it. Nobody could go to the page. That was for about an hour-and-a-half, during the height of the mobilization while people were still getting their No Kings protests together.”

Levin added: “This is strikingly reminiscent of what we saw in Brazil just this week. A court ruled against Meta for favoring the authoritarians in that country. And we might be seeing something similar from Meta in our country right now, but rest assured, we’re not going to stop organizing against this regime.”

The White House previously responded to the demonstrations through spokeswoman Lauren Bis, who told Newsweek that the group’s focus on early voting proved “they should change their name,” adding that Americans faced a choice between Trump’s policies and ”extreme Democrats’ radical socialist, open-border policies.”

News.title: Cindy Crawford breaks silence on son Presley Gerber’s death at 27
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Cindy Crawford has spoken out about the death of her son, Presley Gerber, at age 27.

Nearly a month after Presley died September 20 of a suspected overdose, Crawford shared a tribute to him on Instagram on Sunday that was co-signed with Presley’s father, Rande Gerber, and sister, Kaia Gerber.

With a black-and-white picture of Presley, the family wrote: “We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother.

“We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years,” the post continued. “He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.”

The post concluded: “We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia.”

open image in gallery Presley Gerber is the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber ( Getty )

Presley, the son of supermodel Crawford and businessman Rande, was in a rehab facility in Los Angeles at the time of his death, the county’s medical examiner confirmed to The Independent.

A representative for Crawford, 60, Rande, 64, and Kaia, 25, told The Independent in a statement at the time: “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”

open image in gallery Rande Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Kaia Gerber shared a statement Sunday remembering Presley Gerber ( PA Archive )

In addition to the family’s statement shared on Crawford’s page, Kaia shared her own tribute to her brother on Instagram on Sunday.

“I love you the bluest, to the moon and back and back again, forever big brother,” the actor shared in the post, which included a childhood video and picture of her and Presley together.

Kaia went on to say, “I don’t have the words” to address “the magnitude of losing you.”

“You know how much I loved being your sister. It has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself,” she said. “I came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. I had more love for you than I knew what to do with. And now that it has nowhere obvious to go, I’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole.”

She continued: “To say loving you was the easiest thing in the world would imply that it required any effort at all. I was born loving you. I will die loving you. There was never anything else.”

Kaia went on to say that she “would walk knowingly toward this grief if it meant that on the other side of it I got to be your sister.”

“My darling brother, I do adore you,” she wrote. “I love my brother. My brother is dead. And this party sucks so bad without you, prez.”

Presley was open about his struggles with substance abuse and mental health issues in the years before his death. In March, he posted a video of himself using experimental drug Ibogaine in a drug withdrawal treatment in Cancun, Mexico.

He captioned the post, in part, “letting go of control didn’t come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why I was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself.”

“Praying it’s the last time I have to come back,” he wrote. “Next time I’d like to choose.”

If you or someone you know is suffering from drug addiction, you can seek confidential help and support 24-7 from Frank, by calling 0300 123 6600, texting 82111, sending an email or visiting their website here.

In the US, the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration can be reached at 1-800-662-HELP.
