Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha delivers Liverpool contract update amid Arsenal transfer interest
Sports.content:
Liverpool are in talks with Rio Ngumoha's representatives over a new contract, the player has revealed.

The teenage winger's current deal expires at the end of next season.

3 Ngumoha's current Liverpool contract expires in 2028 Credit: Getty

Ngumoha could be set to commit his long-term future to the Reds amid transfer interest in the forward.

Arsenal have been linked with a potential move for the England international in recent weeks.

It comes amid a strong start to the new season for the 18-year-old.

Ngumoha has featured eight times in all competitions for Andoni Iraola's side this term.

Those outings have taken his total number of first-team appearances for Liverpool to 38.

Since making his debut aged 16, Ngumoha has also scored twice and provided an assist for the Reds.

Ngumoha contract update

The youngster provided an update on his contract situation following Saturday's win over Brentford.

Speaking to reporters, Ngumoha admitted: "It's all with my agent now. I think it is all going well. I am not too sure.

"I just let the football do the talking, I enjoy playing and all of that is in the back of my mind. I just play for Liverpool and hopefully I can carry on doing well."

Ngumoha appeared as a second half substitute in Liverpool's 2-1 away win over the Bees.

3 Arsenal have been linked with a move for Ngumoha in recent weeks Credit: Getty

He replaced the injured Jeremie Frimpong in the 52nd minute at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Despite beating their nine-man opponents, the Reds remain eight points adrift of Premier League leaders Manchester City in fifth.

Ngumoha is into his third season at Anfield, having joined Liverpool's academy from Chelsea as a 16-year-old in 2024.

Following his breakthrough in the first-team, he was handed his senior England debut back in June.

He has now won three caps for the Three Lions after featuring against the Czech Republic home and away during the recent international break.

Meanwhile, Ngumoha is one of four Liverpool players currently out of contract at the end of next season.

3 Ngumoha has already won three caps for England at 18 Credit: Getty

Alexis Mac Allister, Federico Chiesa and Vitezslav Jaros' deals also expire in 2028.

The Reds also have seven players who could leave the club on a free transfer next summer.

Those include club captain Virgil van Dijk as well as both Alisson and Joe Gomez.

Sports.title: Eberechi Eze given harsh reality check over Arsenal future after ruthless Mikel Arteta act
Sports.content:
Eberechi Eze has been told he may need to accept his role at Arsenal being an impact substitute after a nightmare cameo.

Eze was handed his first start of the Premier League season during the Gunners' 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday.

3 Eze was hooked at half time during Arsenal's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest after being handed his first league start of the season Credit: Getty

However, the England international was substituted at half time at the City Ground by Mikel Arteta in a brutal decision.

To make matters worse, his replacement, Noni Madueke, was the player to score the late winning goal for the visitors.

In his first half showing, Eze lost possession eight times and failed to complete a dribble while playing off the left wing.

He also misplaced four of his passes and really struggled to make an impact against the deep defensive line of Forest.

And after failing to prove why he deserves a starting place, concerns are rising as to whether he'll ever have a key role.

Will Eze ever become an Arsenal starter?

Speaking on talkSPORT's The Final Word, host Majestic said: "Apart from bodying Spurs last season, he hasn't really set the world on fire for Arsenal.

"I can't help but think that the way Arteta sets his team up, the freedom that Eze needs a player...he doesn't seem like an Arteta player."

That then prompted ex-Premier League boss Alan Pardew to admit he thinks Eze won't ever be a starter in this Arsenal team.

"In the way he sets up his No.10, I don't see Eze getting a lot of action there," Pardew said.

"There's a real defensive side to that No.10 position he likes that Martin Odegaard does and Eze doesn't do.

3 Pardew doesn't think Eze will ever be a starter for Arsenal and that his role may be coming on as a late substitute Credit: Getty

"I think Arteta doesn't feel comfortable with that."

He added: "In certain games, against lesser oppositon, Eze will be given that No.10 position.

"But I've seen him on that left side for Crystal Palace a few times and it's just not him. He's never going to go down the left hand side and whip crosses in, he wants to come and play centrally. He's going to make the game too narrow and therefore you've not got enough width, so it's a problem.

"Arteta took him off rightly, in my opinion, as it just wasn't working.

"In the first instance though, perhaps he shouldn't have started him there, and used him as an impact as a No.10. And I think that will be his role at Arsenal, if they need a goal.

"I don't think Eze is going to a starter for Arsenal, I think he's a sub and if they need a moment, then the manager can give him the last 10-15 minutes of games."

3 Arteta admitted it was tough for Eze coming up against a deep defensive line, but remained positive on his star Credit: Getty

What has Arteta said on Eze?

Arteta may have taken Eze off at the break against Forest on Sunday, but he remained positive on the midfielder post-match.

The 28-year-old scored for Arsenal in the Champions League on Tuesday after starting on the left wing against Lille.

“Three days ago he scored a goal, he should have scored three and we were all happy," Arteta told Sky Sports.

He then went on to admit that Eze couldn't find space against Nottingham Forest's deep block, so he had to try a new approach.

"This is football, one day it's brilliant, the next day, especially with attacking players to play against a team that defends with 10 players in and around the box, the nine dropping almost at the edge, it's extremely difficult to get in there and that's it.

"But that's why you need fresh legs, a different profile and try different things.”

Sports.title: Sunderland star claims team ‘became arrogant’ in brutal review amid 11-year low
Sports.content:
Nordi Mukiele unleashed an explosive assessment of his Sunderland team-mates following their latest defeat.

The Black Cats were beaten 2-0 at Bournemouth on Sunday as they dropped into the Premier League relegation zone.

3 Mukiele labelled his Sunderland team-mates 'arrogant' after their fourth successive defeat Credit: AFP

A lacklustre display saw the visitors muster just three shots, with none of them on target.

Meanwhile, defender Kevin Danso was sent off just 17 minutes in after bringing down Evanilson.

It marked the club's fifth league loss of the season, with Regis Le Bris' side winning just one of their first seven matches this term.

In contrast, they did not suffer their fifth defeat last season until January.

Sunderland's run of fourth successive reverses is also their longest losing streak in the Premier League for 11 years.

They last suffered the unwanted feat under Sam Allardyce in December 2015, losing five straight matches.

Errors leading to goals have also become a worrying issue for Le Bris to assess.

Omar Alderete was at fault for Bournemouth's second goal as his back pass sent Evanilson through one on one.

It is the fifth error leading to a goal that Sunderland have committed already in the Premier League this season.

What did Mukiele say?

The manner of their latest setback was not lost on Mukiele, who did not hold back at full-time.

3 Sunderland were beaten 2-0 at Bournemouth amid their worst run of top-flight results since 2015 Credit: Getty

Speaking to Sky Sports, the defender admitted: "This game is what we (have been like) from the beginning of the season, to be honest with you.

"We are not good enough. We deserve to be where we are today, definitely.

"Why? I don't know. Maybe because we became arrogant, this is what I think."

Mukiele, who joined the club on a four-year deal last summer, has played every minute of the Black Cats' last six league outings.

Sunderland's slow start follows their seventh place finish last season on their return to the top-flight.

Following an eight-year absence from the Premier League, they qualified for the Europa League, their first European campaign for 53 years.

3 Sunderland have dropped into the relegation zone after winning just one of their opening seven matches Credit: Getty

It was also their highest finish since the 2000/01 season, when they also ended the campaign in seventh.

Le Bris has found success in the Europa League this term, though.

The Black Cats have won each of their opening two matches, beating AZ Alkmaar and Torreense.

Sunderland face Lech Poznan in Poland on Thursday before hosting Leeds United at the Stadium of Light next weekend.

Sports.title: Manchester United suffer disastrous unwanted Premier League first with Leeds draw
Sports.content:
Manchester United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season after their winless run continued on Sunday.

Michael Carrick's side have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions.

3 United have made their worst-ever start to a Premier League season Credit: Getty

It follows a 1-1 draw with Leeds United at Elland Road despite United taking a first half lead.

The visitors had opened the scoring through Bryan Mbeumo before they were pegged back after the break by Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

United now sit just two points above the relegation zone in 13th place.

Meanwhile, they have won just one of their first seven Premier League matches this term.

United make unwanted history

It marks their fewest league victories at this stage of a season since the 1986/87 campaign.

United have also made their worst start in all competitions since that season.

On that occasion, Ron Atkinson was sacked in November 1986 before being replaced in the dugout by Sir Alex Ferguson.

His side then went on to finish 11th, which at the time represented their lowest final position since promotion back to the top-flight in 1975.

As for this season, United have won just twice across all competitions, with their most recent victory coming against Sabah in the Champions League on September 10.

Carrick's side were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton last month as well as losing to Atletico Madrid in Europe on Tuesday.

3 United were denied a first win in six by Calvert-Lewin's equaliser Credit: Getty

The Red Devils boss will be hoping to avoid going seven matches without a win in midweek.

United face a Champions League trip to Italy to face Como on Wednesday before hosting Bournemouth next weekend.

Carrick's slow start to the campaign follows his appointment as permanent boss at the end of last season.

The former United midfielder signed a two-year deal at Old Trafford back in May.

Carrick reaction

Speaking to talkSPORT after the draw with Leeds, Carrick explained: "I thought it was a really good game today.

"I thought it was an edgy game. There was an intensity about it. There was a bit of feeling in it, we could sense that.

3 Carrick's side have won just twice in all competitions this season Credit: Getty

"That's what we expected, but I thought the boys stood up to it unbelievably well.

"I spoke to them before the game about what this means to the football club, to the supporters, the history and the rivalry.

"I think it's important that we attach ourselves to that and the boys were fully committed today.

"We're disappointed we haven't won the game, but it's a tough, tough game. They test you the way they play.

"If there's any leaks or any weaknesses, it gets found out today and a point is a point, but we can certainly take a lot from it the way we went about it."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals why Lisandro Martinez was substituted at half-time
Sports.content:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has revealed why Lisandro Martinez was substitute at half-time against Leeds.

Martinez started for United at Elland Road just days after he launched an angry outburst towards the club's board.

3 Carrick started for Man United a few days after his outburst, but was substituted at half time against Leeds Credit: Getty

The Argentinian centre-back slammed their recruitment after a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League to Atletico Madrid.

But Carrick admitted on Friday that the drama following Martinez's comments was 'done' and that he was available for selection.

He went on to start against Leeds for the Red Devils and kept a clean sheet in the first half, as his side went in 1-0 up.

Bryan Mbeumo's goal was the difference and United looked to be on the top, leading their rivals as the whistle blew.

However, when coming back out for the second half, Martinez didn't return to the pitch, sitting on the bench instead.

Carrick replaced the defender with Noussair Mazraoui, with Leeds going on to score an equaliser as the game ended 1-1.

Why did Carrick substitute Martinez?

Speaking post-match, Man United boss Carrick explained the reasoning behind Martinez's half-time withdrawal.

He said: "He felt his thigh a little bit."

Martinez had been spotted hobbling during the first half.

He could potentially now be a doubt for United's Champions League trip to Como on Wednesday, which will be live on talkSPORT 2.

3 Carrick has revealed why he took Martinez off at the break after his side drew 1-1 at Elland Road Credit: AFP

Martinez's angry outburst

Martinez, who has started eight games in all competitions for Man United this season, was not substituted for off-the-pitch reasons.

He was reportedly fined for his outburst, but Carrick was clearly happy enough to keep him in his team on Sunday and only took him off due to his knock.

The 28-year-old targeted United's technical director Jason Wilcox in his rant, which he went on to apologise for.

"I have to control myself a lot," Martinez said on Tuesday. "But sometimes it's a reflection of our club at the moment. We did it last season and now we expect more from the top.

"To bring more players, to compete. Other teams bring in many more players. I expect more from everyone… 100 per cent I expected more from our technical director.

"I have to be honest and also the players have to do more but it's just important when you make a strong squad for this type of night."

3 Martinez was fined by United for his comments about the club on Tuesday, but he started for them again on Sunday Credit: Getty

On whether Carrick has not been backed enough, he added: "I don't think so. He does his best. The team knows how you play, every detail and if you don't change the next season, it's a big problem.

"You start changing, changing, changing manager, but what about other areas. I can't say more.

"It's easy to say the players but also we have to see other areas."

Sports.title: Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first
Sports.content:
Premier League manager tipped to be sacked instantly after 70-year first

Pierre Sage has been warned he could be sacked by Crystal Palace if they risk being sucked into a relegation battle.

It follows the Eagles' heavy defeat to bitter rivals Brighton on Sunday afternoon.



3 Sage's side made a disastrous start to their clash with Brighton on Sunday Credit: Getty

Palace were thrashed 5-0 at the Amex after shipping three goals inside the opening 10 minutes.

Those included an own goal from Jaydee Canvot before Diego Gomez scored a goal of the season contender from the halfway line.

The defeat marks Palace's heaviest loss to Brighton since January 1956 and leaves Sage's side just two points above the relegation zone.



A toxic atmosphere amongst the travelling supporters also saw his players booed off at the final whistle.

Assistant manager Paddy McCarthy did his best to calm the situation as Sage was met with jeers from the Palace fans.



Despite only being appointed in the summer, the Frenchman could now find himself under pressure at Selhurst Park.

Sage under pressure

talkSPORT's Perry Groves admitted Sage is 'done' after the derby defeat.



Speaking to Sam Matterface on GameDay Live, Groves said: "I think Sage is going to be demobbed at the end of this game. He’s done."

Alex Crook echoed the sentiment that Palace chairman Steve Parish could soon consider a change in the dugout.

He explained: "There was that story earlier in the season that Jaydee Canvot, who scored the own goal today, was left out of the team.

3 Brighton secured their biggest win over Palace for 70 years Credit: Getty



"Steve Parish wasn’t particularly happy with Pierre Sage for that decision. So I think there are signs of cracks in the relationship.

"I know Steve Parish came out and did quite an in-depth interview with our colleagues at The Athletic and said it’s going to take time, ‘we’re behind him’, but they are giving away too many chances, no doubt about that.

"I fancy Brighton today, despite the fact they’ve got a dreadful recent record in this fixture, because even though they won last weekend against Forest, Crystal Palace, they should have been out of the game by half-time.

"It was down to Forest’s wastefulness, really, that they ended up getting all three points in that match.



"History tells us that if Steve Parish sees signals that his side are heading for a relegation fight, he will make a change. He did with (Frank) De Boer when he was brought in to change the playing style.

"I think that lasted 10 matches, so at the moment, I don’t think the manager is covering himself in glory."

3 Sage was appointed on a three-year deal in the summer Credit: AFP

What's next for Palace?

Frank De Boer was sacked just four matches into the 2017/18 season after suffering four successive Premier League defeats without scoring a goal.



Sage has already seen his side lose four of his nine matches across all competitions.

The loss to Brighton followed league defeats against both Everton and Ipswich Town so far this term.

Meanwhile, Palace were beaten by Lyon in the Europa League in midweek.

They are once again in European action on Thursday as they travel to Turkey to face Besiktas.



Palace then host Newcastle United in the Premier League three days later.

Sports.title: Premier League LIVE: Arsenal beat Nottingham Forest thanks to late Madueke goal, Leeds draw with Man United, Brighton hammer Palace
Sports.content:
'The time has come to hang up the boots'

Saido Berahino has announced his retirement from football.

The 33-year-old striker has called time on his career after 14 years in the game, having played for 11 clubs in total.

He was once tipped to become England's next big thing, having starred as a youngster in the Premier League.

Berahino played 133 top flight games, scoring 23 goals and providing three assists, also playing 84 games in the EFL.

Most of his career was spent at West Brom, while he also had stints with Stoke and Sheffield Wednesday before spending two years in Cyprus and last playing for Tabor Sezana in Slovenia.

Issues off the pitch around transfers and general conduct largely derailed his progress, and now, he's retired from the game.

He wrote on Instagram: "A Letter to the Game Football has given me everything. From the streets of Bujumbura to the Hawthorns, from the Premier League to places I never imagined I’d play — this game carried a young refugee kid through life.

"I want to thank West Bromwich Albion for believing in me when I was a boy. Those years at the club, the goals, the fans, the moments… they will always be special. To every teammate, coach, and supporter who shared the journey — thank you.

"There were highs and lows, mistakes and lessons. I learned that the game can lift you up and test you at the same time. Through it all, football remained my constant.

"The time has come to hang up the boots. My body and my heart are ready for the next chapter. I am proud and grateful to now serve the Burundi national team as a coach. Giving back to the country that made me, and helping the next generation, feels right.

"To my family — you have been my strength. To the fans who stayed with me through every chapter — I will never forget your support.

"This is not goodbye to football. It is simply the end of one story and the beginning of another."

Sports.title: Brighton star scores outrageous goal of the season as Seagulls tear rivals Crystal Palace apart
Sports.content:
Brighton star scores outrageous goal of the season as Seagulls tear rivals Crystal Palace apart

Brighton's Diego Gomez scored the Premier League's 'goal of the season' on Sunday during a 10-minute rout of Crystal Palace.

Gomez incredibly scored from the halfway line in the opening stages of the Seagulls' 5-0 win over rivals Palace at the Amex Stadium.

2 Gomez and his teammates couldn't believe what had just happened after the Brighton star scored from the halfway line Credit: Getty

The Paraguay international received a quick pass into his feet from Oliver Boscagli after Adam Wharton lost possession.

He took one touch, turned and spotted Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez well off his line in the goal.

And he unleashed a perfect strike, beating Benitez with a powerful effort that sailed over him and into the net.

The Brighton fans roared as the players chased after Gomez in disbelief at what had just happened.

Speaking on talkSPORT, ex-Arsenal winger Perry Groves said: "Don't worry about goal of the season. We've just seen it."

Gomez's remarkable strike was from 51 metres out from the goal.

That is the furthest range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney for Everton vs West Ham in November 2017 (58m).

Brighton's 10-minute triple

Gomez's incredible halfway line strike was the second goal of the game for Brighton after just seven minutes.

Palace's Jaydee Canvot had already headed into his own net just moments before, putting the hosts into the lead.

And then just three minutes after Gomez's goal, Yasin Ayari got in on the act and finished into the bottom corner.

2 Gomez's goal was from the furthest distance since 2017 in the Premier League, proving just how incredible the strike was Credit: AFP

By scoring three in 10 minutes, Brighton became the ninth side in Premier League history to score three in that time.

They are the first since Newcastle against Tottenham in April 2023.

Spurs conceded three in 9 minutes on that day, before the Magpies went on to win the match 6-1 in the end.

Brighton then went on to add a fourth just after half time, with Charalampos Kostoulas finishing after a ricochet in the box.

And Jack Hinshelwood added his side's fifth with a tap-in from close range in the final stages of the match.

Gomez's stunner was his first of the season for Brighton in all competitions, adding to his two assists.

He had a hand in a goal in the Seagulls' 3-0 win over Arsenal in September and their season opener against Aston Villa.

Since joining the club last January from Lionel Messi's Inter Miami, the right midfielder has scored 12 times in 66 appearances.

Sports.title: Under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage could become first Premier League managerial sacking this season after 5-0 thrashing at bitter rivals Brighton - with club chiefs concerned about his defensive tactics
Sports.content:
Under-fire Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage could become first Premier League managerial sacking this season after 5-0 thrashing at bitter rivals Brighton - with club chiefs concerned about his defensive tactics

Pierre Sage is under growing pressure at Crystal Palace and could become the first Premier League manager sacked this season after an embarrassing 5-0 defeat against rivals Brighton.

Palace chiefs have raised concerns about Sage’s defensive approach for several weeks and considered sacking him in September but a goalless draw against Leeds bought him more time.

However, the backline continues to ring alarm bells at Selhurst Park, leaving Sage’s position at risk.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League games.

The French coach is also understood to have a strained relationship with key decision-makers, who doubt his defensive methods.

The Daily Mail previously reported that his decision to bench Jaydee Canvot after a bad game irked chairman Steve Parish.

Pierre Sage said he didn't know how long he would be given to turn things round at Palace

Speaking after Palace’s 5-0 defeat at Brighton, Sage was unsure whether he would be given more time in the job.

‘I don’t know,’ Sage said when asked if he would keep his job. ‘I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face for this club against this other club and we are not at the level we expected.

‘I am really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them. We didn’t show that today. It was really important for us too. We didn’t understand in which context this game was played.

‘I will always give my best. When we lose, I’m really frustrated, but I always take the lesson and try to change things. But it’s the same when I win because I know we can improve.

‘I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we can do better. Today the work is really important to do and I will do it. It’s my job and I like to change this kind of thing.’

Sports.title: Where once we had Arsene Wenger's Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta's Unwatchables. Arsenal may have got the job done against Nottingham Forest, but it was scruffy not stylish, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Where once we had Arsene Wenger's Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta's Unwatchables. Arsenal may have got the job done against Nottingham Forest, but it was scruffy not stylish, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

They are Premier League champions and may well retain their title but Arsenal will never set pulses racing outside north London.

Gunners players, coaches and fans will not care and why should they? They waited 22 years to lift the title and if they go back to back, why would any of those supporters worry about how they did it?

This stuff matters, though. Especially this season, which is already in big trouble due to the Manchester City cheating verdict.

Fans are disillusioned by the ongoing saga and the wider game needs a spectacular team to celebrate. Sadly, where once we had Arsene Wenger’s Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta’s Unwatchables.

Yes, their defence is fabulous, as demonstrated when Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa made goal-saving challenges late on. They do that bit much better than anyone else and you can only admire it.

But for a club who has spent so much on players, where is the spark? Where is the flair? Where is the magic, the wow? It was somehow fitting that their winner from Noni Madueke should take a huge deflection off Forest defender Jair Cunha. Scruffy, not stylish.

Arsenal leaped back into second in the Premier League after victory over Nottingham Forest

Noni Madueke came off the bench to score an 80th minute winner for the Mikel Arteta's side

In the first half, their best effort was a Gabriel back heel that hit his team-mate Konsa and nearly rolled into the Forest net.

One area you cannot question Arteta is in his use of substitutes. Madueke’s strike made it 24 goal involvements from players off the bench for Arsenal since the start of last season. The five-subs rule is a huge advantage for wealthy clubs with expensive squads but you still need huge skill to make the most of it.

Still though, Arsenal feel like a team reaching success by spreadsheet rather than artistry. The best of Europe, like Bayern Munich, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, thrill with their attacking play. It would be lovely to see Arsenal match that, even sometimes.

They have apparently hired a creativity guru to bring innovative practices and out-of-the-box thinking to their bid for multiple honours this season. Perhaps Arteta should ask German Castanos if he can unlock a well-organised defence, as this was beyond his team for much of this encounter.

These are unsettling times for Forest, who competed impressively but are still without a win or a goal at home all season. Oliver Glasner was hired at huge expense in the summer and the start has not been as owner Evangelos Marinakis would have liked.

Starting the day six points behind Manchester City, Arsenal brought back some of their main men, with Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Bukayo Saka restored to the starting XI while Arteta preferred Eberechi Eze to Madueke on the left. Eze would last only 45 minutes, however.

In the absence of their main creator Morgan Gibbs-White, who did not train all week due to a muscular problem, Forest set up cautiously. Without a league win at the City Ground since April and with only five points on the board, Oliver Glasner could not risk a hiding at home.

In the opening 15 minutes, his team had barely 20 per cent of the ball and completed only 24 passes inside the Arsenal half. Crucially, though, Arsenal were not stretching Glasner’s men.

Arsenal may have gotten the job done but they have become Mikel Arteta's Unwatchables

So carefully are Arsenal’s build-up patterns planned that, at times in the first half, we saw Rice on the right of a back three, and Havertz in the left-back spot. Full-backs Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori stepped into midfield but still Forest stuck to their task.

Midfielder Xaver Schlager was everywhere and at the back, Murillo did not miss a trick. Though often imprecise, Liam Delap did not allow Gabriel or Ezri Konsa a moment’s peace.

Indeed Forest had the first chance as Nico Dominguez, who replaced Gibbs-White, seized on a poor pass from Calafiori. Delap collected Daniel Munoz’s deflected cross and teed up Dan Ndoye for a shot that was tipped around the post. Attempting to meet Neco Williams’ corner, Murillo clashed with Konsa and suffered a cut to his face.

Unable to break through in open play, Arsenal turned to one of last season’s old set-piece favourites. Saka swung over the corner, Calafiori flicked it on and Gabriel backheeled the loose ball goalwards. Luckily for Forest, it hit Konsa and rebounded favourably.

That was about as good as it would be for Arsenal before the break and when Schlager was treated for a head injury, Arteta summoned his players for a mid-match briefing.

Just before the interval, Rice brought down Delap with a clumsy lunge. Williams’ free-kick hit the wall and as players jostled, Bruno Guimaraes hit the deck holding his face. Arsenal ball, danger averted. ‘Are you City in disguise?’ howled the home fans.

It had been desperately poor stuff from the champions though and it was no surprise to see Arteta sprint down the tunnel when referee Michael Oliver blew the half-time whistle.

Ineffective again, Eze was hauled off by. Huddled in his training jacket for the second half, Eze appeared lost in thought.

Right-back Jurrien Timber made a massive impact for the Gunners off the bench

Arteta’s team made just as little impact during the first part of the second half and midway through it, he sent for three more subs. Mikel Merino, Jurrien Timber and Victor Gyokeres were his selections from the £300m worth of talent in reserve, as Havertz, Guimaraes and Ben White made way.

Timber nearly made an immediate impact when he burst into the box from the right and fed the unmarked Rice, whose finish from 15 yards was woeful and did not even test Sels.

Arsenal’s breakthrough arrived when Jair Cunha’s clearance only reached Rice, who transferred it to Madueke. The England winger charged into the box and when his angled effort clipped Cunha’s left thigh, Sels had no chance to stop it.

Forest would have their moments but could not take them. Callum Hudson-Odoi found fellow substitute Chris Wood only for the forward to delay his aim, allowing Rice to race back and make a crucial block.

There was still time for Murillo to glide in from the left and beat Rice with an outrageous piece of skill. Instead of the net, though, the Brazilian defender fired into the Trent End and when Konsa blocked another effort from Delap, Arsenal were home.

Sports.title: Celtic 7-1 Hearts: Another Tynecastle title dream dies a death at Celtic Park as Benjamin Nygren and Callum Osmand both score twice to ruthlessly rip apart Wouter Vrancken's men
Sports.content:
Celtic 7-1 Hearts: Another Tynecastle title dream dies a death at Celtic Park as Benjamin Nygren and Callum Osmand both score twice to ruthlessly rip apart Wouter Vrancken's men

Earlier this week, Tony Bloom reaffirmed his vision for Hearts and spoke of his belief that they will be crowned champions of Scotland within the next ten years.

It made for some nice soundbites, as was the case when Bloom laid out the same blueprint after his involvement as a Hearts investor started just over a year ago.

Yet, in each of Bloom’s first two seasons at the club, it has been here at Celtic Park where Hearts have seen their title ambitions crushed.

The circumstances may have been different. What happened towards the end of last season was a travesty, given some of the refereeing calls that went against them. The final-day debacle against Celtic and subsequent pitch invasion will forever be a stain on Scottish football.

But the two outcomes have ultimately been the same; Hearts’ title dream died here in the east end of Glasgow last May, and it died here once again yesterday.

There will be some who view that as a premature assessment in mid-October. Wouter Vrancken’s side are eight points behind Celtic and four behind Rangers with almost 30 games still to play.

Callum Osmand knows Celtic's third past beleaguered Hearts goalkeeper Beau Reus

But the damage inflicted here felt too significant, the flaws exposed in this team too glaring, and the prospect of this team being title contenders felt too fanciful for even the most ardent of Hearts fans.

By quite a distance, this was the worst performance Hearts have delivered during Bloom’s involvement with the club.

They were absolutely annihilated by a Celtic side who themselves came into this with fragile confidence after being dismantled by Benfica in the Europa League on Thursday night.

After conceding twice from set-plays in the opening ten minutes, Hearts completely and utterly capitulated. It was a horror show. On the touchline, Vrancken did nothing to change the flow of the match.

There was a naivety to how his team set up here. It was as if Hearts arrived at Parkhead and believed they were better than they actually are.

Like they expected to turn up and roll Celtic over on account of how good they have been in attack at times this season under Vrancken.

But, defensively, they were appalling. Teams of genuine substance do not capitulate like this. Hearts were 5-1 down by half-time – and they were lucky it wasn’t seven or eight.

Wouter Vrancken set his Hearts side out ambitiously and was negligent in reining them in

Any notion of this team winning the title this season is for the birds. So open, so weak, so naïve; this defeat was entirely on Vrancken.

As a man who made part of his fortune as a professional poker player, Bloom will already recognise that this season is a busted flush.

Indeed, the same could have been said of Martin O’Neill and Celtic had they lost this match. Yet, credit where it’s due, O’Neill rallied his players and delivered a statement result.

For the first time this season, Celtic actually turned up and delivered a big performance in a match of genuine consequence.

The pressure on O’Neill will lift for now. He dropped Kasper Hogh yesterday and the decision was vindicated entirely by Celtic turning in their most stylish performance of the season.

The challenge now will be to sustain this in the Europa League clash here with Celta Vigo on Thursday night as Celtic look to breathe some life into their European season.

On the back of the 4-1 hammering against Benfica in Lisbon on Thursday night, O’Neill opted to freshen things up by making four changes to his Celtic team. The most eye-catching saw Hogh dropped to the bench, with Camilo Duran operating as the central striker and Callum Osmand and Haissem Hassan on the wings.

O’Neill had spoken on Thursday night about Hogh’s form and the fact that the £11million club-record signing has failed to score in over two months.

Kieran Tierney nods home the opener to kickstart a day Celtic fans will long remember

Insisting he still has faith that Hogh will eventually come good and score over 20 goals this season, the Celtic boss explained that the Danish international striker ‘had to earn the right’ to be in the team.

The other changes saw Liam Scales and Benjamin Nygren come into the team, with Auston Trusty and Oliver Sorensen dropping to the bench.

Hearts drew 1-1 against Nordsjaelland on Thursday night and boss Wouter Vrancken made three changes for this trip to Parkhead. Defenders Stephen Kingsley and Jordi Altena started along with midfielder Sabri Guendouz, with Harry Milne, James Wilson and Christian Borchgrevink dropping out.

Hearts actually started the match reasonably well and looked like they were on the front foot in the opening five minutes or so. But the whole thing fell apart in double-quick time. The concession of two goals from set-plays saw them go 2-0 down after only ten minutes.

First, a Mika Baur corner was flicked on by Scales and Kieran Tierney had the simple task of heading in from point-blank range.

The lead was doubled when Nygren wriggled free and converted from another Baur corner. From Hearts’ point of view, the defending was criminal.

To score twice from corners was certainly a feather in the cap of Celtic’s new set-piece coach Ross Grant, who joined the club from Hearts back in the summer.

Jamie McCart contrives to knock the ball over for Celtic's fifth goal before half time

Yet, so deplorable was the defending from Hearts, it hardly required the most creative set-piece routines in Grant’s playbook. Rather, it was all painfully simple.

For all that they have won plaudits for an exciting style of football going forward, defensive frailties are now rapidly becoming a theme of Hearts’ season under Vrancken.

As was the case when they were ripped to shreds by Benfica in Lisbon a couple of months ago, this was another example of a team who don’t know how to stop the bleeding once it starts.

Back in the side after an injury lay-off, Osmand scored twice in little more than 60 seconds to put Celtic 4-0 up after 38 minutes, one of which was a really classy finish with his right foot.

It was Osmand who scored deep into stoppage-time here to clinch the title when the teams met here on the final day of last season, a goal which sparked a mass pitch invasion.

Hearts pulled a goal back when Laurent Mendy fired low into the bottom corner from the edge of the box, but any notion of a comeback was swiftly extinguished.

Baur danced through a couple of feeble efforts at tackles from Hearts players and dinked the ball over Reus, before Kingsley’s attempted clearance cannoned off Jamie McCart and rolled back into the net.

This was utter humiliation for Hearts fans, many of whom had seen enough. With their team 5-1 down at half-time, some of them headed for the exits.

Truthfully, they were lucky it was only five. It could easily have been seven or eight in the first half alone. Celtic were utterly rampant.

Benjamin Nygren fires home Celtic's second goal as Hearts afternoon quickly turns sour

It took a last-ditch block from McCart to deny Nygren after a smart interception from Tierney sparked a rapid Celtic counter-attack.

A jinking run from Hassan saw the Egyptian winger hit the post, with Nygren also forcing a good save from Reus.

On days like this, you wonder what neutral observers must make of Scottish football. Celtic have been a laughing stock in Europe this season, yet this is what they do to their domestic rivals.

Duran made it 6-1 early in the second half when he swept a clinical left-foot finish low past Reus. There was still effectively a full half of football to play but Hearts were desperate for the final whistle.

Celtic made it 7-1 when Nygren netted his second goal of the game with just under ten minutes remaining.

A day of complete and utter humiliation for Hearts and Vrancken. The scars from this defeat may take quite some time to heal.

Celtic (4-3-3): Sinisalo 7; Donovan 7.5, Murray 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Emenalo 60); McGregor 7 (Oxlade-Chamberlain 60), Baur 8, Nygren 8; Hassan 8.5 (Forrest 70), Osmand 8 (Jota 46), DURAN 8.5 (Hogh 60). Booked: Jota, Baur, Donovan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 8.

Hearts (4-2-3-1): Reus 6; Altena 2, McCart 2, Fagan-Walcott 1, Kingsley 3; McEntee 3 (Magnusson 46), Mendy 5; McPake 6 (Kerjota 54), Guendouz 5 (Wilson 84), Miller 5 (Mato 54); Braga 4 (Ba-Sy 71). Booked: Miller. Manager: Wouter Vrancken 1.

Referee: David Dickinson.

Attendance: N/A.

Sports.title: Fabian Hurzeler breaks his Crystal Palace hoodoo as Brighton blow their bitter rivals away 5-0 to leave Pierre Sage smarting, writes NICK SZCZEPANIK
Sports.content:
This match kicked off in a rainstorm of biblical proportions - and Brighton swept Crystal Palace away. This will take some getting over for the travelling fans, and their under-fire manager Pierre Sage.

Jaydee Canvot nodded Pascal Gross’s free kick into his own net after only four minutes and Diego Gomez hit a spectacular over the head of Walter Benitez from the half way line three minutes later, his first goal of the season. After nine minutes it was 3-0, Yasin Ayari’s shot deflecting in off the luckless Canvot.

Charalampos Kostoulas made it 4-0 early in the second half after Ayari’s shot from Gross’s cross had been blocked. Sussex-born sub Jack Hinshelwood – whose grandfather had played for Palace in the fixture – scored the fifth after Benitez had parried Luka Vuskovic’s header.

Goal of the month twice in a row?

Brighton won the September goal of the month award thanks to a 25-yard thunderbolt from captain Lewis Dunk in their 5-0 win at Coventry.

And his teammate Gomez must surely be favourite for the October award. The ball was just crossing the half-way line when the Paraguay midfielder looked up and drove it fiercely goalwards, catching goalkeeper Benitez far enough off his line to have no chance of getting back.

This was no Beckhamesque lob, but a blast that succeeded through its power as much as its height and shock value, and it made him Brighton’s 11th different scorer in the league this season.

Diego Gomez scored a goal of the season contender from the halfway line as Brighton got off to a flying start

A rivalry, not a derby

Many people unfamiliar with the history of this fixture question how two clubs some 45 miles apart can have a real rivalry. According to well-known motoring website, the distance between Selhurst Park and the Amex Stadium is about the same as that between Portman Road and Carrow Road, yet nobody questions the antagonism between Ipswich Town and Norwich City.

It all began in the mid-70s as the two clubs – managed by former Tottenham rivals Alan Mullery (Brighton) and Terry Venables (Palace) followed each other from the third division to the first and also clashed in a series of FA Cup ties.

The intense atmosphere has sometimes produced results that have defied league form, and home fans with memories of a few such games were concerned that Palace might burst the Brighton bubble despite the excellent recent performances that took them into the match in third place in the Premier League and as the division’s top scorers. Those fears were put to bed after just nine minutes.

Hurzeler: Something is missing!

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler had yet to beat Palace in four meetings before Sunday.

On the eve of the game he said: 'In my journey so far with this club, we've experienced a lot of really, really positive things. But one thing is still missing.'

Not any more. He has built a team and a squad that exudes self-belief and they tore into Palace from the first whistle. Sage will hope he does not have to wait as long for his first win in the fixture.

Brighton exude self-belief and tore into their opponents from the first whistle to win 5-0

Sage in trouble?

A section of the Brighton fans chanted “sacked in the morning” at Hurzeler during Palace’s 1-0 win at the Amex in February. But despite that nadir, owner Tony Bloom kept faith in the German, he pulled his team round and they qualified for the UEFA Conference League.

So this defeat may not do any long-lasting damage to the Eagles’ prospects in general and those of Sage in particular – despite gleeful “sacked in the morning” chants predictably directed at the Palace dugout. That said, Sage may have even greater cause today to feel grateful for last weekend's victory over Nottingham Forest and his predecessor, Oliver Glasner.

The Thursday-Sunday grind:

Both sides were in European action on Thursday, and Brighton’s squad strength told then as they were able to make eight changes and still stroll past FK Kauno Zalgiris 4-0, while Palace had a tougher evening in a 3-2 defeat away to Lyons.

Eight of Palace’s starting eleven here had also started that game while Brighton had seven fresh faces and it showed.

The Seagulls were again able to deploy the energetic high press that was too much for Arsenal in their previous home Premier League game. Brighton were first to every ball, even in the second half.

Sports.title: This is how far ragged Man United have fallen. Anything that isn't a defeat is a good result, they can't control games, are weak in the centre and had to hang on against Leeds, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
It may not have looked, felt or smelled like it, but this was a good result for Manchester United.

It wasn't a performance or an outcome to mask problems or deficiencies that run right through Michael Carrick's squad but in terms of an outcome it was about par.

For this is where United are right now. Anything that isn't a defeat – especially away from home – to a team with ideas and ambition and a good coach represents a decent day out. This, frankly, is how far they have fallen.

Carrick's team took the lead in the first half and had the better of it for a while. But then they lost control of things to the extent that it took them half an hour to have another shot. By then Leeds had equalised and taken a grip of the game.

In fact, by the end, Daniel Farke's energetic and likeable team had mustered 62 per cent of the possession and this is one of the reasons that the other United – the one from along the M62 – are stuck in such a rut. They simply cannot control games.

They have some good players and Bryan Mbeumo is one of them. He scored in the 35th minute. But in the centre of the field where tempo and rhythm are set and territory is won, United are weak.

Manchester United and Leeds played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road on Sunday

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the second half after Bryan Mbeumo had put United ahead

Here, with Carrick betraying the look of the team sheet by deploying what looked like a back three, it was new signings Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba who were given the job of securing ball and position. They were okay but that was all they were.

Over time, Leeds won that battle and as the game wore on, it was they who had the loftier ambitions. It was they who sensed a win and Carrick's players who were looking to get out of town with what they had.

They were a little bit all over the place by the end. Three promising counters in the space of five minutes, for example, were halted by utterly needless and brainless offsides.

But United survived and some of the noise around Carrick's position will quieten between now and Wednesday's Champions League game in Como. The pattern seems once again set now, however.

We are seven games in to the new Premier League season and United have won just once – against Ipswich at home.

Here Carrick's formation had a look of Ruben Amorim's back five about it. It was inflexibility – not to mention poor results – that got Amorim the sack last season but at least Carrick appeared to be trying something different.

Mbeumo slid home from close range in the first half after Youri Tielemans' inviting cross

Calvert-Lewin levelled by firing home from close range after the ball broke to him from a corner

Diogo Dalot and Amad Diallo appeared to be playing as wing-backs in a line-up that saw United start without a clear centre forward. Youri Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Mbeumo were the front three with Fernandes more often than not occupying the central position. After all the fuss of the week, Lisandro Martinez was in the team but only until half-time, after which the Argentinean failed to appear.

Arguably, United's problems have not been about tactics and formations but about application. Here, against an upwardly mobile Leeds team, Carrick's team seemed for a while to have more about them than they showed in drawing against ten-man Tottenham eight days earlier.

They were more compact but also more energetic and it ensured they initially competed with the home team on the metrics that really mattered. Sadly for United, it wasn't to last. Leeds were honest and spirited but lacked consistent tempo in the first half. They created sporadic half chances but nothing that sufficiently engaged the home crowd. Indeed Elland Road was rather quiet at times and that told part of the early story.

Mbeumo's opening goal didn't arrive until the 35th minute. Up until that point the game had been scrappy and occasionally required the vigilance of referee Darren England.

Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu should have been booked for an early stamp – accidental or not – on Mbeumo while Fernandes was indeed cautioned for a late challenge on Tarik Muharemovic. That offence came after Fernandes applied a heavy touch to the through pass and was perhaps indicative of his recent poor form. Prior to that, the United captain had taken a free-kick from a good position on the far side and delivered it straight out of play.

Leeds were occasionally progressive around this point and United keeper Senne Lammens was sharp enough to touch a header from Nico Elvedi over the bar in the 25th minute. At that stage, it stood as the only chance of the game.

The result slightly eases the pressure on under-fire Red Devils boss Michael Carrick

Lisandro Martinez was subbed off at half-time in the first game since his explosive rant

United always looked as they may carry a threat when they did motor up field, though, and Mbeumo served notice of this almost immediately when he found space to meet a Tielemans cross six yards out only to head the ball six inches wide of James Trafford's left hand post.

As the visiting team grew into the game, so they settled a little. There was nothing haphazard about this performance at this point and after Trafford tore from goal to stop one dangerous attack with a slide tackle on Diallo, United returned again to take the lead.

It was Tielemans again with the cross from the right only this time it was a low one. Mbeumo was under pressure from James Justin with the Leeds defender taking a piece of his shirt. But the United forward was strong and determined and he kept enough of his balance to side foot the ball in from a few yards out.

United just about deserved their lead. They had looked just a little more clinical than their opponents. They held it until half-time – despite half chances for Calvert-Lewin and Jayden Bogle – but it took only six minutes of the second period for the game to change.

With Noussair Mazraoui replacing Martinez at half-time, the Moroccan conceded a corner in the 51st minute. When the kick arrived, however, he was beaten to it in the air by Muharemovic who headed the ball down for Calvert-Lewin to swivel and volley in.

Thereafter United were ragged. All their previous structure and composure had gone and for a period they hung on. There was nothing particularly sophisticated about Leeds' football. It involved width and crosses – not always as accurate as Farke would have liked - and high energy. But it made United look ordinary and uncomfortable. Indeed when Fernandes swivelled and drove a low shot across goal and wide in the 65th minute, it represented United's first effort on goal of note since they scored.

Bruno Fernandes, Carrick and Amad Diallo salute United's fans at the final whistle

Technical director Jason Wilcox, the subject of much of Martinez's ire, was in attendnace

Leeds were not creating lots of chances, either. Just a couple of smashed shots over from Ao Tanaka and Noah Okafor and then another from Anton Stach with 18 minutes left. But the home team did have some momentum and that threatened to be precious.

As they looked to turn the game back their way, United's options from the bench were limited. Mason Mount came on for Carlos Baleba with 15 minutes left but Carrick seemed reluctant to introduce Marcus Rashford or Matheus Cunha. Maybe that was a sign that the United manager valued a point above anything else. Eventually, with six and a half minutes left, Cunha was given his chance.

It was still Leeds who finished the stronger and they could have stolen it in added time. United keeper Lammens applied a weak punch to a cross and watched Stach's shot dribble through his legs. Fortunately for Lammens – and indeed Carrick's emotional wellbeing – Mazraoui was positioned behind him to hack the ball away.

Sports.title: Leeds 1-1 Man United PLAYER RATINGS: Who 'still looks short of his best'? Which star was 'a real handful'? And whose performance will have pleased Michael Carrick? Plus, vote for YOUR scores
Sports.content:
Leeds and Manchester United played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road in the Premier League on Sunday afternoon. Under-fire United boss Michael Carrick saw his side go 1-0 up through Bryan Mbeumo after he turned home Youri Tielemans' cross, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised early in the second half when he fired home from close range. Both sides pushed for a winner but neither could find a breakthrough as they were forced to settle for a point on an intense afternoon. The result leaves United with seven points from seven league games, while Leeds are up in seventh place after racking up ten points so far this season. Daily Mail Sport's CHRIS WHEELER was at Elland Road and he has rated both sets of players below... Manchester United and Leeds played out a hard-fought 1-1 draw at Elland Road on Sunday LEEDS UTD (3-4-2-1) JAMES TRAFFORD 6 – Looked solid and showed good anticipation to race 40 yards out of his goal and clear at the feet of Diallo. Had little chance with Mbeumo’s goal from close-range. JAMES JUSTIN 4 – Will be angry at himself that he lost track of Mbeumo for United’s opener. You can’t afford to switch off in games like this. NICO ELVEDI 6 – Presented with one of Leeds’ few chances in the first half when his header was saved by Lammens. Had his hands full with Mbeumo as United’s forward line chopped and changed. TARIK MUHAREMOVIC 6 – The big Bosnia defender was on the end of an ugly challenge from Fernandes early on, but recovered to get the crucial knockdown for Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser. JAYDEN BOGLE 7 – Got forward to offer a real threat at times and also defended well. Great interception tackle on Dalot in the first half got a huge cheer. ETHAN AMPADU 7 – Right in the thick of it. Set the tone with a couple of strong tackles early on, and squared up to Fernandes in the second half. Just the kind of approach Leeds fans love to see in this fixture. Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu was up for the fight on what was an intense afternoon But James Justin (right) was caught out after switching off for Bryan Mbeumo's opener AO TANAKA 5 – Had a couple of half chances, including a volley over the bar shortly after Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser. Replaced by Longstaff towards the end. GABRIEL GUDMUNDSSON 5 – Booked for a challenge on Andrey Santos in the first half and was perhaps fortunate it wasn’t a red. Referee Darren England did well to let the tackles go in a fixture that was never going to be short on intensity. ANTON STACH 6 – Had two chances to make his mark on this game but volleyed over in the 72nd minute and then side-footed straight at Lammens late on. Got away with a cheap shot on Fernandes but the United captain was never going to have much sympathy here. NOAH OKAFOR 5 – Leeds’ two-goal hero from the win at Old Trafford in April rarely looked like scoring in this one and was replaced by Nmecha for the final quarter of the game. DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN 8 – Playing with the confidence of a striker who only needs one chance and he took it with a clinical finish early in the second half. A real handful for United’s defenders. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is in the form of his life and was a real handful for United's defence Subs: Zetterer, Longstaff (for Tanaka 80, 6), Wilson, Aaronson, Nmecha (for Okafor 73, 6), Bijol, Bahoya, Bard, Gruev. Scorer: Calvert-Lewin 51 Booked: Gudmundsson, Ampadu DANIEL FARKE 6 - Will see this as a missed opportunity with Leeds on such a good run and their opponents struggling so far this season. MAN UTD (4-2-3-1) SENNE LAMMENS 5 – Couldn’t be faulted for the goal but still lacks the composure of last season which is perhaps inevitable in a United side short of confidence. LENY YORO 6 – Looking more comfortable at right-back with each game he plays there. Took a blow to the face from Calvert-Lewin in the first half, but recovered well and stood strong against Okafor. Good battle against Calvert-Lewin but wasn’t marking the Leeds striker when he equalised which was odd. Showed why United needed him here with a solid first-half display. DIOGO DALOT 6 – Played out of position at left-back in the absence of Luke Shaw again and performed well in his duel with Bogle. Got forward well on occasions. Scored the first goal with a simple finish after heading wide unmarked in front of goal.
