Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Track Verstappen’s best result Hamilton’s best result Bahrain International Circuit 1st 1st Jeddah Corniche Circuit 1st 1st Albert Park 1st 1st Suzuka 1st 1st Shanghai International Circuit 1st 1st Miami International Autodrome 1st 6th Circuit Gilles Villeneuve 1st 1st Monaco 1st 1st Autodromo do Algarve 2nd 1st Silverstone 1st 1st Red Bull Ring 1st 1st Spa-Francorchamps 1st 1st Hungaroring 1st 1st Monza 1st 1st Madring 2nd DNF Baku City Circuit 1st 1st Istanbul Park 2nd 1st Singapore 1st 1st Circuit of the Americas 1st 1st Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez 1st 1st Interlagos 1st 1st Las Vegas Strip Circuit 1st 2nd Losail International Circuit 1st 1st Yas Marina 1st 1st

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Sports.title: Dalton Smith Wants Shakur Stevenson After Alberto Puello
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith is already eyeing a massive unification bout with Shakur Stevenson, even with his first WBC light welterweight title defense against Alberto Puello just days away.

Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) meets Puello on October 24 at Utilita Arena Sheffield. The unbeaten titleholder wants this victory to catapult him toward marquee names. Shakur sits near the top of his target list, but Puello can ruin everything.

“I’m boxing to be a part of the biggest fights possible. Of course the Shakur fight would be up there as one of the biggest. I’d love to be a part of that,” Smith told the Boxing World YouTube channel. “But of course, I have to get through Puello first.”

Smith grabbed the WBC belt back in January by stopping Subriel Matias inside five rounds during his US debut. Blowing through Matias earned him huge momentum, though it guarantees nothing against Puello.

Puello brings an awkward southpaw style. Smith will not get the same gifts he received from Matias, who walked straight in until he got caught by heavy counters. Puello is far more than a tune-up on the way to a Shakur payday. This matchup tests whether Dalton can defend his crown against a completely different kind of opponent.

“I don’t overlook what’s in front of me, but once I get the job done against Puello, I want to be chasing the biggest fights possible,” Smith said.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) has his own motives to spoil the party and steal that massive future date for himself. Calling out Shakur is the easy part for Smith. He still has to leave the ring with the belt.

Even if he gets past Puello, Dalton is overlooking the obstacles that will prevent him from fighting Shakur next. The network and promotional divide makes the Shakur-Smith fight virtually impossible to assemble right now. Shakur is signed with Zuffa and locked into Paramount+, while Smith is a Matchroom flagship fighter tied to DAZN.

Dual-network broadcasts only happen when the revenue numbers are astronomical, like Gervonta Davis against Ryan Garcia or massive undisputed heavyweight cards funded by deep foreign pockets. Dalton Smith versus Shakur Stevenson is nowhere near that category.

Neither guy moves US pay-per-view buys on that scale, and Zuffa has zero incentive to share production, split domestic rights, or loan out Shakur to DAZN for an ordinary regular-subscription card.

Dalton is known almost exclusively in the UK, and Shakur has struggled to build an audience that translates into commercial event revenue.

Zuffa Boxing did not bring Shakur to Paramount+ just to farm him out to DAZN or hand Matchroom control of an international production. If Zuffa wants Shakur in a unification or a meaningful fight at 140 pounds, they have zero business justification to share the pie with an outside streaming rival on an event with minimal domestic pay-per-view appetite.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford, Tim Bradley Challenge Fundora Stoppage
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s last-second stoppage of Ermal Hadribeaj drew objections during a post-fight discussion involving Terence Crawford and Tim Bradley, while Dan Rafael called for the result to be changed to a decision.

Hadribeaj appeared able to continue when the referee halted Saturday’s fight in Las Vegas. The unusual ending put a cloud over Fundora’s WBC junior middleweight title defense, with the dispute focused on Hadribeaj beating the count after the final bell had already sounded.

“All he had to do was get on his feet,” came one objection during the discussion involving Crawford, Bradley and the referee.

The referee defended his intervention by pointing to Hadribeaj falling back into the ropes and arguing that another attack would have left him in trouble.

“If there’s five seconds left, that guy gets destroyed,” he said.

But those five seconds did not exist. That is the problem with using a possible follow-up attack to justify the stoppage. Hadribeaj had no more fighting left to do if he had beaten the count after the final bell.

Rafael made that argument forcefully on X, urging Hadribeaj’s team to protest to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

“HE BEAT THE COUNT and the bell had already rung,” Rafael said. “Won’t be surprised at all if the NSAC changes the result to a unanimous decision.”

That was Rafael’s expectation, rather than an announced commission action. Still, his criticism gives Hadribeaj’s team a specific issue to raise: whether the referee improperly extended the process beyond the completed count when the fight had already ended.

This is about dollars and cents, not just hurt feelings. Getting tagged with an illegitimate knockout loss hurts Hadribeaj’s marketability and ruins his leverage for future paydays. Fundora keeps his win on the cards anyway, but the commission needs to step in, overturn the bogus stoppage, and take an undeserved KO loss off Hadribeaj’s record.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Tells Moses Itauma: “No Time For Crying”
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic is having a grand time talking down to Moses Itauma. As the young heavyweight mopes over his first defeat and fixates on replays, Hrgovic delivered a blunt reality check: stop crying, get back in the gym, and figure out how to win when your opponent refuses to fall over.

Itauma admitted this week that rewatching the bout eats away at him. He landed his best artillery, watched Hrgovic walk straight through it, and kept winging power shots until his gas tank emptied completely. He sounds like a fighter in denial, still convinced the knockout was right there if he had just thrown a little harder.

Hrgovic responded with dripping condescension, offering to comfort the 21-year-old prospect like a disappointed toddler.

“I’ll tell him, ‘Look, Moses, everything will be good,'” Hrgovic told The Stomping Ground. “I will cuddle him … on the head, like, ‘Moses, everything will be good. Don’t be upset.'”

The mocking humor carried an unforgiving point. Hrgovic pointed out that a loss should light a fire under a fighter rather than shatter his nerve, before making sure to remind everyone who dismantled the hype train.

“You must learn from that that you can’t knock out Filip Hrgovic,” he said. “You must learn you can’t knock out everyone. You must be ready for a 12-round fight.”

That diagnosis is right on the money. Itauma got exposed by his own reliance on early blowouts. Once his power failed to create a shortcut, he had no Plan B, frantically emptying his reserves against an immovable target walking him down.

Surviving at the top level means knowing how to bank rounds without punching yourself into exhaustion. Itauma needs to accept that durable heavyweights will absorb his Sunday punch and keep coming.

Hrgovic threw in obligatory compliments about Itauma’s raw speed, but the core message was pure dismissal.

“No time for crying. Go back to the gym, and that’s it, man. Simple.”

Staring at the tape will not undo the beating. Itauma either learns how to box when the stoppage vanishes, or the next seasoned heavyweight will run the exact same script on him.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II – FIGHT REVIEW
Sports.content:
This past Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, England, in a championship rematch that was available live worldwide on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois made an emphatic statement, stopping former titleholder Fabio Wardley in the 2nd round to successfully retain his championship.

Get DAZN Ultimate Tier HERE

The heavyweight division has been in total chaos ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts, leaving the rest of the division battling for supremacy in a wide-open landscape. Entering the night, the big question was whether Wardley could make the necessary pacing adjustments after dropping Dubois twice early before being stopped in the 11th round of their first encounter five months ago. Instead, Dubois erased all doubt immediately and authored a destructive blowout.

Rather than another back-and-forth war of attrition, Dubois completely flipped the script from their first clash right out of the gate. In the opening seconds of round 1, Dubois caught Wardley flush with a booming shot that dropped the challenger hard to the canvas. Wardley beat the count, but he remained on unsteady legs for the rest of the frame. Staying cool, calm, and composed, Dubois patiently picked his spots and battered Wardley mercilessly before the bell.

Wardley came out for the 2nd round trying to establish his footing and survive the storm, but Dubois was completely dialed in. Stalking his hurt rival with authority, Dubois unleashed another heavy barrage of clubbing shots traps along the ropes, prompting Wardley’s corner to mercifully throw in the towel to save their fighter from further punishment.

This edition of Rummy’s Corner provides a full recap and post-fight review of Dubois’s dominant title defense, while exploring what could be next in the heavyweight division. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: “The Towering Inferno” Fundora Stops Hadribeaj in Final Round
Sports.content:
WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora stopped Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the twelfth and final round of an action-packed but often sloppy fight at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Nevada.

Promoters Tom Brown of TGB Promotions and Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing presented the card Saturday on DAZN and TNT.

In the main event, southpaw Fundora, 25-1-1 (17 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped fellow southpaw Hadribeaj, 23-1-1 (8 KOs), of Tirana, Albania, and Miami Beach, Florida, at 2:59 of the final round.

In the second round, Fundora used his considerable height advantage to hurt Hadribeaj early. The challenger fought back and had Fundora in trouble near the end of the round. In the third, referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point from Hadribeaj for excessive holding.

There was nonstop action from the fourth through the tenth as Hadribeaj forced his way inside and Fundora answered with short punches. The challenger made it competitive, although Fundora held an overall edge and increasingly found success with his body attack.

In the eleventh round, Taylor deducted another point from Hadribeaj for holding. Despite his height disadvantage, the challenger continued trying to force the fight at close range.

In the closing seconds of the twelfth, Fundora dropped Hadribeaj with a left hand. Hadribeaj beat the count but was in no condition to continue, prompting Taylor to wave it off with one second remaining.

In the co-main event, former WBA super middleweight champion Armando “Toro” Resendiz, 17-3 (11 KOs), of Guayabitos, Mexico, defeated Koen Mazoudier, 16-5-1 (6 KOs), of Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, by unanimous decision over ten action-packed rounds.

Resendiz rocked Mazoudier with a right hand to the chin in the final seconds of the fourth round, knocking him off balance. From the sixth through the ninth, Mazoudier pressed the action and fought his way back into the contest, giving the crowd plenty to cheer about while Resendiz continued landing the heavier punches.

In the final minute of the tenth, Resendiz hurt Mazoudier with a flurry of unanswered shots. The Australian survived to hear the final bell.

The scores were 98-92 and 97-93 twice. Harvey Dock was the referee.

In an eight-round super middleweight bout, Jaime Osuna, 12-0 (5 KOs), of Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur, Mexico, won a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi, 13-1-1 (5 KOs), of Palermo, Italy, and Brooklyn, New York.

Osuna suffered a cut over his right eye from a left hook in the third round, which Cangelosi took with his cleaner work.

In the fifth, Osuna rocked Cangelosi early as the fight developed into a slugfest. Cangelosi answered in the seventh, catching Osuna with a right hand to the chin in the closing seconds.

Both had their moments in the eighth and final round, fighting hard with the result still in doubt.

Two judges scored it 77-75 for Osuna, while the third had it even at 76-76. Robert Hoyle was the referee.

Super middleweight Marco “El Tiburon” Romero, 16-0 (14 KOs), of Olathe, Kansas, stopped Matias Ferreira, 8-4 (3 KOs), of Rosario, Uruguay, at 1:54 of the first round of their scheduled eight-round bout.

Ferreira landed a left hook midway through the opening round, but Romero countered with a right hand to the chin that dropped him onto the seat of his trunks. Referee Tony Weeks stopped the contest following the knockdown.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

The scheduled bout between Brandon Figueroa and Tomoki Kameda was canceled after Figueroa became ill following his weight cut. Figueroa was also stripped of his WBA featherweight title after failing to make the division limit.

Sports.title: Ennis vs. Kelly Winner Targeted By Sebastian Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the Jaron Ennis–Josh Kelly winner next, but a potential Ennis fight comes with a financial obstacle: promoter Sampson Lewkowicz’s demand for a 50-50 purse split.

Fundora called for undisputed after stopping Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round. The WBC junior middleweight champion sounded ready to pursue the other belts, although agreeing on an opponent is only part of getting a unification made.

“Absolutely, let’s go for undisputed,” Fundora told DAZN when asked about facing the Ennis–Kelly winner. “We will break them down like we broke this guy, like the guy before that, before that, and before. We’ll keep breaking these guys down.”

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had just completed his fourth successful title defense, wearing down Hadribeaj with short punches and sustained body work before dropping him with a left hand at 2:59 of the final round.

That performance supported his description of breaking opponents down. Hadribeaj made the early rounds competitive by crowding Fundora, but the champion gradually took over through his greater activity inside.

Getting Ennis into the ring could require a different kind of patience. Lewkowicz has called for an equal split for Fundora against Ennis, leaving the financial terms as something the camps would have to resolve if Ennis beats Kelly.

There is no agreement established by Fundora’s post-fight comments, nor do they show that Ennis has accepted or rejected those terms. The potential obstacle is whether an equal split becomes a firm condition or a starting position in negotiations.

Fundora has made his preference clear. If Ennis wins, the next question will be whether the promoters can find a price both sides accept and turn that undisputed ambition into a scheduled fight.

Tonight’s showing only hurts Fundora’s negotiating position. Needing until the final second of the twelfth round to finish a gritty but limited challenger like Hadribeaj showed the exact vulnerabilities that have always followed Fundora. He surrenders his 6’6″ frame, stays glued in the pocket, eats clean shots on the inside, and relies strictly on outlasting foes in a war of attrition.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Stops Ermal Hadribeaj With One Second Left
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora stopped Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round, finishing a physically taxing fight with a left hand after gradually wearing down the challenger with body punches and a higher work rate.

The victory gave Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) his fourth successful defense of the WBC junior middleweight title on Saturday night at The Chelsea at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs) suffered his first defeat after making the champion work considerably harder than his heavy favorite status suggested.

Hadribeaj had little interest in remaining at the end of Fundora’s punches. The challenger stayed low, moved inside and landed hard shots, forcing the taller champion into a fight where his height and reach offered fewer benefits.

A long left hand buzzed Hadribeaj in the second round, but he recovered quickly and returned to pressing the action. Referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point for holding in the third, adding an early cost to the challenger’s attempts to crowd and smother Fundora.

The inside fighting remained competitive through the middle rounds. Hadribeaj landed some of the heavier individual punches, while Fundora answered with more frequent short shots and uppercuts.

Fundora’s body attack became increasingly effective as the fight progressed. Rather than consistently creating distance, he found room to punch where Hadribeaj wanted to fight, digging downstairs and keeping his hands moving.

That made the challenger’s approach harder to sustain. Getting close no longer prevented Fundora from scoring, and Hadribeaj increasingly held as the champion continued working.

Taylor took another point from Hadribeaj in the 11th. By then, Fundora was producing the cleaner, more consistent offense, leaving the challenger needing a dramatic finish.

The decisive punch came from the champion instead. Fundora maintained his pressure in the final round before a left hand dropped Hadribeaj and ended the fight at 2:59.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora vs Ermal Hadribeaj Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Super middleweight Armando Resendiz (17-3, 11 KOs) defeated Koen Mazoudier (16-5-1, 6 KOs) by a 10-round unanimous decision in a hard-fought fight. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93 and 97-93, giving Resendiz a wider victory than the competitive action suggested.

Mazoudier kept coming forward and throwing, making Resendiz work at close range and enjoying success through the middle rounds. Resendiz answered with the heavier punches, hurting the Australian with right hands and left hooks as the two traded throughout.

A sustained attack in the final round left Mazoudier reeling and close to being stopped, but he survived and continued firing back until the bell. Resendiz earned his first victory since losing to Jaime Munguia, while Mazoudier made him fight for it in his U.S. debut.

Marco Romero (16-0, 14 KOs) stopped Braulio Matias Ferreira (8-4, 3 KOs) in the first round of their scheduled eight-round super middleweight fight. The 20-year-old Romero immediately pressed the attack, digging to the body and landing right hands upstairs at close range.

A right hand and left hook to the body helped set up a sweeping right to the chin that dropped Ferreira hard into the ropes. Ferreira beat the count, but he was in no condition to continue, prompting the referee to stop the fight. Romero gave the veteran little chance to settle, keeping him under attack throughout the brief contest. It was the Kansas prospect’s third consecutive first-round stoppage.

Super middleweight Jaime Enrique Osuna Diaz (12-0, 5 KOs) kept his unbeaten record with an eight-round majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi (13-1-1, 5 KOs). The judges scored the competitive bout 77-75, 77-75 and 76-76 on the Sebastian Fundora–Ermal Hadribeaj undercard.

Osuna applied pressure from the start, using his activity and body punching to make Cangelosi work. His best round came in the fifth, when he hurt Cangelosi twice with straight right hands but crowded his own punches while trying to finish.

Cangelosi fought back and had a strong seventh round, landing a big shot to keep the outcome in doubt heading into the eighth. Neither fighter scored a knockdown, with Osuna’s pressure and cleaner work in key stretches earning him the narrow victory.

Ghana News.title: IMF/ World Bank signs agreement with UAE over holding 2029 Annual Meetings in Abu Dhabi
Ghana News.content:
The World Bank Group and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have signed an agreement with the United Arab Emirates to hold the 2029 Annual Meetings in Abu Dhabi.

The President of the World Bank Group, Ajay Banga and the Managing Director of the IMF, Kristalina Georgieva, initialled the agreement on behalf of their respective Institutions, while Mohamed bin Hadi Al Hussaini, Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE and Khaled Mohamed Balama, Governor of the Central Bank, UAE, signed for the UAE.

Speaking at the signing Programme in Bangkok, Thailand, on the Sidelines of the Annual IMF/World Bank meetings, Ajay Banga expressed his excitement about the UAE hosting the 2029 Annual Meetings.

He stated that “we are very delighted that the UAE, Abu Dhabi is the destination of the next Annual Meetings”.

Mr. Banga also highlighted how significant UAE is hosting this Annual Meetings in 2029 is to the group that also happens to host the World Bank’s Knowledge Hub on Gender.

“The World Group is really delighted, because I have had an opportunity of attending two meetings outside Washington, DC, USA, and that has been excellent”, the World Bank President stated.

On her Part,Kristalina Georgieva said, “We are all coming to Abu Dhabi, so prepare for the world. Indeed, the UAE is changing rapidly, a country that is transforming every day”.

“These Annual Meetings outside Washington, DC are the most memorable ones for participants and even the IMF/ World Bank”, the Managing Director of the IMF stated.

Madam Georgieva reminded officials of the UAE that “ We spent a week here in Bangkok, and you saw the preparation, the food and culture, so I can say that Thailand has set a very high standard”.

“But I am optimistic that the UAE is always able to meet this challenge”, she added.

The Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE, said the UAE appreciates the opportunity and would build on the partnership that exit with the IMF/ World Bank.

He said, “we look forward to welcoming members of the IMF/ World Bank back to the UAE after 26 years”.

“I will like to thank the World Bank and the IMF for the trust in our country”, the Minister of State for Financial Affairs, UAE, added.

The Governor of the Central Bank, UAE, for his part said the hosting of the Annual Meetings in 2029 is a vote of confidence in the economy of UAE as well as “our business model and hope to see all the members of IMF/ World Bank in our country soon.

UAE Hosting the Annual Meetings in 2029

The Board of Governors of the IMF/ World Bank in April 2026 voted to select Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates as the host country for the October 2029 meetings.

According to the Finance Ministry of the UAE, hosting the meeting is in line with the UAE's ​strategic vision of strengthening international partnerships.

The last time the Annual Meetings were held in the UAE was in 2003 in Dubai.

The Annual Meetings are usually held for two consecutive years at the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund headquarters in Washington, D.C. and every third year in one of the institutions’ member countries.

The 2026 Annual Meetings, which were hosted in Bangkok, Thailand, from October 12 to 18, have received a lot of praise from the Managing Director of the IMF.

The Meetings bring together central bankers, ministers of finance and development, private sector leaders, and a wide range of stakeholders across civil society, media, and academia to discuss the most pressing issues facing the global economy. This includes global economic and financial stability, job creation, and poverty eradication.

Ghana News.title: Two feared dead, several injured in Walewale road crash involving truck, Voxy
Ghana News.content:
Two people are feared dead in a road accident involving an articulated truck carrying cement, a Toyota Voxy and several motorbikes on the Walewale Road on Sunday, October 18, 2026.

Several others sustained injuries, with initial reports indicating that up to 12 people were hurt, some critically.

However, the Municipal Chief Executive for West Mamprusi, Mohammed Jabaah, told Accra-based Citi News that eight people were injured.

The accident reportedly occurred when the articulated truck, travelling from Walewale, collided with the Toyota Voxy, which was heading from Bolgatanga towards Tamale. Several motorbike riders were also caught up in the collision, while the truck reportedly hit electricity poles.

The circumstances leading to the crash remain unclear, with conflicting accounts of which vehicle lost control.

While initial reports suggest the articulated truck lost control, Mr Jabaah said the Toyota Voxy was responsible for the accident.

“There was a collision between the articulated truck, which was carrying POP cement, and the Toyota Voxy. The Voxy lost control, resulting in the accident, involving several vehicles. Two people died and eight were injured,” he said.

The deceased are reported to include a female student and a motorbike rider.

The injured victims were transported to the Tamale Teaching Hospital and other health facilities for medical attention. Some are reportedly in critical condition.

Investigations are expected to establish the circumstances surrounding the accident and determine what caused the collision.

Ghana News.title: Ghana now has two economies. A Paper Economy and a Pocket Economy – Dr Bawumia
Ghana News.content:
The NPP Presidential Candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has taken a swipe at the NDC government, describing Ghana's current economy as a tale of two economies - a paper economy and a pocket economy.

Speaking at the NPP's National Thanksgiving Service at the Church of Pentecost in Sunyani this morning, Dr Bawumia said despite the government's claim of lower inflation and a stronger cedi, life is still hard for Ghanaians.

"As you can all attest, things are not going well. Things are really hard for the people. And when you ask them what they have done, they will tell you that inflation is down and the dollar is down. The reason we all want inflation and the dollar to go down is because we want it to have a positive impact and make life and the cost of living easier. But if inflation and the dollar go down and the people are suffering, is that how we want it?" he quizzed.

"You cannot have a stable economy with people suffering. The stability should be a way of improving the lives of the people. So what is the use of the stability they are talking about when the people are suffering?"

Farmers, Teachers, Traders Deceived

Dr Bawumia questioned who has benefited from the so-called stability, listing a number of sectors he said have been deceived, alongside Ghanaians.

"Have cocoa farmers benefited? They told them they will pay them 6000 cedis per bag. Has that happened? Have cashew farmers benefited? They told cashew farmers to look for land and expand their farms because they will pay them more but that has not happened. Soybean, rice and maize farmers have all been deceived. Teachers too, the same. Same with nurses and doctors. Traders are also complaining because people are not buying their goods," he said.

He added that electricity bills, water bills, petrol and transport fares have all increased, worsening the cost of living.

On education, Dr. Bawumia accused the government of collapsing Free SHS, failing to cancel double track, failing to cancel the teacher licensure exam, and failing to post teachers automatically as promised.

The NPP flagbearer also took on government over galamsey and the 24-hour economy policy.

"Galamsey is even worse. Maybe when they mentioned 1:3:3 they meant galamsey because galamsey has now more than tripled. Dr. Sam Jonah said our river bodies now look like chocolate milk. They said they would end galamsey within one month but they have failed."

"They promised Ghanaians a new economy called 24-hour economy. We have been waiting for nearly 2 years to see it but it has not happened. Clearly they did not even understand what they were talking about. It was a campaign propaganda to deceive Ghanaians. They said 1:3:3 - one job for three people and the question Ghanaians are asking is, where are the jobs? They also promised to complete Agenda 111 hospitals but they have failed," he added.

Paper Economy vs Pocket Eleconomy

Summing up, Dr Bawumia said Ghana now has two economies.

"One is a paper economy - they say inflation is down and exchange rate is down. The second economy is the pocket economy - the high cost of living and your sufferings. That is more important to the people of Ghana. The stability of the economy is meaningless if it cannot be linked to the liberation of the suffering of our people."

Dr. Bawumia concluded by saying that towards 2028, the NPP will not promise what it cannot do. "We are going with ideas, costed ideas, practical ideas, workable ideas," he stressed.

Ghana News.title: Miracles Aboagye questions discrepancies in South Africa evacuee payment records
Ghana News.content:
The Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has questioned discrepancies in records covering payments to Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa, arguing that the figures do not support claims that all beneficiaries received the full GH¢5,500 allowance.

Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, he said a line-by-line analysis of documents provided by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa showed inconsistencies between the lists of beneficiaries who signed for the payments.

Mr Aboagye said although the minister maintained that all 1,964 evacuees received GH¢5,500 each, the records showed that only 1,001 people signed for the GH¢500 transport allowance.

"The signatures do not match the headcounts. The minister says all 1,964 evacuees , received GH¢5,500. His own signed sheet, which is submitted, carried only about 1,001 signatures for the GH¢500 transport allowance, and 1,508 recorded as receiving only for just the GH¢500.

"Match, name by name, only 824 people appear on both lists. It means, ladies and gentlemen, when our compatriots arrive in Ghana they go to desk one, sign, pick up GH¢5,00 in an envelope, go to desk two, sign, pick up GH¢500 in an envelope, has a total of GH¢5,500. Now, this is what is sad. The document that the foreign affairs minister himself gave to us when you analyse the data line by line, we realised that the people who signed for and collected the GH¢500 are 1,001 people. It means that about 963 of the 1,964 did not receive GH¢500," he said.

According to him, the figures raise questions about whether all the evacuees received the full amount as stated by the minister.

His comments follow a challenge by Mr Ablakwa to the Minority in Parliament to identify a Ghanaian evacuated from South Africa who did not receive the GH¢5,500 allowance.

The minister dismissed allegations of unaccounted funds, describing them as an attempt to create a scandal.

The dispute centres on whether the payment records adequately account for the allowances distributed to all 1,964 evacuees.

Former Vice President and NPP Presidential Candidate, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, says economic stability means nothing if it does not put money in the pockets of ordinary Ghanaians.

Speaking at the NPP's National Thanksgiving Service at the Church of Pentecost in Sunyani this morning, Dr Bawumia said the stability being touted by the NDC government is meaningless to the suffering Ghanaian.

"Our economy is a tale of two economies. One is a paper economy - they say inflation is down and exchange rate is down. The second economy is the pocket economy. The high cost of living and your sufferings. That is more important to the people of Ghana," he said.

"The stability of the economy is meaningless if it cannot be linked up to the liberation of the suffering of our people. If you claim you have stabilised the economy, and it is not reflecting on the lives of the people, it is meaningless. Stability by itself is meaningless unless it is linked up to the total liberation of the pockets of Ghanaians," Dr. Bawumia stressed.

He argued that the purpose of bringing inflation and the dollar down is to make life easier, not harder.

"The reason we all want inflation and dollar to go down is because we want it to have a positive impact and make life and cost of living easier and lower for the people. But if inflation and dollar go down and the people are suffering, is that how we want it? That's not how we want it."

"You cannot have a stable economy with people suffering. The stability should be a way of improving the lives of the people," he added.

Ghana News.title: Recovery is not enough, ‘New Economy’ will turn stability into jobs and higher incomes — Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson wants Ghana’s economic recovery to translate into decent jobs, higher incomes and a stronger productive economy, saying stabilisation is never the ultimate goal of the government’s reforms.

According to him, the ‘New Economy’ would turn the sacrifices made to restore stability into tangible benefits for the Ghanaian people.

He was speaking during an engagement with faculty and students at the University of Ghana,

“Stabilisation was never the destination. It was the price of entry,” he mentioned.

The Finance Minister acknowledged the progress made in restoring economic confidence but stressed that recovery alone could not fulfil the country’s ambitions.

“Ghana has fought hard to restore stability. Inflation has come down. Confidence is returning. Debt pressures are being managed. The economy is recovering. But recovery is not enough.”

Dr Forson said the next task is to build on those gains by expanding production, attracting investment and creating opportunities that improve people’s livelihoods.

“Stability must now become production, exports, investment, decent jobs and higher incomes. That is the central purpose of the New Economy.”

He outlined a vision of a Ghana that produces more of what it consumes, adds value to its agricultural and mineral resources, and creates decent jobs at scale.

That vision also places public investment at the service of private enterprise, opening opportunities for businesses to invest, expand and employ more Ghanaians.

For Dr Forson, the purpose of the transition is to ensure that the benefits of economic recovery reach the people whose sacrifices helped make it possible.

The New Economy, he said, is about building a Ghana that “turns the sacrifices of stabilisation into real benefits for the Ghanaian people.”

Ghana News.title: T-bills auction: Government records 16% undersubscription; interest rates register mixed performance across yield curve
Ghana News.content:
Demand for treasury bills slumped as the government missed its treasury bills target for the first time in several weeks.

According to the Bank of Ghana's auction results, the government recorded an undersubscription of 16%.

The Treasury received GH¢4.17 billion of the total bids but accepted GH¢3.48 billion.

According to the auction results, the majority of the bids came from the 91-day instrument.

A little over GH¢2.9 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 70.5% of the total bids. The uptake was, however, about GH¢2.2 billion.

The 182-day bill received bids of about GH¢1.1 billion. The bids accepted were GH¢692.30.

For the 364-day bill, a little above GH¢1.1 billion in bids were tendered. The Treasury accepted GH¢ 587.61 million of the bids.

Meanwhile, interest rates recorded mixed performance on the yield curve.

The yield on the 91-day bill increased by 2.0 basis points to 4.62%.

Similarly, the yield on the 182-day bill went up to 6.31% from 6.27% the previous week.

However, the yield on the 364-day bill dropped by 4.0 basis points to 9.71%.

Ghana News.content:
A 15-year-old student of Ada Senior High Technical School (ASTECH), Monde Konedu Agyemang, has died after reportedly collapsing during a sporting activity organised as part of the school’s Girls’ Education Week celebration.

The incident occurred on Thursday, October 15, 2026, which was also her 15th birthday.

Monde was rushed to the Sege Polyclinic but was pronounced dead on arrival.

Ada West District Director of Education, Dr Stephen Arthur, said the cause of death was yet to be established, adding that arrangements were being made for an autopsy to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.

He disclosed that the student had enrolled at the school about three weeks before her death and had no known medical condition declared on her admission form.

Her body has since been transferred to the General Hospital as police investigate the incident.

The autopsy is expected to help establish the cause of death.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting intensifies
World.content:
Gulf ministers urge action against Houthis as fighting displaces more than 233,000 people across Yemen.

Share GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as Yemen fighting intensifies on social media

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) has condemned repeated attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi fighters on Saudi Arabia and pledged support for the kingdom.

The political and economic bloc that includes Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates issued a statement on Sunday, shortly after their foreign ministers’ meeting in Manama, Bahrain.

The statement said an attack on any member affected all six, invoking a joint defence agreement and backing Saudi Arabia’s right to protect itself.

The condemnation came as the Saudi-led military coalition fighting the Houthis reported shooting down two drones near Riyadh and in Saudi Arabia‘s Eastern Province early on Sunday.

The coalition said another drone had been intercepted near the capital hours earlier, but did not identify who launched it.

Gulf ministers accused the Houthis of carrying out deadly strikes on civilian airports and vital facilities.

They also pressed for tighter enforcement of a United Nations arms embargo against the group and urged countries to formally designate it “a terrorist organisation”.

The ministers welcomed an October 15 statement from the UN Security Council (UNSC), the body responsible for maintaining international peace, which condemned Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and threats to Red Sea shipping.

Yemen’s internationally recognised government separately appealed to the UNSC to act against Houthi attacks on homes and state facilities.

In letters addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the UNSC’s president for October, Aglaia Balta, the Yemeni government cited an attack on the presidential palace in Aden, where the government is temporarily based.



Separately on Sunday, UAE Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan met Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman Al Saud in Abu Dhabi to discuss regional security, the UAE’s state news agency WAM reported.

Meanwhile, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces press offensives on several fronts.

The Yemeni military said the Houthis fired missiles towards the central city of Marib on Sunday, while government troops reported gains in Taiz, further south.

Government-aligned commanders said eight soldiers died in fighting in Lahij province on Saturday.

Government forces also claimed to have killed 12 Houthi fighters in southern Taiz, figures that could not be independently confirmed.

This latest phase of the war followed Houthi gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month.

Government forces launched a counteroffensive intended to recapture territory from the Houthis, who seized the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

Civilians face deepening shortages

The fighting has uprooted more than 233,000 people, according to the International Organization for Migration, the UN’s migration agency.

About 121,000 are in Taiz province, where supply routes have been disrupted by the fighting.

Al Jazeera’s Hadeel al-Yamani, reporting from Taiz, said cooking gas was unavailable and food stocks were dwindling as Houthi forces blocked supplies through the city’s western entrance.

A local office tracking the siege said food prices had risen fivefold.

The World Health Organization, the UN health agency, warned that Taiz’s 12 hospitals had fuel for just four more days and had run out of surgical supplies.

Oxygen and medicines were also critically scarce as the city struggled with a cholera outbreak.

World.title: Madueke scores only goal as below-par Arsenal beat Nottingham Forest
World.content:
Arsenal did not register a shot on target until Noni Madueke bagged their winner 10 minutes from full-time.

Noni Madueke’s late goal sealed Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest as the champions survived a scrappy display to close the gap on Premier League leaders Manchester City.

Mikel Arteta’s side were well below their best at the City Ground on Sunday and did not register a shot on target until Madueke bagged their winner 10 minutes from full-time.

While the Gunners earned few style points in the East Midlands, they will not be overly concerned after moving to within three points of table-toppers City, who beat Ipswich 3-2 on Saturday.

After a shock 3-0 loss at Brighton on September 19 , second-placed Arsenal have bounced back with three successive victories.

They beat Leeds in the Premier League and Lille in the Champions League, before their hard-fought success by the banks of the River Trent.

The north Londoners have not been able to recapture the relentless consistency that took them to their first title in 22 years last season.

But they retain the priceless ability to grind out wins and this was their sixth in seven league matches.

Arsenal head to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday before hosting Everton in the top flight next weekend.

Third-from-bottom Forest have won just twice at home in their last 17 league games, while boss Oliver Glasner has managed only one victory in seven top-flight matches since taking charge in the close season.

Arsenal leave it late

Bukayo Saka’s cross forced Forest goalkeeper Matz Sels to claw the ball from under his crossbar, but Arsenal struggled to establish any rhythm in a scrappy opening.



Forest’s Dan Ndoye tested Arsenal keeper David Raya after drifting in at the far post.

In a rare threat from Arteta’s men, Kai Havertz fired into the side-netting from an acute angle after Martin Odegaard’s pass opened up the Forest defence.

Arteta looked increasingly frustrated on the touchline as a turgid half petered out.

Eberechi Eze paid the price for Arsenal’s lethargy as the England forward was replaced by Madueke at the interval.

There was no immediate improvement from Arsenal despite that change and Forest striker Liam Delap drilled just wide after a rampaging run.

Arsenal were too slow in possession and lacked penetration when they went forward, so Arteta introduced Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Jurrien Timber in a bid to ignite a revival.

Bruno Guimaraes was one of the Arsenal players sacrificed after another underwhelming display from the Brazil midfielder in only his second league start since his summer move from Newcastle.

Gabriel Magalhaes headed over from a Declan Rice corner, while Delap could not muster the accuracy to beat Raya from Xaver Schlager’s pass.

Odegaard picked out Timber’s run and the defender teed up Declan Rice inside the Forest area, but his wasteful shot ballooned over, encapsulating the visitors’ impotence.

It was the first time since 2023 that Arsenal had failed to have a shot on target in the first 70 minutes of a Premier League match.

But they finally made the breakthrough in the 80th minute as Madueke cut in from the left flank and unleashed a powerful drive that took a hefty deflection off Forest’s Jair Cunha as it flashed past Sels.

Murillo was inches away from snatching a late leveller for Forest as the defender’s rocket whistled over.
