World.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu in Israeli legislative elections
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump has issued an endorsement of Israel’s incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is facing a close race in parliamentary elections scheduled for October 27.

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump praised the Israeli leader for being an ally of the US in its war on Iran. He added that he was giving his “Complete and Total Endorsement” to Netanyahu.

“BIBI NETANYAHU WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!” Trump wrote.

The US president’s backing comes nine days before the Israeli election — and after speculation that it might not come at all.

Trump had refused to endorse Netanyahu earlier this month, when asked repeatedly about the Israeli leader’s job performance in an interview with Time magazine.

Instead, when pressed by his interviewer, Trump avoided the subject, shifting the focus instead to his own popularity or security in the Middle East.

The two leaders have met more than a half dozen times since January 2025, but there have been reports of disagreements, including over the war against Iran and other conflicts.

In June, Trump acknowledged calling Netanyahu “f***ing crazy” in a phone conversation where he expressed frustration about Israel’s attacks on Lebanon.

Trump had reportedly asked Netanyahu not to take further action in Lebanon, in an apparent attempt to preserve a short-lived April ceasefire with Iran.

The two leaders had jointly launched a war against Iran on February 28, but the conflict has cost Trump domestic support.

The war has upended the global oil and gas supply, with no clear end in sight.



A Pew Research Center poll found this month that roughly two-thirds of US voters disapprove of Trump’s handling of the war, which has driven up consumer fuel prices and raised concerns about draining military stockpiles.

Trump’s Republican Party is facing a critical midterm election on November 3 that will decide whether it maintains control of the US Congress, as well as other key state and local offices.

Experts have speculated that Trump’s prior reticence to endorse Netanyahu may have come from public perception that Israel may have coaxed the US into the war.

Netanyahu’s Likud Party and its far-right coalition are also facing the prospect of losing the October contest to an opposition bloc led by Yashar party head Gadi Eisenkot.

But despite reports of fraying relations, Trump told the news outlet Axios on Sunday that his endorsement of Netanyahu was never in doubt.

“I was always going to do that. I just didn’t want to do it too soon,” Trump said in a short telephone interview to the publication, adding: “It is important that Israel has a person they can count on.”

Axios said it questioned Trump about whether he could work with another Israeli leader other than Netanyahu. The US president answered evasively.

“Maybe I will, maybe I won’t. Who wants to take the chance?” Trump replied.

In his social media post announcing the endorsement, Trump also defended his and Netanyahu’s decision to initiate the war against Iran. The president argued it was only a matter of time before Iran would have attacked both the US and Israel.

The war, Trump argued, had already left Iran “systematically destroyed, both Militarily and Financially, and unless they change their ways, rapidly, we will soon finish the job”.

“If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” Trump wrote.

“Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself.”

In response to the post, Netanyahu posted a video on social media expressing gratitude to the US president.

“I’m so honoured and humbled by your extraordinary endorsement,” Netanyahu said. “There’s never been a greater friend of Israel in the White House. That’s an understatement.”

Netanyahu also praised Trump for not being “set back by internal criticism” about the war against Iran. He directed several of his comments to US voters, in an attempt to offer support for Trump’s Republican Party amid questions about the rising cost of living.



“Let me say to the American people: If you are worried about today’s gas prices, think of what will happen if Iran gets nuclear weapons, something that Donald Trump and I will never allow,” Netanyahu said.

“When that threat of that regime disappears, gas prices will go down, and how. But only under Trump. It’s not going to happen with those who want to accommodate and appease these tyrants.”

World.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting
World.content:
France awoke to scenes of widespread damage on Sunday after a day of riots and demonstrations, with shopfronts shattered, burnt out cars, charred bikes, and piles of glass and debris on the pavements of Paris.

Police arrested about 1,800 people on Saturday as some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for protests that were largely peaceful.

They were demonstrating against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings.

Widespread looting took place across the cities of Paris, Marseille and Lille, as well as other areas.

President Emmanuel Macron was due to address the nation at 20:00 local time on Sunday after what has been described as one of the worst outbreaks of disorder in modern French history.

In Paris, protesters clashed with riot police, who turned tear gas and water cannon on the crowds. During the day, some groups lit fires in the street and torched vehicles. At least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups.

Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons.

"It's like we had a war," Paris resident Mehmet Ozeden told news agency AFP.

Another resident, Anita GrasIt, said it was "terrifying" to see groups of young people "smashing everything, with total impunity".

The looters were "proudly carrying supermarket baskets filled with goods and laughing about their thefts", Maryse, a woman living nearby who gave only her first name, told the BBC.

Further south in Marseille, protesters broke into the city hall by using a metal fence as a battering ram. In Lille, a McDonalds was set on fire, police said, and an Apple store in the city was broken into and looted.

World.title: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
World.content:
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.

The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.

A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

Kyiv has not yet commented on the strikes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday morning that Russia had targeted his country's energy sector 76 times since Donald Trump declared an "energy ceasefire" last week.

Ukraine had paused its strikes on Russian oil facilities - which it says are to limit the main revenue stream for Moscow's war effort - for three days after the announcement, while accusing Russia of continuing.

It then resumed strikes earlier this week, drawing the ire of Trump, who called for a truce to facilitate a deal he struck with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to supply diesel.

Ukraine has struck St Petersburg before, though regions closer to Ukraine are threatened more often. The city's oil terminal was last hit in July.

Russia's defence ministry said it had shot down more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight into Sunday.

St Petersburg's governor said 12 apartment buildings and two homes were damaged in the attacks on the city, while Pulkovo Airport was temporarily closed.

He also said mobile internet service disruption was possible.

Social network VK confirmed a drone had targeted its regional data centre, but stressed its services were available "as usual" after users reported outages in the early hours of the morning.

Ozon also confirmed its local logistics centre had been targeted by a drone, sparking a fire.

It said staff were evacuated and no one was injured, and that it was not accepting shipments from sellers at the location "as it is currently serving other operational purposes".

As well as numerous oil facilities across Russia, Ukraine has also mounted strikes aimed at disrupting the Russian economy more broadly. Earlier this month, it launched a series of attacks on Yandex, Russia's largest search engine, that led to service disruptions.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv have frayed since the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel in the hope of bringing down US energy prices, which have skyrocketed during the Iran war, ahead of the midterm elections.

Zelensky suggested the deal was tantamount to the US investing in Russia's war effort.

Trump's decision to temporarily suspend a raft of sanctions against Russia has brought fresh criticism, including from some US Republicans.

However, on Sunday, Zelensky said on Telegram he had had conversations with Trump's top negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

He said their teams are in constant communication and preparing the next diplomatic steps.

Both Russia and Ukraine have been striking one another's energy infrastructure with increasing intensity ahead of the winter, as Moscow's full-scale invasion drags on in its fifth year.

Russia says it hits targets used by Ukraine's military, though the UN noted on Friday that the first two weeks of October had been the deadliest for Ukrainian civilians in years.

Russian strikes on energy facilities have left hundreds of thousands without power, raising concerns about civilians enduring another freezing winter.

Zelensky said on Saturday that tens of thousands of people were still without power. Russia launched nearly 2,700 drones, 1,700 aerial bombs and 66 missiles in the past week, most of which were aimed at energy facilities, he said.

World.title: A wave of homemade, synthetic drugs sweeps US and deepens crisis
World.content:
Warning: This story contains descriptions of drug-taking from the start and discusses suicide

The few grains of fentanyl sit in the silver foil as a straw, held between Mike's lips, hovers above, with a cigarette lighter below. The 48-year-old army veteran is crouched low in an alleyway in Columbus, Ohio's Linden neighbourhood.

"This drug will damn near make you do anything, unfortunately," he says.

The hit he's smoking cost three or four dollars.

"You can snort too much and you can't take it back. Kind of like a gunshot. Can't call the bullet back," he says.

He burns the foil and inhales. As the opioid takes hold, he grips the fence behind him. He sways as a low moan comes from deep in his throat - he could be humming a tune.

We've spent a few days with Mike - he's been our guide through the neighbourhood's back streets. Everyone seems to know him and he's regarded fondly. He helps out at a local pawn shop and gas station, and that's how he feeds his 20-year-old opioid addiction.

Synthetic opioids are more powerful and in plentiful supply, and they have transformed the drugs landscape.

Fentanyl, which is entirely man-made, is 50 to 100 times more powerful than heroin, which is cultivated from poppies. It is now often cut with synthetic tranquillisers, which make reviving overdose victims more difficult. These are homemade threats, where cocktails of synthetics can be made in American basements and bathtubs.

World.title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
World.content:
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.

But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".

The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".

It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".

World.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as row with Zelensky intensifies
World.content:
Donald Trump has blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky deepens.

The sanctions were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September.

But Trump issued an executive order on Friday night saying that suspending some was in the US national interest, prompting a backlash from US lawmakers. Zelensky said it was unfortunate the US has decided to "completely disregard" the sanctions.

Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev said Trump's order was "an important and truly historic moment", and that the sanctions would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market.

Relations between Washington and Kyiv frayed after the US struck a controversial deal to import Russian diesel last week. Ukraine has accused the Trump administration of withdrawing key military support.

Since then, Ukraine's president declared it was nice to be among "real leaders" while addressing an EU summit, after Trump said Zelensky was "more difficult to deal with" than Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The sanctions suspension seemed to add further fuel to the fire.

Zelensky said on Saturday morning that the sanctions "could have helped enormously" and that the law was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end".

He pointed to Russian overnight attacks on 15 Ukrainian energy facilities that had caused power cuts in several regions and said: "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine â right before winter."

Zelensky said it was "important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening" on the ground.

World.title: Anti-government protesters battle with police in Albania
World.content:
Demonstrators and riot police fought pitched battles in the centre of Tirana on Saturday for the fifth day in a row.

Masked protesters, many of them high school and university students, hurled rocks and petrol bombs at riot police trying to defend the education ministry, one of the focal points of the protests.

The police responded with water cannon and volleys of tear gas, sending the crowds scattering. There are also reports that rubber bullets were used for the first time.

Protests which began in the summer have grown into a wider anti-government movement, with calls for the prime minister to resign following corruption allegations linked to his administration.

Many of the protesters in central Tirana wore gas masks or face masks, while volunteers handed out syringes of saline eyewash to reduce the pain from the tear gas which billows down the street.

The constant boom of petrol bombs could be heard exploding on Saturday.

During the afternoon, the focus of the protests shifted to the office of Prime Minister Edi Rama on the city's main boulevard.

Here the crowds swelled to far larger numbers than on previous days.

Riot police faced a steady hail of cobble stones and fireworks, and responded with barrage after barrage of tear gas, some of the canisters landing far back in the crowds, causing panic.

Incensed by the gas, the crowds waited for it to clear, then renewed their attacks.

World.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
World.content:
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.

A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.

Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday.

"We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku.

The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.

But the weather - powered by strong El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific - has so far prevented them from beginning a second of three phases, in which underwater objects will be probed to determine their depth and sediment will be dredged.

World.title: At least 17 dead in crush at Hindu festival event in India
World.content:
At least 17 people have been killed and many more injured in a crush at an event in the Indian city of Kolkata to mark the Hindu festival of Durga Puja, officials say.

The incident occurred during sudden rainfall, which witnesses say prompted a surge of people to try to seek shelter.

West Bengal's Chief Minister Suvendhu Adhikari said a seven-year-old girl was among the dead, and that 25 people were being treated for injuries.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the regional government was providing help to affected families.

Six of the dead have been identified, Adhikari said.

A senior police official told the AFP news agency that an announcement caused "commotion" after it started raining and the crowd started "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede.".

Deadly crowd incidents, including during religious festivals, are not uncommon in India due to poor management and lack of adequate safety precautions.

Two years ago, 121 people were killed in Uttar Pradesh during a Hindu religious gathering.

World.title: Nigerian inventor’s bionic arm named among TIME’s best inventions of 2026
World.content:
Nigerian inventor Ubokobong Amanam has earned international recognition after TIME magazine named his bionic arm, designed to restore both the appearance and functionality of missing limbs, among its Best Inventions of 2026.

Mr Amanam, who hails from Akwa Ibom State, South-South Nigeria, announced the recognition in a Facebook post on Thursday, describing it as a milestone for African innovation and a reminder that transformative ideas can emerge from anywhere.

Immortal Cosmetic Art developed the invention, known as the Ubokobong Bionic Arm, after Mr Amanam co-founded the company with his brother, John, following a fireworks accident that cost him his fingers on New Year’s Day in 2019.

According to TIME, Mr Amanam struggled to find a prosthetic hand that matched his dark skin tone after the accident. His brother, a special-effects artist, subsequently crafted a highly realistic artificial hand for him. This experience inspired the brothers to create lifelike prosthetics for other Black amputees.

The project later evolved beyond cosmetic restoration when John, drawing on his special-effects expertise and his brother’s background in technology and electronics, developed a prosthetic that combines a realistic appearance with functional movement.

The resulting bionic arm is myoelectric, meaning the user’s muscles generate electrical signals that control it. The technology enables amputees to operate the prosthesis through muscle activity rather than relying solely on a passive artificial limb.

TIME said clients in 56 countries were using the device, highlighting the international reach of an innovation that emerged from a personal struggle to find a suitable prosthesis.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In his announcement, Mr Amanam said the recognition was inspired by his experience and the pain he endured after the accident.

“This international recognition is a significant milestone for African innovation and a reminder that world-changing ideas can emerge from anywhere,” he wrote.

He added that he hoped his journey would encourage others to persevere, innovate, and develop solutions that can make a lasting contribution to humanity.

The recognition also points to the importance of designing assistive technologies that account for the needs and physical characteristics of users who have historically been underserved by conventional prosthetics.

For many amputees, prosthetic devices are more than functional aids. Their appearance, fit, and ability to reflect a user’s skin tone can affect comfort, confidence, and social interaction.

By combining realistic skin-tone matching with muscle-controlled movement, the Ubokobong Bionic Arm seeks to address both the practical and psychological challenges associated with limb loss.

The recognition places a Nigerian-developed assistive technology among the innovations TIME selected for its 2026 list, drawing international attention to African inventors’ ability to develop solutions with applications beyond the continent.

The recognition follows earlier reporting by PREMIUM TIMES on Mr Amanam’s work in medical technology. In June, the newspaper reported that he had launched a robotic rehabilitation glove designed to help stroke survivors and people with hand disabilities regain movement. The device features guided hand exercises and mirror-mode training intended to support rehabilitation.

The bionic arm has also attracted international media attention. A Reuters report published in August 2025 examined how the brothers developed the prosthesis to address the shortage of realistic, functional artificial limbs designed for Black amputees.

World.title: How I’ve managed diabetes for 30 years — Jide Kosoko
World.content:
Veteran actor Jide Kosoko has disclosed that he has lived with diabetes for 30 years, sharing how he has managed the condition over the years.

In an excerpt from his interview on actress Biola Adebayo’s “Talk To B” podcast, which went viral on Sunday, the 72-year-old said his long experience with the condition had taught him to pay closer attention to his health.

He added that living with diabetes had made him take regular medical tests seriously to ensure that his health remained stable.

He said: “My daily activities help my health so much. I became diabetic in 1996. So, I’ve been managing it. So, you can easily understand that I understand it. In fact, I understand my health more than some doctors. And I know when to take sugar and not to. Take this or take that—my medication.

“I refuse to allow anybody to deceive me into thinking that any herb can solve it. We know the causes of high blood sugar. And as such, you need to understand your ailments. Get to understand your body. I have several signs to determine. It’s like I need sugar. I need to rest. So, with that, you are good to go.”

Foundation

Kosoko said his experience of living with diabetes and undergoing a colonoscopy inspired him to consider establishing a foundation to help less privileged colleagues access medical tests.

He encouraged fellow actors and Nigerians to prioritise their health and take necessary steps to prevent avoidable medical complications.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The actor pledged to cover the medical testing costs of colleagues who could not afford them, urging them to take their health seriously.

“They check everything. To detect if there are any ailments. Or maybe cancer or something is growing anywhere within. And yeah, it wasn’t difficult. In fact, it wasn’t just a colonoscopy; there was another test.

“After doing everything, if death eventually comes, to God be the glory. He knows when he wants to call you. But you need to try for yourself. It’s important. We should not wait until things get worse. Anybody can die anytime”, said Kosoko.

“20% of your earnings”

Kosoko said illness could affect anyone, but stressed the need to identify and address its underlying causes to prevent future health problems.

He added that maintaining good health did not necessarily require money, but depended on following basic health guidelines, including avoiding alcohol and cannabis smoking.

He noted, “Whatever amount you are making, 20% of it is not too much to take care of yourself. Use the remaining 80% for whatever you want to do. It’s important. Our people out there, our fans, they don’t even know how much we help ourselves. They don’t know. I have been challenged on several occasions that ‘Your colleague is having this. You are not doing it.’ I say, you are only stupid because I don’t need to come to see you to help my colleague.

“There is no way one person can actually settle you completely. Is it possible? You have different things besides ailments. You have other responsibilities. You have things you need to do; in fact, we must work towards ensuring we have a trust fund as a body and work independently. To take care of all practitioners. Each of us must subscribe, even if it is one Naira. Our helpers out there are willing to help.”

“From 40 years upward”

The actor also advised people aged 40 and above to make regular medical check-ups a priority, stressing the importance of monitoring their health as they grow older.

He explained that routine tests could help uncover hidden health conditions before they become serious.

“If you get to know it on time. Am I looking like a diabetic patient? If you see me coming down, you should know it is age, if not for this topic and maybe because my dosage and medications are a regular thing. I have even seen it as food. I don’t always keep it in mind, even if I have any ailments. I have forgotten.

“But my normal daily things. Working towards my good health. I take them. And I will advise, because I only know diabetes. And my advice to all diabetic patients is to use your drugs as prescribed. Reduce your food. Eat anything you like to eat. Anything you like to eat. Moderately. In fact, my stomach cannot even take any more because I have so much to curb myself.”

World.title: Food Security: Abiodun deepens Ogun’s agricultural transformation drive, By Kayode Akinmade
World.content:
With support for 10,000 farmers, new mechanisation equipment, digital technology and investments in agro-processing, Governor Dapo Abiodun is pursuing a multi-pronged strategy to boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses and improve farmers’ livelihoods.

As Nigeria grapples with food affordability and rising agricultural production costs, Ogun State, under Governor Dapo Abiodun, is strengthening efforts to improve food security through targeted support for farmers, mechanisation, digital innovation and investments across the agricultural value chain.

The latest intervention, unveiled at the 2026 World Food Day celebration in Abeokuta, provides a clear indication of this approach. It targets 10,000 rice and cassava farmers with subsidised farm inputs, alongside the distribution of 10 tractors, other agricultural equipment and 1,200 Android phones equipped with applications for weather information, market prices and best agricultural practices.

The initiative reflects an understanding that improving food security requires more than increasing the volume of crops planted. It also demands affordable inputs, timely information, efficient production systems, better storage, processing facilities and reliable access to markets.

For farmers, the cost of fertilisers, herbicides, improved planting materials and machinery can determine whether a farming season produces a profit or deepens existing financial difficulties. By intervening in these areas, the Ogun State Government is seeking to reduce some of the barriers confronting farmers while improving their capacity to respond to market demands.

At the World Food Day event, themed “Innovate Today, Nourish Tomorrow,” Abiodun announced a package of agricultural inputs for 2,000 rice farmers and 8,000 cassava farmers.

Under the arrangement, each beneficiary will receive two bags of fertiliser and one bag of urea. Cassava farmers will also receive 25 bundles of cassava stems each, while the government will provide 10 litres of herbicides to each beneficiary cassava farmer and three litres to each beneficiary rice farmer.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to the state government, beneficiaries will contribute 30 per cent of the cost of the inputs, depending on the category, while the government will cover the remaining 70 per cent through its partnership with the International Fund for Agricultural Development.

The cost-sharing arrangement is intended to make essential farm inputs more accessible while supporting farmers to increase production. Its ultimate impact will depend on the timely distribution of the inputs, effective monitoring and the extent to which the intervention translates into higher yields and better incomes.

For a state with considerable agricultural potential and proximity to major consumer markets, such interventions carry economic significance beyond the farm. Increased production can support food processing, transportation, wholesale and retail trade, while creating employment opportunities for people who may not be directly engaged in cultivation.

Mechanisation and the Productivity Challenge

One of the longstanding challenges of Nigerian agriculture is the limited access of smallholder farmers to modern equipment. Dependence on manual labour can restrict the size of cultivated land, delay planting and harvesting, and increase in production costs.

The distribution of 10 tractors and other agricultural equipment to farm settlements and farmers’ associations is part of Ogun State’s response to this challenge.

Abiodun disclosed that his administration had also procured 39 tractors, four self-propelled harvesters and other agricultural equipment to support mechanisation across the sector.

The importance of mechanisation lies not merely in the number of machines acquired but in the additional land farmers can cultivate, the time saved during critical farming operations and the reduction in losses caused by delays in planting and harvesting.

When appropriately deployed and maintained, tractors and harvesters can help farmers improve operational efficiency and increase production. Shared access through farm settlements and farmers’ associations can also extend the benefits of mechanisation to farmers who cannot afford to purchase equipment individually.

For these investments to deliver sustainable results, however, arrangements for maintenance, spare parts, fuel, operator training and equitable access will be essential.

The objective is to establish a system in which agricultural machinery remains productive, serves a broad base of farmers and contributes to sustained improvements in output.

Digital Technology Comes to the Farm

Another notable feature of the intervention is the distribution of 1,200 Android phones loaded with applications providing weather information, market prices and guidance on good agricultural practices.

The initiative recognises the growing role of information in modern agriculture.

Weather information can help farmers make better decisions about planting and other farm operations, while market-price data can improve their understanding of where and when to sell their produce. Access to agricultural information can also help farmers adopt improved practices and respond more effectively to changing conditions.

For farmers operating in an increasingly unpredictable environment, timely information can influence both productivity and profitability.

The digital initiative is linked to the Ogun State Farmer Information Management System, launched in April 2023 to support agricultural planning and targeted interventions.

Abiodun disclosed that more than 160,000 farmers and agricultural value-chain actors had been captured on the platform.

The database provides a foundation for identifying farmers, understanding their needs and improving the delivery of government support. It can also help the state develop more evidence-based agricultural policies, provided the information is regularly updated and effectively used.

The challenge ahead is to ensure that the technology reaches farmers who need it, that beneficiaries can use the applications effectively and that the information provided is reliable and relevant to local farming conditions.

If these conditions are met, digital technology can become an important tool for bridging information gaps between farmers, agricultural extension services, markets and policymakers.

From Primary Production to Agro-Industrial Development

Beyond the immediate provision of farm inputs and equipment, the Abiodun administration has identified agro-processing as an important component of its agricultural transformation agenda.

The governor disclosed that 28 agricultural projects had been completed in the preceding two years across crop production, aquaculture and poultry.

The projects include solar dryers, warehouses, cassava processing centres and a poultry processing plant at Ajegunle Farm Settlement in Odeda Local Government Area.

According to the governor, the poultry facility has the capacity to process 5,000 birds daily, equivalent to approximately 1.3 million birds annually.

Such facilities are important because agricultural production alone does not guarantee improved incomes for farmers. Where storage and processing infrastructure are inadequate, produce can deteriorate before reaching consumers, while farmers may be forced to sell quickly at unfavourable prices.

Processing facilities can create additional markets for agricultural produce, reduce avoidable losses and support the development of businesses involved in packaging, distribution and food manufacturing.

Cassava processing, for instance, can create opportunities beyond the sale of fresh roots, while poultry processing can improve the handling and distribution of poultry products.

Warehouses and solar dryers can help preserve produce, reduce spoilage and give farmers greater flexibility in deciding when to sell.

The broader economic objective is to retain more value within Ogun State by encouraging agricultural produce to be processed locally rather than sold exclusively in its raw form.

This approach also offers opportunities for industrial investment, especially when farmers can supply processors with consistent quantities and quality of produce.

For Ogun, whose location provides access to major markets, the development of an integrated agricultural value chain could strengthen the relationship between farming, manufacturing, logistics and commerce.

OGSTEP and the Market Connection

The Ogun State Economic Transformation Project (OGSTEP) is another component of the administration’s agricultural development efforts.

Abiodun said agribusiness firms under the programme had purchased more than 283,000 tonnes of agricultural produce, while farmers organised into clusters had received capacity-building support and connections to off-takers.

The emphasis on market access addresses one of the central difficulties confronting farmers: producing crops without having dependable buyers or sufficient information about market conditions.

Connections between farmers and off-takers can help create more predictable demand, while organised clusters can improve coordination, facilitate access to training and inputs, and make it easier for buyers to source produce in commercial quantities.

Where these relationships are sustained, farmers may be better positioned to plan production, negotiate sales and reduce the uncertainty associated with finding markets after harvest.

The reported purchases under OGSTEP also point to the importance of linking agricultural production with commercial demand.

The next stage of the process is to deepen these connections, expand participation and ensure that the benefits of commercial agriculture reach smallholder farmers as well as larger agribusinesses.

Investing in the Next Generation

Agriculture’s capacity to create employment is particularly important in a country with a large population of young people seeking sustainable sources of income.

Yet attracting young Nigerians to farming requires more than encouraging them to cultivate the land. It requires demonstrating that agriculture can support viable businesses through technology, modern production methods, access to finance and dependable markets.

Abiodun disclosed that his administration had partnered with Soilless Farm Lab to train more than 200 young people in soilless farming and provide start-up support to beneficiaries.

Soilless farming offers an alternative production method that can be used in appropriate settings to cultivate selected crops without conventional soil-based cultivation. Depending on the crop, system and operating costs, it can create opportunities for intensive production and specialised agribusiness.

The training initiative represents an effort to expose young people to alternative farming methods and equip them with skills that can support enterprise development.

For such programmes to generate lasting results, training must be accompanied by access to productive resources, business guidance, financing and markets. The long-term measure of success will be the number of viable enterprises established, the jobs created and the extent to which beneficiaries can sustain their operations.

Women also remain central to agricultural production, processing and food distribution. Improving their access to land, inputs, technology, finance and markets can strengthen household incomes and broaden participation in the agricultural economy.

These considerations underline the need for agricultural programmes to combine production support with enterprise development and inclusive economic opportunities.

Land, Investment and Agricultural Expansion

Access to suitable land is another factor that can determine the scale and efficiency of agricultural investment.

The governor said his administration established the Ogun State Agricultural Land Management Agency to facilitate access to land and promote a responsible and inclusive framework for land-intensive agricultural investment.

The agency is intended to address land-access challenges while encouraging investment in commercial agriculture.

At his World Food Day address, Professor Kolawole Adebayo, a former Deputy Vice-Chancellor of the Federal University of Agriculture, Abeokuta, noted that Ogun State had approximately 1.2 million hectares of arable land, representing significant potential for agricultural production and agro-industrial development.

He argued that the state needed forward-looking policies and sustained investment in innovation to realise this potential.

The availability of arable land, however, is only one part of the equation. Agricultural expansion also requires dependable water supplies, suitable roads, storage facilities, access to finance, appropriate technology and a functioning market system.

Adebayo called for an integrated transport network linking rail, road, water and air transport to improve the movement of agricultural produce and preserve its quality before it reaches consumers.

The proposal reflects a broader challenge in food distribution: even when farmers achieve good harvests, poor transportation and inadequate storage can increase costs and reduce the quantity of food that reaches the market in good condition.

Better connectivity between farms, processing centres, warehouses and urban markets could therefore complement investments in production.

For Ogun State, the opportunity lies in linking its agricultural resources with its industrial base, transport connections and proximity to large consumer markets.

Building a More Resilient Food System

The administration’s agricultural initiatives are also part of a wider effort to strengthen the state’s contribution to national food security.

Abiodun commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for efforts to strengthen local fertiliser production and improve farmers’ access to agricultural inputs. He also acknowledged the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for initiatives supporting women farmers.

The governor said Ogun would continue to complement federal agricultural interventions through targeted support for farmers, responsible investment and stronger market linkages.

Speaking at the World Food Day celebration, the Commissioner for Agriculture and Food Security, Bolu Owotomo, stressed that access to nutritious and affordable food was fundamental to human dignity and sustainable development.

He called for greater investment in women and young people through improved access to land, finance, training, technology and profitable agricultural opportunities. He also disclosed that more than 12,000 farmers had benefited from training and agricultural inputs under OGSTEP.

The National Programme Coordinator of the Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones Programme, Dr Kabiru Yusuf, represented by the National Agriculture Expert, Dr Louis Enaberue, commended the state government for its support for agriculture and urged beneficiaries to make effective use of the equipment and inputs provided.

Similarly, the South-West Coordinator of the Commodity Farmers Association of Nigeria, Prince Segun Dasaolu, acknowledged the state’s interventions, while Rotimi Sogunle, speaking on behalf of farm settlers, thanked the governor for supporting farming communities.

Their remarks highlighted the importance of sustained collaboration among government, farmers, development partners, research institutions and private investors.

The Road Ahead

Ogun State’s agricultural strategy combines immediate support for farmers with investments intended to strengthen the wider agricultural economy.

The provision of subsidised inputs can help address production costs. Mechanisation can improve operational efficiency, while digital tools can expand access to information. Processing and storage facilities can create additional markets, reduce post-harvest losses and support value addition. Training and access to land can also open opportunities for new agricultural enterprises.

The ultimate test, however, will be the results these interventions produce over time.

Higher yields, lower production costs, improved farmers’ incomes, reduced post-harvest losses, greater private investment and increased availability of affordable food will provide more concrete measures of progress than the number of projects launched or equipment distributed.

Effective implementation, transparent beneficiary selection, regular monitoring and proper maintenance of public agricultural assets will be critical to sustaining the gains.

Equally important is the need to ensure that smallholder farmers, who constitute a significant part of the agricultural sector, can access the opportunities created by government programmes and private investment.

The 2026 World Food Day intervention places these issues in focus. By combining support for 10,000 rice and cassava farmers with mechanisation, digital technology and investments across the agricultural value chain, the Ogun State Government is seeking to address several constraints on food production simultaneously.

Whether these efforts translate into lasting improvements in food security will depend on their implementation, reach and measurable impact on the people who produce and consume food.

For Ogun State, the challenge is to turn agricultural potential into sustained productivity, profitable enterprises and a more resilient food system—one in which farmers earn better incomes, businesses find opportunities to grow and consumers have improved access to nutritious and affordable food.

*Akinmade is the Special Adviser to Governor Dapo Abiodun on Information and Strategy

World.title: Murray-Bruce says Donald Duke once praised Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, shares photo
World.content:
Former senator Ben Murray-Bruce has claimed that former Cross River State Governor and Peoples Redemption Party presidential candidate for the 2027 Nigeria general election, Donald Duke, previously praised the vision behind the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.

He challenged Mr Duke to reconcile the alleged endorsement with his recent criticism of the project.

Mr Murray-Bruce made the claim in a Facebook post on Friday, addressing Mr Duke directly and recalling an earlier trip they allegedly made together along the coastline where the highway is being constructed.

To reinforce his account, Mr Murray-Bruce attached a photograph that appears to show both men standing on a coastal road. However, the photograph does not independently prove when or where it was taken, or what Mr Duke said about the project at the time.

“Some years ago, you and I travelled along the stretch of the coastline where this road now runs, and I clearly remember your praise for the vision behind it. That is why your recent comments surprised me,” Mr Murray-Bruce wrote.

He acknowledged that the highway was expensive but insisted that the cost should be weighed against its potential long-term benefits.

“Great nations are built by leaders willing to make bold, costly investments that will serve generations yet unborn,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Murray-Bruce also defended President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to financing the project, insisting that there was no funding shortfall and that construction was progressing.

He described the work as international standard, aligning himself with Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, who defended the highway against Mr Duke’s criticism.

“When Governor Douye Diri commended the road, he was not speaking as a local champion; he was speaking as a statesman who recognises infrastructure of international standard when he sees it. I agree with him completely,” Mr Murray-Bruce said.

Mr Duke had questioned the project’s cost and feasibility, raising concerns about the proposed route through Bayelsa State’s swampy terrain and whether the country could afford such an expensive undertaking.

His criticism prompted Mr Diri to defend the project, after which Mr Duke described the governor as a “local champion”, arguing that his assessment failed to consider Nigeria’s financial constraints and competing development priorities sufficiently.

Mr Murray-Bruce, however, suggested that Mr Duke’s criticism was influenced by his reported ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election.

“Donald, I understand that you are running for president, and that your statement is political. That is the nature of the season, and I respect your right to make your case to Nigerians,” he wrote.

“But we must be careful never to undermine a project of national importance, or the President delivering it, simply for political advantage.”

He compared the highway to the United States’ moon-landing programme, saying expensive projects can deliver lasting benefits to future generations.

“When mankind went to the moon, it was neither cheap nor free. But it was necessary. So is this road,” he said.

Duke yet to respond

PREMIUM TIMES made several telephone calls to Mr Duke on Friday afternoon to seek his reaction to Mr Murray-Bruce’s claim that he had previously praised the project, but he did not answer.

The newspaper also sent a media enquiry through text message, WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger, asking whether Mr Duke had previously visited and commended any stretch of the highway and seeking his response to the allegation that his criticism was politically motivated. He had not responded as of the time of filing this report.

The exchange also comes against the backdrop of Mr Murray-Bruce’s open support for Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

The former Bayelsa East senator defected from the PDP to the ruling APC in October 2025 and later said he would vote for Mr Tinubu in 2027, citing confidence in the president’s reforms.

Mr Murray-Bruce, who hails from Akassa in Bayelsa State, represented Bayelsa East in the Senate from 2015 to 2019. His defence of the coastal highway aligns him with Mr Diri, the Bayelsa governor, who has also defended the project against Mr Duke’s criticism.

The exchange adds a new dimension to the debate over the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, shifting attention beyond its cost and engineering feasibility to whether Mr Duke’s current position differs from his alleged earlier assessment.

Mr Murray-Bruce’s account of the earlier visit and the circumstances surrounding the photograph could not be independently verified by PREMIUM TIMES as of the time of filing this report.

World.title: Two killed, two injured in Lagos road crash – LASTMA
World.content:
Two people have died and two others sustained serious injuries in a road crash involving a commercial bus and a pickup van along the Adekunle corridor, inward Iyana Oworo, in Lagos, the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has said.

The crash involved a Suzuki commercial bus with registration number KTU 333 YF and a pickup van, according to a statement LASTMA posted on X on Sunday.

LASTMA said its operatives responded to the scene, coordinated rescue efforts and secured the area. The two injured victims, a man and a woman, were taken to the General Hospital, Odan, for treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were handed over to the Lagos State Environmental Health Monitoring Unit (SEHMU), popularly known as SHEMU.

The agency noted that its operatives handed over the vehicles and the Suzuki bus driver to officers of the Yaba Police Division, who maintained order until the rescue and recovery operations were completed.

Between January and March, LASTMA recorded 69 deaths and 246 injuries in road crashes across Lagos, according to a report by Radio Nigeria Lagos. The agency also attended to more than 600 accident scenes during the period.

LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed condolences to the families of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery.

He urged motorists to obey traffic regulations, observe speed limits, maintain safe following distances and ensure their vehicles were roadworthy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The agency did not disclose the cause of the crash.

World.title: Lagos ready to host CAF 2026 Awards, Gov Sanwo-Olu assures
World.content:
Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has assured the Confederation of African Football (CAF) of the state government’s readiness to host the 2026 CAF Awards, scheduled for 7 December.

Mr Sanwo-Olu gave the assurance after meeting a CAF delegation led by Christian Emeruwa, the organisation’s Head of Safety and Security and project lead for the awards and its Ordinary General Assembly.

In a Facebook post, the governor said the state was committed to ensuring a smooth event, with particular attention to security, logistics, branding and access to the venue.

“Lagos is pleased to host the 2026 Confederation of African Football (CAF) Awards this December,r and we are committed to making it a memorable experience,” he wrote.

“Meeting with the CAF delegation, led by Dr Christian Emeruwa, Project Lead for the CAF Awards and CAF General Assembly, I assured them of our full support, with particular attention to security, logistics, branding and venue access.”

The governor said the ceremony would provide an opportunity to showcase Lagos’ culture, enterprise and hospitality to visitors from across Africa and beyond.

The awards will bring together leading African footballers, coaches, clubs and administrators to recognise outstanding performances in the men’s and women’s games.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

CAF delegation inspects facilities

The meeting comes as CAF and Nigerian authorities prepare for two major events on the continental football calendar.

According to the inspection schedule announced by the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), a 15-member CAF delegation is on the ground to assess facilities in Lagos and Abuja ahead of the awards and the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly.

The inspection programme includes the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, Eko Hotel & Suites and Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos.

In Abuja, the delegation is scheduled to inspect the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre, Transcorp Hilton Hotel and Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport.

The General Assembly is scheduled for 21 November at the Bola Ahmed Tinubu International Conference Centre in Abuja, while the awards ceremony will take place in Lagos on 7 December.

This latest inspection process follows an earlier visit by CAF officials from 31 July to 4 August, when representatives of the institutions and agencies involved in organising the events discussed coordination and other arrangements.

A six-member NFF team led by its Director of Communications, Ademola Olajire, is also expected to accompany the CAF delegation during the inspections.

Nigeria’s history at the CAF Awards

The 2026 ceremony will give Nigerian football another chance to feature prominently at the continent’s annual awards.

Nigeria has produced several winners in the men’s and women’s Player of the Year categories. Victor Osimhen won the men’s award in 2023, followed by Ademola Lookman in 2024.

Their successive victories continued a tradition set by Nwankwo Kanu, who won in 1996 and 1999, and Victor Ikpeba, who won in 1997.

At the 2024 ceremony in Marrakech, Morocco, Nigeria’s Super Falcons were named Women’s National Team of the Year, while goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie won the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year award.

At the 2025 edition in Rabat, Morocco’s Achraf Hakimi and Ghizlane Chebbak won the men’s and women’s Player of the Year awards, respectively. Nnadozie retained the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year honour.

Beyond recognising individual and team achievements, the Lagos ceremony will place the state before an international audience of football officials, players and visitors.

Mr Sanwo-Olu said the state looked forward to welcoming football leaders and guests while demonstrating its capacity to host major international events.

The preparations will require coordination among the state government, CAF, the NFF, and other relevant agencies, particularly on security, transport, accommodation, and access to the ceremony venue.

World.title: CAF Champions League: Rangers strike late to beat MC Alger
World.content:
Rangers International secured a crucial 2-0 victory over Algerian champions MC Alger in the first leg of their CAF Champions League second preliminary-round tie at the MKO Abiola Stadium in Abeokuta on Sunday.

Despite Rangers playing with 10 men from the 13th minute, MC Alger conceded two late goals in the 84th and 87th minutes, resulting in a 2-0 victory for the Flying Antelopes.

Kenneth Igboke converted a penalty in the 84th minute before James Emo struck three minutes later to give the Nigerian champions a valuable advantage ahead of the return leg in Algeria.

The late goals rewarded Rangers’ persistence and gave the Flying Antelopes a two-goal cushion to defend when the teams meet again in Algeria on Friday, 23 October.

The result also gives the Nigerian side an opportunity to build on their continental campaign after a difficult passage through the previous round.

Rangers advanced to the second preliminary round after overcoming AS Sobemap of Benin Republic on penalties. The tie ended 1-1 after both legs before the Enugu club won 5-4 in the shootout in Lomé.

MC Alger, meanwhile, reached this stage after defeating Nigerien side ASN Nigelec 5-0 on aggregate, following a goalless first leg.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Algerian club arrived in Nigeria as a formidable opponent, having won their domestic league title, but Rangers made home advantage count with their late double strike.

The two-goal margin gives the Nigerian side a useful advantage, although they must remain disciplined in the return leg to secure qualification for the group stage.

Rangers are among Nigeria’s most successful clubs, with nine league titles, including their latest triumph in 2026. They also won the African Cup Winners’ Cup in 1977, establishing a significant place in the country’s football history.

The Flying Antelopes will now turn their attention to the return fixture in Algeria, where they must protect their lead against an MC Alger side seeking to overturn the deficit.

Victory over the two legs would secure Rangers a place in the CAF Champions League group stage and bring them closer to competing among the continent’s leading clubs.

World.title: 2027: Uba Sani targets 3 million votes in Kaduna as top El-Rufai allies defect to APC
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani has announced a target of three million votes for the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections, following the defection of former Kaduna State Commissioner of Finance, Muhammad Bashir Sa’idu, and other prominent politicians from the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

Mr Sani announced the target on Saturday at a ceremony in Zaria to receive Mr Sa’idu and other defectors into the APC.

Mr Sa’idu, a former Chief of Staff and Commissioner for Finance under ex-Governor Nasir El-Rufai, claimed that more than 200,000 ADC members and supporters had joined the APC through his political group, Kaduna De-Initiatives.

Other prominent defectors include Jafaru Sani, a former commissioner for education under Mr El-Rufai and an ADC governorship aspirant, and former Senator Suleiman Abdu Kwari, who also served as commissioner of finance during the former governor’s administration.

The defections mark a significant political realignment in Kaduna ahead of the 2027 elections, particularly as several figures associated with Mr El-Rufai’s administration move to the party led by his successor.

Uba Sani raises APC’s vote target to three million

Speaking at the ceremony, Mr Sani said the APC had raised its target in Kaduna State from two million to three million votes, citing the growing number of supporters joining the party.

He said the state has 4.6 million registered voters, claiming 96 per cent have collected their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Before now, we were promising to deliver two million votes, but we have now upgraded to three million votes, God willing. There are 4,600,000 registered voters in Kaduna State and 96% have received their voter cards,” he said.

The governor said the APC would intensify grassroots mobilisation, including door-to-door campaigns, to canvass support across the state.

“We will go to every nook and cranny of Kaduna State, go house-to-house to canvass for votes, to ensure victory for APC from top to bottom,” he said.

Mr Sani also linked the party’s electoral ambitions to the federal government’s projects and political appointments in Kaduna State, including the emergence of Tajudeen Abbas as Speaker of the House of Representatives.

“The president loves Kaduna because he has sited many projects in our dear State, he has given many citizens of the state political appointments, and so we should reciprocate by voting massively for APC in all elections,” he said.

He described Mr Sa’idu as a principled and trustworthy politician, saying he had anticipated his return to the APC.

“The decampee is a man of the people, and even when he went to ADC, we were confident that he would return home. He stands for justice. Malam Jafaru Sani is also someone who can be trusted. He is also a seasoned public servant,” Mr Sani said.

The governor further insisted that the APC offered equal opportunities to members, regardless of when they joined the party.

“I, as the Governor, House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas, the North West zonal Vice Chairman, Hon Garba Datti Babawo and all of us, none is more important than the other in our party. We are all equal, and everyone has the right to aspire to any position that he wants,” he said.

Sa’idu declares ADC dead in Kaduna

Mr Sa’idu said the ADC had lost political relevance in Kaduna after his group and other supporters left.

He said the Kaduna De-Initiatives had built the party’s structures from the ward to the state level but became dissatisfied with its leadership and candidate selection process.

“We discovered that the party was being teleguided by a family, a situation which we found unacceptable. So, we studied the situation and compared the list of ADC candidates who won the primaries with the APC candidates.

“We saw that there was no basis for comparison; the contrast between the ADC and APC candidates is very glaring,” he said.

Mr Sa’idu said the group subsequently convened an emergency steering committee meeting and resolved to return to the APC.

“So, we have returned home. And as of one month ago, about 100,000 of those who defected with us have returned. These were card-carrying members of ADC. Between then and now, over 100,000 defectors have also joined APC,” he said.

He claimed that no credible opposition remained in Kaduna State following the defections.

“The former Commissioner of Finance said that there is not a single bona fide politician remaining in ADC, adding that there is now no opposition in Kaduna State, following their defection because ‘we were the opposition’.”

He also predicted that the ADC would finish third in the state when the 2027 election results were announced.

Why Sa’idu and other El-Rufai allies left the ADC

The defections followed disagreements over the ADC’s governorship primary, in which Isah Ashiru emerged as the party’s candidate for the 2027 election.

Mr Ashiru secured 86,113 votes, while Mr Sani, who also contested the primary, came second with 29,580 votes. Mr Sani rejected the outcome, alleging irregularities.

Mr Sa’idu said his group grew dissatisfied with what it described as a small group’s influence over the party’s affairs and the quality of candidates produced during the primaries.

The dispute deepened divisions among politicians who had previously aligned with Mr El-Rufai and later joined ADC.

Mr Sa’idu, Mr Sani and Mr Kwari’s return to the APC has now brought several former associates of the ex-governor into the political camp of Mr Sani, who succeeded him in 2023.

From El-Rufai’s government to APC: Former allies change political camps

Mr Sa’idu’s defection is particularly significant given his previous position in Mr El-Rufai’s administration, where he served as Chief of Staff and Commissioner for Finance.

Mr Kwari also held the finance portfolio under the former governor, while Mr Jafaru Sani served as commissioner for education.

Their move to APC marks another shift in the political allegiances of figures who held prominent positions during Mr El-Rufai’s eight-year administration.

El-Rufai reflects on friends who abandoned him

Earlier, in a statement titled “My Relationships and the Aftermath,” Mr El-Rufai reflected on relationships with former colleagues, friends and associates, saying adversity had revealed the nature of some relationships.

Although he did not name specific individuals, his remarks came amid political realignments involving people who had served in his administration or worked closely with him.

“Over the years, I have stood by people and for causes I believed in, sometimes in difficult circumstances and at considerable personal cost. I did so not in expectation of praise, gratitude or reciprocity, but because I believed it was right,” he wrote.

Mr El-Rufai said he did not regret supporting people or causes he believed in, even though some might not reciprocate when circumstances changed.

“I have no regrets about standing by people or for causes when I believed it was right to do so, and I bear no resentment towards anyone who chooses not to do the same for me,” he said.

His continued detention amid legal proceedings has coincided with the political repositioning of several former associates, including those who have now joined Mr Sani’s APC.

It remains to be seen how much the defections will affect the political balance in Kaduna State as parties prepare for the 2027 elections.

World.title: 2027: Opposition coalition too late to stop APC – Senator Plang
World.content:
By Golok Nanmwa

JOS – Senator Diket Plang, representing Plateau Central Senatorial District, has described the opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections as a belated move, arguing that a stronger alliance should have been formed before political parties conducted their primaries and produced candidates.

Plang expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) would win the majority of elective positions in Plateau State in 2027, while backing President Bola Tinubu for a second term.

“I am deeply convinced that APC will win the majority of the seats, whether in the governorship election, the National Assembly election or the State House of Assembly election,” he said.

On the opposition coalition, the senator said its formation came too late to achieve the desired political impact, noting that the parties had already produced their candidates before the alliance emerged.

“They came very late. They came only when candidates of the parties had already emerged. If they had wanted a good coalition, it could have been formed before the parties produced their candidates.”

“So, it is more of a merger of convenience than a holistic coalition,” he said.

On concerns about President Tinubu’s ability to campaign across the country ahead of the elections, Plang argued that effective campaigning did not necessarily require a candidate to visit every community or polling unit personally.

“What is the meaning of going round? Is it going round the states, local governments, wards or polling units?”

“Anybody who claims the capacity to go round the country should tell us whether he will visit every polling unit. I am waiting to see a presidential candidate who will go round all the polling units,” he said.

According to him, “political parties could reach voters through organised campaign structures capable of communicating their programmes at different levels.”

“If you have a campaign team that can take your message to the people, explain your manifesto and tell them what you intend to do, that is also a way of reaching the electorate.”

“The message moves from the national level to the geopolitical zones, states, local governments and wards before eventually getting to individual voters,” he said.

On insecurity, Plang described it as a major concern for Nigerians and cited the establishment of additional military formations as one of the measures he considered important in tackling the challenge.

“At a time like this, you all know that what is foremost in the minds of Nigerians is security.”

“If you find a president who is willing to expand the security forces, improve their salaries reasonably and establish more military formations, including companies, battalions and divisions, you have to consider what that means for the country,” he said.

Speaking specifically about Plateau State, the senator said the establishment of additional military formations in parts of the state could strengthen efforts to address insecurity.

“On the Plateau, it is unprecedented that we have additional battalions in Mangu, Barkin Ladi and Wase, with another one in Langtang.”

“If you wake up tomorrow and find that the President is willing to establish permanent military bases in Mangu and Barkin Ladi, it gives hope that something is being done to address insecurity,” he said.

Plang added that improved welfare for security personnel and the expansion of military formations were necessary to strengthen the country’s response to security threats.

“There is an intentional decision by this President to give priority to security and address the high level of insecurity in the country.”

“For me, we need to give him another opportunity to concentrate on the reforms and efforts he has started in tackling insecurity,” he said.

On infrastructure, the senator, who is a member of the Senate Committee on Works, praised projects embarked upon by the Federal Government, saying his position had enabled him to visit several road projects across the country.

Citing the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Plang said the scale of the project had initially appeared difficult to achieve.

“Honestly, when we went for the flag-off, I saw what looked like an impossibility. When they talked about reclaiming parts of the ocean and constructing drainages around the lagoons to create the road, I thought it was a dream.”

“But I later had the opportunity to attend the commissioning of the first phase of the road. I have seen the project practically, and I can tell you that the reality is different from what many people imagined,” he said.

The senator also cited work on the Akwanga-Keffi road corridor, describing the Federal Government’s infrastructure programme as an investment in the country’s future.

“If you look at the infrastructure projects the President has embarked upon, you will see that they are futuristic and offer hope for economic development.”

“If you have somebody with the courage and determination to undertake such projects, I do not think it is wise to gamble with another trial when we have already seen the direction we are going,” he said.

Plang urged Nigerians to assess political promises against actual performance, cautioning against abandoning tangible progress for an untested alternative.”

World.title: Police arrest suspected cultist over murder in Imo
World.content:
By Emmanuel Iheaka

OWERRI — The Imo State Police Command has arrested a 22-year-old man, Bright Adiene, over the suspected cult-related murder of Okeke Nnamdi in Owerri.

The command said efforts were ongoing to arrest another suspect, identified as Anyima, in connection with the incident reported on October 17, 2026.

The police spokesperson, DSP Henry Okoye, disclosed this in a statement, adding that investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing and identify all those involved.

Following the incident, the Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Garba Bosso, on Sunday convened a strategic security meeting with area commanders, divisional police officers and tactical team commanders to assess the security situation and strengthen operations across the state.

According to the statement, the meeting resulted in directives to operational commanders to intensify intelligence-led operations, conduct targeted raids on identified criminal hideouts, strengthen patrols in security hotspots and respond promptly to emerging threats.

The commissioner also directed closer collaboration with community leaders, youth groups and other stakeholders to improve intelligence gathering and prevent further violence.

Bosso urged parents and guardians to monitor their children’s activities and associations and discourage them from engaging in cultism.

He also called on members of the public to promptly report relevant information to security agencies, warning that anyone found culpable in cult-related violence would face the full consequences of the law.

The police said the arrested suspect remained in custody as investigations continued and efforts to apprehend the other suspect intensified.

World.title: Presidency denies withholding ₦250bn NLNG dividends from states
World.content:
The Presidency has dismissed Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s claim that the Federal Government is withholding ₦250 billion in Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG) dividends for each state until after the 2027 general elections.

Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, described the claim as false, arguing that the amount cited by the governor was inconsistent with the historical dividend payments made by NLNG to the Federation Account.

In a statement issued on Sunday, Onanuga said distributing ₦250 billion to each of Nigeria’s 36 states would amount to ₦9 trillion, excluding the Federal Government, the Federal Capital Territory and the 774 local government areas.

He explained that, under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) revenue-sharing formula, states receive 26.72 per cent of distributable revenue from the Federation Account.

According to him, for the states’ share alone to reach ₦9 trillion, total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed ₦33.68 trillion, or approximately $25 billion, in a single declaration.

“NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout,” he said.

Onanuga added that NLNG had paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the Federation over the past 25 years, with less than $3 billion realised since President Bola Tinubu assumed office.

He argued that the figures contradicted Makinde’s claim that a single dividend payout of the magnitude alleged was being withheld by the Federal Government.

Makinde had raised the issue on Friday at the 2027 Budget Stakeholders’ Consultative Engagement held at the Olola Ogunlana Hall, International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan.

The governor alleged that each state was entitled to ₦250 billion from the NLNG dividend windfall but that the Federal Government had indicated the money would not be released until after the 2027 elections.

“Each state was supposed to get ₦250 billion. We had already identified projects that would expand Oyo State’s economy. But they have now said the money will not be paid until after the election. Is the election more important than the people of Nigeria?” Makinde said.

However, the Presidency accused the governor of making misleading claims and urged him to exercise restraint in his public statements as he pursues his presidential ambition.

Onanuga also criticised Makinde for previously describing the substantial financial allocations from the Federation Account to states, including Oyo, as “voodoo”.

He said the governor was free to pursue his political ambition but should avoid statements the Presidency considers false or misleading.

The presidential spokesman urged Nigerians to disregard Makinde’s claims, arguing that they could mislead the public and create unnecessary tension between citizens and the Federal Government.

World.title: 2027: Tinubu, Nwifuru will win 95% votes in Ebonyi – Umahi
World.content:
Minister of Works, David Umahi

…says opposition candidates are jokers

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

Minister of Works, Sen David Umahi and Deputy Director General, Infrastructure, Mobilization and Sensitization of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu (PBAT)) /APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) has said that the President and Governor Francis Nwifuru will win Ebonyi State convincingly with 95% votes in 2027 general elections.

He stated this on Sunday in Abakaliki, the state capital during South East sensitization campaign for Ebonyi North and Central zones, described oppositional political parties candidates as jokers who will fail in their areas.

He declared the state as APC and vowed that the Tinubu and Nwifuru will win overwhelming during the general election.

Umahi, a former Governor and former Deputy Governor of the state, said the the Governor and APC have many wealthy persons that will bring their resources to support the general election for the party.

“President Bola Tinubu is going to win second tenure. Governor Francis Nwifuru is going to win second tenure.

“Anyone that does not wish Tinubu and Nwifuru second tenures, may he not have second tenure in his life.

“The style of our campaign this time, is going to be very dynamic. We will knock to our fathers and mothers at 6am and deliver our campaign messages to them.

“Ebonyi is completely APC. I have said it that Governor Nwifuru has friends and Ebonyi people who are very rich. We have a lot of Ebonyi youths, Ebonyi elders, Ebonyi women that will bring money to support the government of APC.. Nothing to fear about.

“We will defend President Tinubu, we will defend Governor Nwifuru, we will defend the lion of South East myself.

“We have said that Ebonyi State is totally for President Bola in Ahmed and we shall tackle anybody insults him. Ebonyi State is benefiting from his administration and we have to appreciate and support him.

“We are not looking for 80% win, we are looking to win 95% of our polling units and we will go for it, we will campaign for it and we will educate our people for it”, he said.

He described those who he said are boasting to win the state in the 2027 general election as jokers.

It is very unthinkable that somebody will sit down and think that this Minister will lose his Governor to another person.

“We are supporting President Bola Tinubu, we are supporting the Governor, we are supporting the Minister of Works and we are supporting all APC candidates.

“We are going to be strategic, we are going to be wiser. The project President Bola Tinubu is doing for us, I don’t know any other President that will do it for us; from Ndibe beach to Onueke and the most beautiful flyover in South East, and from there to Ukwuachi, from there to Ishieke and down to our border with Benue State

“The project is continuing through Ardo Local Government Area in Benue and it enters into Benue again, from Benue, it goes into Enugu, it comes out from Enugu and goes into Benue again, enters Kogi State and the second section is in Nassarawa, Owete bridge.

“What this means is that anywhere you are in Ebonyi State from Afikpo and otter parts of South East, you can get to Abuja within three hours. There is nothing that is greater than that. We are working very hard to complete Oferekpe road and complete the bridge so that you can link our brothers in South East”, the Minister stated.

The traditional ruler Nkaliki Unuhu Achara, Eze Sunday Oketa, assured that the state will deliver all the APC candidates for the 2027 general election.

World.title: Madueke strikes late as Arsenal squeeze out 1-0 win over Forest
World.content:
Arsenal’s English midfielder #20 Noni Madueke scores the team’s first goal during the English Premier League football match between Nottingham Forest and Arsenal at The City Ground in Nottingham, central England, on October 18, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services.
