An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Noni Madueke’s late goal sealed Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday as the champions survived a scrappy display to close the gap on Premier League leaders Manchester City.

Mikel Arteta’s side were well below their best at the City Ground and did not register a shot on target until Madueke bagged their winner 10 minutes from full-time.

While the Gunners earned few style points in the east midlands, they will not be overly concerned after moving with three points of table-toppers City, who beat Ipswich 3-2 on Saturday.

After a shock 3-0 loss at Brighton on September 19, second-placed Arsenal have bounced back with three successive victories.

They beat Leeds in the Premier League and Lille in the Champions League before their hard-fought success by the banks of the River Trent.

The north Londoners have not been able to recapture the relentless consistency that took them to a first title in 22 years last season.

But they retain the priceless ability to grind out wins and this was their sixth in seven league matches.

Arsenal head to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday before hosting Everton in the top flight next weekend.

Third-from-bottom Forest have won just twice at home in their last 17 League games, while boss Oliver Glasner has managed only one victory in seven top-flight matches since taking charge in the close season.

– Arsenal leave it late –

Bukayo Saka’s cross forced Forest goalkeeper Matz Sels to claw the ball from under his crossbar, but Arsenal struggled to establish any rhythm in a scrappy opening.

Forest’s Dan Ndoye tested Arsenal keeper David Raya after drifting in at the far post.

In a rare threat from Arteta’s men, Kai Havertz fired into the side-netting from an acute angle after Martin Odegaard’s pass opened up the Forest defence.

Arteta looked increasingly frustrated on the touchline as a turgid half petered out.

Eberechi Eze paid the price for Arsenal’s lethargy as the England forward was replaced by Madueke at the interval.

There was no immediate improvement from Arsenal despite that change and Forest striker Liam Delap drilled just wide after a rampaging run.

Arsenal were too slow in possession and lacked penetration when they went forward, so Arteta introduced Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Jurrien Timber in a bid to spark them into life.

Bruno Guimaraes was one of the Arsenal players sacrified after another underwhelming display from the Brazil midfielder in only his second league start since his summer move from Newcastle.

Gabriel Magalhaes headed over from a Declan Rice corner, while Delap could not muster the accuracy to beat Raya from Xaver Schlager’s pass.

Odegaard picked out Timber’s run and the defender teed up Declan Rice inside the Forest area, but his wasteful shot ballooned over, encapsulating the visitors’ impotence.

It was the first time since 2023 that Arsenal had failed to have a shot on target in the first 70 minutes of a Premier League match.

But they finally made the breakthrough in the 80th minute as Madueke cut in from the left flank and unleashed a powerful drive that took a hefty deflection off Forest’s Jair Cunha as it flashed past Sels.

Murillo was inches away from snatching a late leveller for Forest as the defender’s rocket whistled over.

World.title: Tinubu has turned middle class into beggars – Peter Ameh
World.content:
Peter-Ameh



John Alechenu, Abuja



Former Chairman of the Inter-Party Advisory Council, IPAC, Peter Ameh, has said the Tinubu administration has turned almost the entire Nigerian middle class into “old takers and beggars” through poorly conceived and anti-people policies.

Ameh was reacting to a new United Nations report which revealed that 17.9 million Nigerians have been plunged into multidimensional poverty in the last three years -the largest surge recorded anywhere in the world.

He spoke to Vanguard in Abuja, on Sunday.

According to the UN report, the surge goes beyond low income to include deprivations in health, education, housing, clean water and basic living standards.

“This is a case of a poorly conceived vision backed by poorly implemented, anti-people policies. This government has failed woefully to deliver on any of the promises it made to Nigerians,” Ameh said.

He said the figures confirm what ordinary Nigerians experience daily, where fuel subsidy removal without adequate palliatives, double-digit inflation, naira devaluation and high cost of living have eroded savings and collapsed small businesses.

“Under the Tinubu government, almost the entire middle class has been turned into old takers and beggars. People who were once self-sufficient can no longer afford school fees, hospital bills or even two decent meals a day,” he said.

Ameh warned that multidimensional poverty is more dangerous than income poverty because it strips people of dignity and future opportunities.

He called on the Federal Government to urgently review its economic reforms and adopt pro-people measures that create jobs, stabilise prices and protect vulnerable households, warning that the country risks creating a permanent underclass if the trend continues. End.

World.title: FG disagrees with World Bank over H1 124% debt servicing/revenue ratio
World.content:
Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Federal Government has disagreed with the World Bank on the latter’s debt servicing/revenue ratio for the first half of 2026, put at 124 percent.

The bank in its recent Nigeria Development Update (NDU) reported that federal government debt servicing was 124 percent above its revenue.

However, the Federal Ministry of Finance, in a statement, yesterday, faulted the bank’s analysis, explaining that the debt servicing figure included those of the state governments and that it was, therefore, wrong to analyse it against the federal government revenue for the period under consideration.

The statement read in part, “This conclusion is misleading, for three reasons, the government said.

“The interest figure includes debt the Federal Government services on behalf of other tiers of government, including external loans to states.

“Measuring this against federal revenue alone overstates the ratio which is only meaningful when debt and revenue cover the same level of government.

“The reported revenue is also incomplete. It excludes independent revenue already earned by government agencies and enterprises but not yet remitted to the Treasury.

” In addition, more revenue is typically earned in the second half of the year than in the first due to the statutory timing of certain tax payments. This is why the ratio stood at 156% in H1 2025, while the full-year 2025 debt-service-to-revenue ratio was below 60%, down from 97% before the reforms.

” This is a clear sign of the progress delivered by the current administration’s reforms.

“Between the first half of 2025 and the first half of 2026, federal revenue rose by 72%, from ₦3.6 trillion to ₦6.2 trillion. Interest payments rose by a much slower 38%, from ₦5.6 trillion to ₦7.7 trillion.

” Revenue is therefore growing almost twice as fast as interest costs. As a result, the interest-to-revenue ratio fell by 32 percentage points in a single year, from 156% to 124%, and the gap between interest and revenue narrowed from ₦2.0 trillion to ₦1.5 trillion. This is the result of reforms working, not a sign of fiscal distress.

“Debt sustainability is assessed on a full-year basis, not over six months. The same World Bank report projects Nigeria’s full-year 2026 debt service, covering both interest and principal, at 46% of revenue.

“This is the appropriate benchmark, and a guide to avoid the invalid conclusions being drawn.

“Every naira borrowed by the Federal Government falls within the limits approved by the National Assembly under the 2026 Appropriation Act and the approved borrowing plan.

“All borrowing is conducted in full compliance with the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 and the Debt Management Office (Establishment) Act 2003, and is published regularly by the Debt Management Office.

“The Ministry welcomes informed scrutiny of public finances. We encourage analysts and commentators to apply the same rigour they seek to hold the government to: compare like with like, read figures in context, and seek clarification where the data is unclear.”

World.title: Atiku tackles Tinubu over Police Exit Bill
World.content:
Collage of Atiku Abubakar and Bola Tinubu

…says serving officers dip into pensions

By Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to explain his delay in acting on the Police Exit Bill, alleging that serving police officers are dipping into their pension savings to feed their families while retired personnel struggle to survive on meagre stipends.

Atiku said the plight of serving and retired officers demanded urgent action on police welfare, including a salary review and resolution of the pension concerns raised by retirees, following the pay increase approved for members of the Armed Forces.

In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council, ADC-PCC, on October 18, Atiku recounted cases of retired officers allegedly living on inadequate pensions, searching for menial jobs and begging for alms after decades of service.

“Men and women who answered Nigeria’s call for decades are now waiting outside its legislature for Nigeria to answer theirs. Bola Tinubu should be ashamed that it has come to this,” he said.

Atiku cited the case of a retired Assistant Superintendent of Police who allegedly receives a monthly pension of ₦29,000 and told him that more than 120 members of his association had died in the past three years.

He also recounted how a retired Assistant Commissioner of Police allegedly resorted to begging at the Central Mosque in Abuja after failing to find work.

“No former officer should have to be discovered in distress before Nigeria remembers what it owes her,” Atiku said.

In another account, he said a retired officer in Bauchi had resorted to gathering firewood for sale to afford food, while some serving policemen had allegedly withdrawn 25 per cent of their pension savings to meet their families’ needs.

“We ask them to risk their lives for Nigeria while they wonder how to feed their families and whether their country will stand by them when their service ends. That is a disgrace,” he said.

Turning to the Police Exit Bill, Atiku said the legislation was sent to Tinubu in March but that the President had yet to make his position known as of October.

Citing Section 58 of the Constitution, he said the President had a 30-day period to signify assent or withhold it from a bill presented for assent, and demanded an explanation for the delay.

“Bola, a bill gathering dust cannot buy food or medicine. Tell Nigerians what you have done with it,” he said.

Atiku urged the National Assembly to publish the bill’s formal status, demand an explanation for the delay and determine the constitutional steps available to resolve the matter.

He also pledged that, if elected president in 2027, he would introduce a Police Dignity Guarantee Plan to settle verified pension arrears and gratuity claims, establish a pension floor, provide healthcare coverage for serving and retired officers, and ensure timely support for families of personnel killed in service.

The proposed plan, he said, would also include a police salary review, clearer records of pension contributions and entitlements, and published payment schedules to improve accountability.

“We will provide for the Guarantee in the budget and publish what has been paid,” he said.

World.title: DSS Arrests: Why Intelligence Must Drive Nigeria’s Fight Against Insecurity
World.content:
By Olufemi Lawson

The recent arrest of five suspected kidnappers linked to the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members, alongside the arrest of fugitive Faisal Maina, represents a significant achievement by the Department of State Services (DSS) and a welcome development in Nigeria’s fight against insecurity.

Beyond the arrests themselves, these operations reinforce the importance of intelligence gathering, strategic surveillance and coordinated security operations in confronting terrorism, kidnapping and other organised crimes threatening the country.

The rescue of the abducted prospective corps members and the subsequent arrest of five suspects demonstrate the value of sustained intelligence work beyond the immediate scene of a crime. Similarly, the reported arrest of Faisal Maina, who had been on the run since 2020, underscores the importance of intelligence in tracking fugitives and ensuring that nobody remains permanently beyond the reach of the law.

As I argued during a television interview yesterday, Nigeria must invest significantly more in intelligence if the country is to achieve lasting success in its war against terrorism, kidnapping, banditry and other criminal activities.

While military operations, weapons and personnel remain important, security cannot be sustained through force alone. Intelligence enables security agencies to identify criminal networks, anticipate attacks, track perpetrators and dismantle their operational structures before they inflict further damage.

Intelligence must therefore become the backbone of Nigeria’s national security strategy.

The Federal Government must prioritise modern intelligence technology, digital forensics, personnel training, secure communication systems and improved operational logistics. Investing in prevention through intelligence is ultimately more effective and less costly than continually responding to attacks after lives and property have beecommend

I particularly commend Mr. Adeola Oluwatosin the Director-General of the DSS for the renewed emphasis on the service’s traditional national security responsibilities, especially intelligence gathering, threat assessment and the prevention of threats to national security.

In my assessment, this renewed direction represents a welcome departure from what critics had perceived in previous periods as a diversion towards unconventional approaches that risked overshadowing the service’s core intelligence mandate.

The DSS occupies a critical position in Nigeria’s security architecture, and its effectiveness should be measured by its capacity to uncover threats, disrupt criminal networks and provide actionable intelligence that protects lives and national interests.

The latest arrests demonstrate the practical value of a focused intelligence service. I salute the Director-General for his leadership and, more importantly, the officers and men of the DSS whose vigilance, professionalism and dedication contributed to these successes.

However, the remaining suspects linked to the NYSC abduction must be tracked down, and all those found culpable must face the law.

The successes also raised the need for greater synergy among the DSS, the military, the police, the EFCC and other relevant security and law-enforcement agencies.

Criminal networks exploit gaps in coordination and information sharing. A more integrated security system, supported by joint intelligence operations and timely exchange of credible information, would significantly improve the country’s ability to prevent attacks and apprehend offenders.

The Federal Government must also increase funding and operational support for the DSS to strengthen its technological capacity, personnel welfare, intelligence infrastructure and field operations.

Adequate funding, accompanied by accountability and effective oversight, will enable the service to respond more effectively to evolving security threats.

The arrest of the suspected kidnappers and Faisal Maina sends a strong message that intelligence-led operations can deliver tangible results. Nevertheless, the ultimate measure of success must be the prevention of future crimes, the dismantling of criminal networks and the restoration of public confidence.

I urge the Federal Government to sustain its support for the DSS and other security agencies while ensuring that investigations and prosecutions are conducted in accordance with the law.

Nigeria cannot afford to treat intelligence as a secondary component of national security. It must be recognised as a strategic national investment.

I once again salute the Director-General and the officers and men of the DSS for their latest achievements. Their efforts deserve commendation and sustained institutional support.

With stronger intelligence capabilities, improved inter-agency cooperation and adequate funding, Nigeria can make meaningful progress towards defeating terrorism, kidnapping and organised crime.

*Comrade Olufemi Lawson, National Secretary of the Campaign for Democracy (CD), writes from Lagos.

World.title: Troops Disrupt Illegal Arms-Trafficking Network in North-central, Arrest One Over Alleged Kidnapping, Sexual Assault
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian military has said that troops of the Joint Task Force, North-Central Operation Enduring Peace, have uncovered, tracked and disrupted an illegal arms-trafficking network in the North-central region, particularly in Plateau State. The troops also dismantled kidnapping networks in the state.

The Director of Defence Media Operations, Major General Michael Onoja, made this known during his weekly update on the operational activities of troops of the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) across the country.

He also revealed that troops of the Joint Task Force, North-West Operation Fansan Yamma, apprehended a suspect identified as Yusuf Iliya Sani at Maraban Kakini over his alleged involvement in kidnapping, extortion, sexual assault and killings in Birnin Gwari Local Government Area (LGA) of Kaduna State.

He said: “Troops of Operation Enduring Peace maintained operations to disrupt illegal arms trafficking, identify suspected perpetrators of violent crime and dismantle kidnapping networks in Plateau State.

“To this end, troops conducted a covert operation in Mangu and Barkin Ladi LGAs of Plateau State and arrested a suspected arms fabricator at Heipang, Barkin Ladi LGA. Three other suspects were also arrested over their alleged involvement in illegal arms trafficking. Troops recovered one locally fabricated revolver rifle, one fabricated pistol, one fabricated AK-47 barrel, one AK-47 magazine and 42 rounds of 7.62mm × 54mm rimmed ammunition.

“On 10 October 2026, troops arrested a suspect, Yusuf Suleiman, at Barkin Ladi Main Market. He was allegedly linked to the attack on Kassa community on 24 September 2026, as well as kidnapping, armed robbery and the killing of a resident, Mr Gyang, on 16 April 2026.

“Also, on 14 October 2026, troops raided a suspected kidnappers’ hideout at Ruga in Methodist Kisahyip, Agingin, Bassa LGA of Plateau State, and arrested two suspects.”

Recounting the operational activities of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma on 9 October 2026, General Onoja said troops operating around the Galadimawa area sighted three suspected terrorists fleeing with a kidnapped person.

He further explained: “Troops engaged the suspects and forced them to abandon the victim.

“On 10 October, troops responded to reports that a local resident travelling from Dogon Dawa to Takama Village in Birnin Gwari LGA of Kaduna State was under attack by an unknown armed group. On arrival, the responding troops engaged the assailants and recovered an AK-47 rifle with 15 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition.

“Following continued tracking and monitoring, troops apprehended a suspect identified as Yusuf Iliya Sani at Maraban Kakini on 10 October 2026 over his alleged involvement in kidnapping, extortion, sexual assault and killings in Birnin Gwari LGA of Kaduna State.”

Onoja said the operations conducted across all operational theatres had sustained the AFN’s efforts to ensure a safe and secure environment and restore security across the country.

The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, commended the resilience of all security personnel, urging them to maintain operational momentum, remain highly vigilant and deny criminal elements any freedom of action.

The Defence Chief also called on all security agencies to strengthen their collaborative intelligence-sharing frameworks to enhance operations against criminal elements across the country.

He said national security was a collective civic responsibility, adding that through unwavering unity and resolve, the military would secure a peaceful and prosperous future for Nigeria.

World.title: Peter Obi Media Office Faults Shettima Over ‘Diminished Obi’ Remark
World.content:
* Says political leaders should debate records, policies not personal attacks

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Peter Obi Media Office has criticised Vice-President Kashim Shettima over his description of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, as “diminished,” urging political leaders to focus on candidates’ records, policies and ideas rather than personal attacks.

In a statement issued Sunday by its spokesman, Idris Zekeri Jnr, the media office described the remark as inconsistent with the standards of political engagement expected of leaders, particularly at a time when political parties are positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 general election.

The office took exception to what it considered a contrast between Shettima’s call for northerners to respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, an opposition figure, and his description of Obi, another opposition leader.

“Although Shettima has the right to oppose Obi, it is difficult to understand why he would demand respect for one opposition leader while casually dismissing another,” the statement said.

It added that political disagreements should not prevent public officials from recognising the contributions and political standing of their opponents.

The media office said Obi had maintained a campaign focused on issues and had avoided abusive language against political opponents.

“As a man of great decency, our candidate has conducted his campaign professionally and decorously. He has consistently focused his remarks on issues and has neither discussed nor used abusive language against anyone,” it said.

The statement also drew attention to the records of Obi and Shettima as former governors of Anambra and Borno States, respectively, arguing that their respective performances should be assessed against verifiable evidence rather than political rhetoric.

“However, Obi’s performance in Anambra State across key areas of governance surpassed Shettima’s record in Borno State, as demonstrated by performance statistics and the awards he received,” the office said.

It cited Obi’s record in fiscal management and investments in education and healthcare as areas that, in its view, distinguished his administration.

The office, however, did not provide comparative statistics in the statement to substantiate its assessment of the two former governors’ performances.

It challenged the vice-president and other political opponents to interrogate Obi’s record using verifiable facts and figures if they disagreed with the assessment.

“If Shettima contests any aspect of Obi’s record, he should present the facts rather than resort to political name-calling,” the statement added.

The media office said the controversy raised broader questions about political civility, the treatment of opposition figures and the responsibility of public officials to sustain issue-based debate in Nigeria’s democratic process.

It also appealed to political leaders from the South-east, including those in the All Progressives Congress (APC), to distinguish political loyalty from their responsibility to uphold mutual respect among political actors.

The statement urged South-east political leaders who support the APC to reflect on the implications of the exchange, particularly where they believe that criticism of an opposition politician from their region is inconsistent with the treatment accorded other political figures.

It said disagreements over party affiliation should not become grounds for tolerating what it considers disrespectful language against fellow Nigerians.

“We urge Igbo leaders in the APC and all Nigerians to draw the appropriate lesson from this episode and note that political loyalty must never justify tolerating disrespect towards a fellow Nigerian,” the statement said.

The office maintained that political competition should provide an opportunity for candidates and their supporters to examine competing records, policy proposals and governing philosophies.

“Those who oppose Obi should scrutinise his ideas and record rather than resort to personal abuse,” it said.

“Nigeria needs a contest based on records and ideas, not selective respect and political denigration.”

The media office further argued that Obi’s political relevance should ultimately be determined by voters rather than by comments from political opponents.

“The Nigerian people, rather than Shettima’s rhetoric, will determine Peter Obi’s political relevance,” it said.

The statement, dated October 18, 2026, was signed by Zekeri on behalf of the Peter Obi Media Office.

The development comes as political parties and their leading figures intensify their positioning ahead of the 2027 general election, with the conduct of political campaigns, the credibility of candidates and the tone of public debate expected to feature prominently in the contest.

While political leaders are entitled to criticise opponents and challenge their records in office, the exchange underscores the importance of substantiating political claims with evidence and maintaining a distinction between legitimate criticism and personal disparagement.

For the NDC presidential candidate and his supporters, the central argument is that Obi’s record as a former governor should be judged on its merits. For his political opponents, the challenge is to present competing evidence and policy alternatives capable of persuading voters.

Ultimately, the debate over the records of former governors and their suitability for national leadership is likely to remain part of the broader political contest as the 2027 election approaches.

World.title: 2027: Abia Youths Declare Support for Tinubu, Deputy Speaker Kalu, Plan One-Million-Man March in Aba
World.content:
A group of youths comprising artisans and Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) owners under the umbrella of “Great Aba Men” in Abia State has declared support for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu.

The declaration was made during a courtesy visit to the Deputy Speaker at his country home in Bende on Saturday.

Speaking on behalf of the group, its leader, Prince Okwudiri Uche, said Abia youths will give President Tinubu the highest number of votes in the South East in the 2027 presidential election.

He said: “From today, we have declared for Mr. President. We will support Mr. President and Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu. Asiwaju is the next President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“There is no way we will have the Deputy Speaker of this federation from Abia State, supported by Mr. President, and not return the President. It will not happen. Rt. Hon. Sir, we will make you proud because we will deliver President Tinubu. Abia youths will make it happen. He will go for a second term. Aba people will not let you down”.

The group, which congratulated the Deputy Speaker on his appointment as Director-General II (South) of the PBAT/APC Presidential Campaign Council, requested him to serve as its Grand Patron.

It also revealed plans to organize a one-million-man march for President Tinubu in Aba.

In his remarks, Kalu commended the group for declaring support for President Tinubu and himself.

He noted the President’s love for the people of the South East, particularly Abia State, stating that the President who supported a son of Abia to emerge as Deputy Speaker deserves to be repaid with gratitude.

“From today, you have become Mr. President’s foot soldiers and will take the message of Renewed Hope to every nook and cranny of Aba. I declare you the sons of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. We are starting a movement that will go beyond January 16, 2026,” Kalu said.

He promised to support the group with a campaign bus for the planned march, charging them to mobilize across the State and take the message of Renewed Hope Agenda to the hinterlands.

“Every street will come out to show that we are supporting President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. In Bende, the President will harvest all the votes because the Deputy Speaker is from this Local Government. So, go and put up your strategy. We will show that Great Aba Men are behind the President. We must make sure the President wins in Aba. I want you to be very visible in Aba and take over Aba. Let’s comb the city to announce our presence,” he said.

World.title: FG Tasks VCs to Prioritize High-demand Degree Programmes
World.content:
* Reaffirms commitment to establishing autism centres across six geopolitical zones



Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Federal Government has called on vice-chancellors of Nigerian universities to prioritise degree programmes that address critical manpower shortages, respond to emerging societal needs and equip graduates with specialised skills for professional practice and employment.

It said such programmes should include degrees in Audiology, Occupational Therapy, Speech and Language Therapy, Clinical Psychology and Medical Social Work, noting that expanding training in these fields would help bridge gaps in specialised healthcare and social services while creating more career opportunities for young Nigerians.

Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, also reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to establishing autism centres across the six geopolitical zones to improve access to specialised care and support for persons on the autism spectrum and their families.

Alausa stressed that universities must align their academic offerings with national workforce needs and the growing demand for specialised professional services.

He noted that developing these programmes would strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to provide essential services locally, reduce gaps in specialist care and build a skilled workforce capable of meeting the needs of the population.

The planned autism centres are expected to support access to diagnosis, therapeutic services and research, while serving as regional hubs for families, healthcare professionals and educational institutions.

The initiative reflects the Federal Government’s determination to strengthen local capacity and improve support for persons with autism and related developmental conditions.

The minister assured stakeholders that the Federal Government would continue to pursue reforms that expand access to relevant education, strengthen institutional capacity and promote skills development.

Alausa commended the Chairman of the Federal Government Committee for the Advancement of Audiology, Occupational Therapy and Speech and Language Therapy, Dr. Victoria Amu, for her passion and dedication to duty.

He called on vice-vhancellors and other university administrators to work closely with the Ministerial Committee Chairman, Dr. Victoria Amu, the relevant regulatory agencies and professional bodies to facilitate the development of the proposed programmes and ensure that training meets appropriate academic and professional standards.

The minister reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to building a responsive and inclusive higher education system that equips Nigerians with relevant skills, addresses critical manpower gaps and expands access to essential specialised services.

The initiatives form part of the administration’s broader efforts to strengthen human capital development, improve service delivery and ensure that Nigeria’s education system responds effectively to national priorities and the needs of its citizens.

World.title: Birmingham, UNILAG Bring UK Postgraduate Degrees Closer to Nigerians
World.content:
Iyke Bede

Nigerian students seeking internationally recognised postgraduate qualifications will have an opportunity to study programmes offered by a United Kingdom university without relocating abroad, following a new partnership between the University of Birmingham and the University of Lagos (UNILAG).

The universities have launched two one-year postgraduate programmes in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Technologies, and Digital Media and Communications, which will be delivered in Lagos from September 2027.

The initiative, developed under a Transnational Education (TNE) arrangement in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission, is designed to expand access to international higher education while developing skills relevant to Nigeria’s growing economy.

Speaking at the launch on Thursday, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, described the partnership as crucial to Nigeria’s tertiary education development.

“Our planned collaboration and partnership with the University of Birmingham is both timely and strategic at this critical phase of Nigeria’s tertiary education advancement. It is designed to consolidate and deepen the significant gains we have made in strengthening our university system, while expanding access to world-class, high-quality education anchored in global best practices,” he said.

The MSc in AI and Data Technologies will cover machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, large language models and AI ethics, preparing graduates for opportunities in fintech, healthcare innovation and business analytics.

The MA in Digital Media and Communications will focus on digital cultures, communication, power, identity and media ethics, while equipping students with research, content creation and broadcasting skills for careers in journalism and digital communications.

The Provost of the University of Birmingham, Professor Nick Vaughan-Williams, said the programmes would support Nigeria’s educational and workforce development needs.

“We’re proud to launch these programmes with our partners at UNILAG. Together we are supporting Nigeria’s tertiary education and talent needs, which are central to its ambitions for economic growth,” he said.

Echoing the emphasis on the partnership’s long-term value, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, Professor Folasade T. Ogunsola, said the collaboration reflected the university’s broader approach to international partnerships:

“The University of Lagos-University of Birmingham TNE collaboration reflects UNILAG’s broader vision of reimagining partnerships built on mutual respect, co-creation, and shared responsibility.”

The British Council Nigeria described the arrangement as a more affordable and accessible route for Nigerian students to obtain UK postgraduate qualifications without studying abroad.

World.title: Stretford Hill Advocates Durable, Safer Infrastructure at Sustainability Series
World.content:
Vanessa Obioha

Stretford Hill Limited has stressed the need to prioritise quality, safety and durability in infrastructure development, arguing that the value of construction goes beyond the structures delivered to the benefits they provide for people, businesses and communities.

The Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian construction and infrastructure company, Engr. Lakunle Runsewe, made this point as the company participated as a partner and exhibitor at the 10th Sustainability Table Series, held on October 15 and 16 at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos.

“The true value of infrastructure is not measured by what we build alone, but by what it makes possible for people, businesses and communities,” Runsewe said.

He added that infrastructure development required deliberate attention to planning, construction and maintenance, with safety and durability serving as priorities to ensure structures remained functional and secure over time.

The event, themed “Leading the Sustainable Development Agenda: People, Planet, and Prosperity,” brought together policymakers, business leaders and sustainability stakeholders to discuss approaches to sustainable development.

At its exhibition stand, Stretford Hill showcased its capabilities in building construction, civil and structural engineering, project management, interior fit-outs and furnishing, specialised architectural metal works, fabrication and facilities support.

The exhibition also provided an opportunity for the company to engage industry stakeholders, exchange ideas on the built environment and strengthen professional relationships.

The event underscored the importance of public-private sector collaboration in advancing sustainable development, particularly in the construction industry, where effective planning, technical expertise and adherence to quality and safety standards are essential throughout a project’s lifecycle.

Founded in 2013, Stretford Hill provides integrated construction and engineering services.

The company said its approach was guided by diligence, integrity, safety and excellence, with a commitment to delivering construction and infrastructure solutions that meet professional standards and serve the needs of businesses and communities.

World.title: Ibori Mourns Dele Cole, Hails His Contributions to Resource Control, True Federalism
World.content:
Former Delta State Governor, Chief James Ibori has mourned prominent Niger Delta leader, Patrick Dele Cole, praising his unwavering commitment to the struggle for true federalism and resource control.

Cole, who was born on August 4, 1940, in Abonnema, in the Kalabari Kingdom of present-day Rivers State, died in London at the age of 86.

In a statement issued on Sunday, titled “PDC: So Long My Leader,” Ibori described the late Cole as a steadfast advocate of the Niger Delta cause who remained loyal to his roots despite the political implications of his position.

He said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, noting that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a Special Adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo.

According to Ibori, Cole’s dedication to the region demonstrated his willingness to stand with his people at a time when doing so could attract considerable political costs.

Cole’s political choices, he added, were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people.

“He was a prominent leader in the Niger Delta who stood firmly with us in our struggle for True Federalism and Resource Control. Even while serving as a Special Adviser in President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, he remained committed to his people and their legitimate aspirations.

“His actions reflected deep loyalty to his roots and an unwavering commitment to the Niger Delta cause. At a time when such a stance could carry significant political costs, he chose to stand with his people,”

Ibori who enjoined the family of the late statesman to take solace in God, said his contributions to the development of Nigeria, especially the Niger Delta region will forever be cherished.

World.title: All grown up! Charlize steps out with two daughters [video]
World.content:
Charlize Theron and her two daughters Jackson and August. Images via IG

Charlize Theron and her two daughters turned heads at the Academy Museum Gala in Los Angeles on Saturday, 17 October.

The South-African born actress adopted Jackson (who now identifies as a girl) and August in 2012 and 2015, respectively.

CHARLIZE THERON AND TWO DAUGHTERS TURN HEADS AT EVENT

On Saturday, Charlize made an appearance at the Sixth Annual Academy Museum Gala in LA, where she received the Icon Award in celebration of her cinematic career.



While the blonde Benoni-born star walked the red carpet alone, she shared a sweet moment with her daughters, Jackson, 14, and August, 12.

Charlize and her model-like kids shared a warm embrace in a video captured by People magazine.

Both girls had their hair styled in long braids and wore black minidresses and strappy heels.

While they aren’t biologically related, it’s clear the girls inherited their style and grace from their South African mom.

WHY SHE CHOSE TO ADOPT

Over the years, Charlize Theron has spoken openly and honestly about her unconventional path to parenthood.



In an interview with Elle Magazine in 2018, the South African-born star revealed that she was intrigued with adoption from a young age.

She shared: “South Africa, orphanages were everywhere, and I wanted a brother or sister. I was always aware that there are so many children in this world who don’t have families. Adoption is a very personal thing – I know people whom I love dearly who don’t feel that they could raise another child as their own. I respect that.

“But for me -and I can’t be the only person out there- I never saw a difference in raising an adopted child versus my own biological child. I don’t feel like I’m missing out on something.

“This was always my first choice, even when I was in a relationship. I was very honest with my partners that I was open to having my own biological kids but that adoption had to be a part of my life. I felt that strongly about it”.

World.title: Monday tides: Check coastal times as damaging winds and waves loom
World.content:
Beachgoers are urged to check Monday’s tide times as damaging winds and waves threaten coastal activities in KwaZulu-Natal. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Monday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Damaging winds and waves along the KZN coast

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds and waves along the KwaZulu-Natal coastline.



These conditions could temporarily disrupt beachfront activities and operations at small harbours and ports until Tuesday morning.

Beachgoers, anglers and others planning coastal activities should follow the latest weather warnings and check local sea conditions before heading out.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.

The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Where to book affordable last-minute beach stays near Durban
World.content:
The most affordable December rentals are usually the ones booked first. The longer you wait, the more likely you are to pay more.

However, if you’re planning a last-minute escape this December, you can still book accommodation for a family of four near Durban.

These are the areas where that’s possible.

Affordable Escape in December Near Durban

You can get 5 nights for a family of four starting at R600 a night (or R150 per person) in December.



But since most of Durban’s beach accommodation has been booked for December, these are your next choices.

Amanzimtoti

Currently, Amanzimtoti is the closest city to Durban with available accommodation.

Amanzimtoti is a 25-minute drive south from Durban and gets quite busy in summer.



Currently, there are at least a dozen self-catering stays starting at R5 300 for 5 nights.

The average price is roughly R6 500 for a last-minute 5-night stay in Amanzimtoti. Ratings on these self-catering units start at 5.9.

Kingsburgh

Kingsburgh, which includes Warner Beach, is a 25-minute drive from Durban.



The town is slightly more expensive than Amanzimtoti, a 5-minute drive away.

For a 5-night stay, the average booking price is R7 700.

However, the stays have higher ratings. In neighbouring Amanzimtoti, some stays have extremely low ratings. But in Kingsburgh, the average rating is 7.9.



Scottsburgh

This is the perfect place to stay if you enjoy the beach and it is very family-friendly.

Scottsburgh is a 45-minute drive from Durban. It also has access to a Blue Flag beach.

You can visit tidal pools, swim and canoe in the lagoon, play putt-putt golf and ride a super tube.



The affordable accommodation in Scottsburgh is booking quickly; only a handful remain. But these self-catering units typically include ocean views.

The average booking price is R6 500, and the average rating is 8.7.

Port Shepstone

Roughly a 1-hour 20-minute drive from Durban without traffic, you’ll find Port Shepstone.



There’s plenty to do in Port Shepstone.

Kayak the Mzimkulu River or play golf at the Port Shepstone Golf Club.

Go hiking or explore the Oribi Gorge Nature Reserve.



Accommodation starts at R4 250 for a self-catering unit.

Hibberdene

Hibberdene is a smaller town over an hour from Durban.

The town is more laid-back, perfect for families who don’t want a full itinerary in December.



Instead, families can access some of the best beaches on the South Coast and activities in neighbouring Scottsburgh and Margate.

Accommodation in Hibberdene starts at R6 500 for a 5-night stay, but affordable stays are going quickly.

To save even more, stay in the surrounding small villages like Mtwalume, where units start at R4 500 for 5 nights.



Margate

Margate, which is about a 90-minute drive from Durban, currently has the most available accommodation.

Holidaymakers can book stays in Margate, Uvongo Beach, Shelly Beach, and Ramsgate.

Of the remaining holiday stays, a 5-night stay for a family of 4 starts at R5 150 in Margate.



In the less-crowded Uvongo Beach or Shelly Beach, prices start at R5 460.

World.title: Warning for WhatsApp users in South Africa
World.content:
WhatsApp users in South Africa are being warned about scammers taking over accounts and using them to trick friends, family members and colleagues into sending money. Image: Wikimedia Commons

WhatsApp users in South Africa are being warned about scammers taking over accounts and using them to trick friends, family members and colleagues into sending money.

Cybercriminals are using several methods to gain access to accounts, including SIM-swapping scams, fraudulent verification requests and malicious links.

Cybersecurity expert Boikokobetso Makhetlane explained that criminals can take control of a victim’s SIM card without their knowledge, a technique commonly known as SIM swapping.



How WhatsApp account takeovers happen

Makhetlane said scammers may send victims verification codes or call them while pretending to be representatives of a service provider.

They may claim there is suspicious activity involving the victim’s phone or SIM card and ask for additional information to verify their identity.

Once criminals gain access to an account, they can impersonate its owner and contact people in their address book to request money.

Friends, family members and work colleagues may believe the messages are genuine because they appear to come from someone they know.

Makhetlane also warned that sensitive information shared through WhatsApp could be exposed if an account is compromised.

This could include banking and credit card details, passwords, and residential addresses belonging to users or their contacts.



Warning signs to watch out for

One possible indication of a SIM-swap attack is a sudden loss of mobile network connectivity.

Another warning sign is a WhatsApp notification stating that the user’s phone number has been registered on another device.

Makhetlane urged users who notice these signs to contact their mobile network provider immediately to establish whether their SIM card or account has been compromised.

“If you do see that, immediately contact your network service provider as soon as possible to verify that everything is still intact because you need to double-check everything,” he said.

Users should also be cautious of unexpected links sent through messages, even when they appear to come from people they know.

Makhetlane noted that scammers increasingly use links as a way to gain access to WhatsApp accounts.

How to protect your WhatsApp account

WhatsApp users can take several steps to reduce the risk of their accounts being compromised.

These include:

Enable two-step verification: Add an extra layer of protection to your WhatsApp account by setting up a PIN.

Add an extra layer of protection to your WhatsApp account by setting up a PIN. Never share verification codes: Do not give one-time passwords or WhatsApp registration codes to anyone, even if they claim to represent a service provider.

Do not give one-time passwords or WhatsApp registration codes to anyone, even if they claim to represent a service provider. Check linked devices: Regularly review the devices connected to your account and log out of any you do not recognise.

Regularly review the devices connected to your account and log out of any you do not recognise. Be cautious of suspicious links: Avoid opening unexpected links, particularly those accompanied by urgent requests or unusual messages.

Avoid opening unexpected links, particularly those accompanied by urgent requests or unusual messages. Verify requests for money: If a friend or relative asks for money through WhatsApp, contact them directly through another channel before making a payment.

If a friend or relative asks for money through WhatsApp, contact them directly through another channel before making a payment. Contact your mobile network provider: If your phone suddenly loses network connectivity without explanation, check whether your SIM card has been compromised.

As scammers continue to exploit trusted relationships and personal information, users are being urged to strengthen their account security and remain alert to unusual activity.

A message that appears to come from a friend or family member may not be genuine, and verifying a request before sending money could prevent a costly scam.

Have you fallen victim to a WhatsApp scam?
