World.title: Entertainment: Kazadi gives The Pawn his blessing and tells Zambians to watch Mwamba’s film
World.content:
Filmmaker Mr David Kazadi urged Zambians to watch Mr Wyclif Mwamba’s new feature film, The Pawn, praising its storyline, cast and cinematography in a candid Facebook review that turned what social media had cast as a bitter feud into a public show of respect between two of the country’s best-known screen names.

Mr Kazadi said he absolutely loved the storyline and described Mr Mwamba as a phenomenal storyteller, calling that gift a core talent and creative strength nobody can take away from him.

“If you haven’t watched The Pawn yet, you definitely should check it out and support the vision,” he wrote.

The verdict landed barely a week after Mr Kazadi publicly took aim at the film’s troubled premiere, where more than 1,000 film lovers were left unable to watch the screening because of technical issues. In that earlier post, he criticised a culture in which local creators take on every role in a production themselves, and warned that one badly executed project damages the trust of audiences, sponsors and investors for everyone who follows.

“Leveraging someone else’s skills, knowledge, or expertise doesn’t make you weak, it makes you stronger,” he wrote at the time.

Many of his followers braced for a demolition job. What they got instead was a balanced, generous review from a producer who had clearly sat through the whole film and found plenty to like.

Mr Kazadi did not pretend the film was flawless. He said Mr Mwamba may not have the best interpersonal skills and lacks some exposure to certain technical and directing disciplines, but added that his passion for the project comes through clearly on screen, making it obvious why he was so determined to bring The Pawn to life.

On production, he pointed to areas common to most independent films. Dialogue could have been polished further, he said, and some on-set audio recording and volume transitions needed balancing to lift the viewing experience.

Those were small blemishes in his view. The sound glitches, he wrote, do not overshadow the film’s strengths. The cast delivered impressive performances, and several moments of striking cinematography caught his eye.

His warmest praise went to what Mr Mwamba has built beyond the film itself. Launching his own streaming platform, Capstone, was in Mr Kazadi’s words “a stroke of genius”, a smart, forward-thinking move for distribution and creative control in a country that usually suffers from exactly that problem.

He closed the review with a line written in capital letters for emphasis: “NOT ALL CRITIQUE IS SYNONYMOUS WITH HATE!”

The comment section quickly filled with surprise and approval. Mr Luckson Chilambwe Kalambulwa admitted he had expected Mr Kazadi to dismiss the film outright, and said the review showed the value of creatives building one another up.

Mr Tinozye Marvin Ndolo called it maturity at its highest, while Ms Nancy Siame described the review as very mature. Nthombz DanieLz Ngoma tagged Mr Mwamba and told him to take his flowers.

Writing in Bemba, Mr Felix Siya Mukonda marvelled at how quickly the beef between the two men had been settled, joking that Mr Kazadi had ended it in the blink of an eye.

Not everyone overlooked the criticism. Mr Mwewa Juma said the point about interpersonal skills matched his own view exactly, though he too gave credit for a storyline he loved. Mr James Maxmillan Makalani Banda put it simply: “In all honesty, it’s a good movie.”

The loudest call in the thread was for the two filmmakers to work together. Ms Glory Sampa said combining Mr Mwamba’s storytelling with Mr Kazadi’s technical experience could open doors to great things, a view echoed by Mr Kunda Chisenga and Ms Chipo Francine Kapoma.

Mc Heiz framed it in national terms. “We want to see you people working together on certain projects, the win for you guys is the win for the whole Zambia,” he wrote.

For Mr Mwamba, the endorsement arrives at a useful moment. The Ndola-based writer, director and producer rose to prominence with the soapie City on Fire for Zambezi Magic, and his credits also include Payback and Contravene. His Facebook page carries more than 930,000 followers.

He launched The Pawn’s trailer in Lusaka on 30 August before an audience of musicians, filmmakers and producers, and announced plans to feature more musicians in his future productions. The trailer hinted at a story built on power, betrayal and survival, the kind of drama Zambian audiences have long asked local filmmakers to deliver.

For viewers still on the fence, the case is now hard to dispute. A storyline praised even by a rival producer, a cast singled out for strong performances and a home-grown streaming platform built to keep Zambian stories in Zambian hands add up to a film worth an evening of anyone’s time.

Viewers can watch The Pawn on Capstone, Mr Mwamba’s own streaming platform. To find the right link and viewing details, fans should go through Mr Mwamba’s official Facebook page, Wyclif Mwamba, rather than unofficial uploads or forwarded links.

Fans who bought tickets for the disrupted premiere at Levy Mall have not lost out. Mr Mwamba said every ticket bought for that night remains valid and that a new screening date would be announced.

“You shall watch The Pawn,” he told fans.

Anyone searching online should check they have the right film. An American thriller from 1999 with the same title appears on several international streaming services, including Amazon Prime Video and Pluto TV. It is not the Zambian production, which stars Ms Mwaka Mugala and veteran actor Mr Clive Mwape in the leading roles.

Mr Kazadi is also preparing his own red-carpet event on 14 November, for which he said tickets reached 60 per cent capacity in just four days. That gives Zambian film fans two homegrown productions to back before the year closes.

Captain Alassane Diarra became the hero in Ndola, firing a late winner as Red Arrows edged South African giants Kaizer Chiefs 1-0 to keep alive Zambia’s hopes in CAF club competition.

Diarra struck inside the box from a corner to settle a tense CAF Confederation Cup Second Round first leg at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium, handing the Airmen a slender but crucial advantage ahead of the return leg in South Africa.

In a match where national pride was at stake, Arrows were the dominant force from start to finish, creating numerous chances in both halves while a cautious Chiefs side sat deep and relied on counter attacks.

It should have been more comfortable for the home side.

Arrows star Ackim Mumba will go home kicking himself after squandering two golden opportunities just before the break.

Twice Mumba was denied by Chiefs goalkeeper Renaldo Leaner, who produced stunning saves to keep his side alive.

But persistence finally paid off late on when Diarra pounced from close range after Arrows’ pressure from a corner, sending the Ndola crowd into raptures.

Arrows head coach Chisi Mbewe hailed his team’s performance, admitting he knew it would not be easy against a side with Chiefs’ continental maturity.

“I knew it wasn’t going to be an easy game playing against Kaizer Chiefs who have a lot of maturity in this competition. I’m so happy with the way the boys performed despite missing numerous chances,” Mbewe said.

“A 1-0 victory gives us advantage but we know the return leg in South Africa won’t be easy. So we have to prepare and go to South Africa to fight. Sometimes football can be like that, you create many chances but you end up scoring one goal,” he said.

For Chiefs, it was a sobering afternoon in Ndola. Coach Fernando Da Cruz conceded his side lacked aggression in the first half but insisted the tie is far from over.

“We played a tough first half with no aggression. In the second half we played better, we didn’t create many chances but had a better second half. We want to congratulate Red Arrows for this win,” Cruz said.

“Now we are focusing on the return leg at home. We know that we can win the match at home,” he said.

The victory means Red Arrows remain Zambia’s sole surviving representative in CAF club competitions this season, carrying the nation’s flag into the most difficult of assignments – a second leg away in Johannesburg where Kaizer Chiefs will be desperate to overturn the deficit in front of their massive home support.

But for now, the Airmen can savour a night when Zambian resilience overcame South African pedigree.

World.title: Councils implored to actualise economic expansion agenda
World.content:
Government has challenged local authorities to translate the Grow Zambia Agenda into practical and measurable results at community level.

Northern Province Acting Permanent Secretary, Beauty Undi-Phiri, underscored the need for councils to take a leading role in actualising economic expansion agenda.

Ms Undi-Phiri said this when she officiated at the installation ceremony for Kasama Mayor, Peter Yuda, held at Civic Centre grounds yesterday.

She noted that Kasama is well-positioned to contribute significantly to the realisation of the Grow Zambia Agenda through sectors such as agriculture, livestock production, trade, tourism, and small-scale enterprise development and that the council should take leading role in actualising opportunities.

“Kasama is well positioned to contribute to the Grow Zambia Agenda, I therefore encourage the council to work closely with stakeholders to support farmers, improve market infrastructure, promote value addition, attract both local and foreign investment and create an enabling environment for business growth,” Ms Undi-Phiri stated.

She further appealed to Mr Yuda and councilors to serve the people of Kasama with diligence regardless of their political affiliation.

“Let the interests of Kasama and its people always take precedence over individual and partisan considerations,” she said.

And the Acting Permanent Secretary has urged the council to spearhead constructive engagement with traders and provide practical solutions that promote lawful economic activity while ensuring orderly urban development.

And delivering his maiden speech, Mr Yuda pledged to work with the government through constructive and collaborative engagement.

He observed that Kasama residents are yearning for development hence the need to put politics aside and provide the much needed services.

“Development knows no political colour, bad roads affect every vehicle; poor sanitation threatens every family and economic hardship touches every household regardless of how they voted,” Mr Yuda said.

He added that there is need for the municipality to work with all stakeholders and come up with practical ideas aimed at increasing the revenue base.

The Mayor further called for the construction of key infrastructure in the district, among them, a modern abattoir and a dry port.

Kasama has 19 Councilors spread across the three Constituencies in the districts with three more Councilors elected under the Proportional Representation Electoral System.

World.title: Lavushimanda DC urges residents to go for HIV testing
World.content:
Lavushimanda District Commissioner Terries Kunda, has encouraged residents in the district to go for HIV testing services and know their HIV status.

‎

‎Speaking during the launch of the commemoration of HIV Testing, Counseling and Treatment (HTCT) Day held at Lukulu Health Center, in a speech read on his behalf by District Health Human Resource Management Officer, Oliver Chanda, Mr Kunda said Knowing one’s HIV status is a critical step towards protecting individual health, safeguarding families, and building healthier communities.

‎

‎Mr Kunda added that effective treatment is available for people who test positive for HIV, noting that early initiation of treatment, good adherence to medication and regular clinical follow-up, people living with HIV can live long, healthy and productive lives.

‎

‎“HIV is not a death sentence; it is an opportunity to take control of one’s health,” he said.

‎

‎He further emphasised the need to fight stigma and discrimination, noting that no one should be discouraged from seeking healthcare services for fear of being judged or rejected.

‎

‎Mr Kunda encouraged community members to create an environment where people can freely access HIV services, receive support and live with dignity.

‎

‎The District Commissioner also commended health workers for their continued commitment to improving the health of communities.

‎

‎He urged them to continue providing quality counselling, safeguarding clients’ confidentiality and treating every client with compassion and respect, noting that more efforts are needed to improve healthcare service delivery.

‎

‎Meanwhile, speaking at the same event, Mpumba Rural Health Centre Right to Care Zambia Professional Counsellor, Kennedy Bwalya, urged community members who test positive for HIV to adhere to their medications in order to improve their health

‎

‎Mr Bwalya explained that taking medications will reduce the spread of the virus as well as maintain better health.

‎

‎“When you go for HIV testing at health facilities and test positive, ensure that you start taking your medication. The medication will improve your health,” he said.

‎

‎This year’s 2026 HIV Testing, Counseling and Treatment Day is being commemorated under the theme “One Door, Many Services: Integrated Health for a Sustainable Future.”

World.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Hunger Crisis Takes an Emotional Toll on Caregivers #WorldFoodDay
World.content:
Fatima Ibrahimâs 23-month-old daughter, Aisha, was admitted to the Nilefa Kiji nutrition facility in Maiduguri after battling meningitis and repeated convulsions. The three weeks spent in hospital were filled with conflicting emotions. While grateful to see her daughter improve, Fatima could not stop thinking about the eight children she had left at home.

As millions of people across northern Nigeria face severe food insecurity, children continue to bear the consequences of a deepening malnutrition crisis. But the impact is far beyond the children in treatment. This can be a source of significant anxiety, exhaustion, and emotional distress for parents and caregivers, particularly those who spend weeks in the hospital when a child is severely malnourished and are concerned about starving children at home.

The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) estimates that 34.7 million people in Nigeria are in crisis levels of food insecurity during the lean season, while more than 5.4 million children are acutely malnourished. In northern Nigeria in 2025, MSF teams provided treatment to 425,634 children who were suffering from acute malnutrition.

The food crisis has particularly affected Nigeria's northeastern states of Borno, Adamawa and Yobe. It is estimated that by 2026 nearly 5.8 million people will be severely food insecure. In Borno State, conflicts, climate shocks and displacement are interfering with people's means of livelihood and damaging local food production, putting about 15,000 people at risk of suffering from catastrophic hunger.

The World Food Programme (WFP) has warned that ongoing insecurity is worsening hunger by forcing communities to flee their homes, preventing farmers from accessing their land and restricting the delivery of humanitarian assistance.

Monica Genya, Association Director at Doctors Without Borders (MSF) Southern Africa, described the "situation as critical," with medical teams treating children suffering from severe acute malnutrition and related illnesses.

In MSF nutrition facilities such as Nilefa Kiji in Maiduguri, she said, teams see intensive care units full of children fighting severe acute malnutrition. Many arrive severely wasted, and because malnutrition weakens their immunity, many also have illnesses such as measles, diphtheria and malaria, she said.

"It is severe, and it is life-threatening for many children," said Genya.

In 2025, MSF treated 353,989 children for severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and 90,723 for moderate acute malnutrition (MAM). She said that SAM is the most dangerous form that continues to claim young lives in the region. Children are severely wasted, and their immune systems are weakened. Some arrive at treatment facilities already suffering from diseases such as measles, diphtheria and malaria. Treatment can last anywhere from a week to more than a month, leaving caregivers facing prolonged separation from the rest of their families.

Genya said MSF treated 41.8 per cent more children for acute malnutrition in 2025 than in the previous year, reflecting a worsening crisis. Admissions have risen steadily since 2022, driven by insecurity, displacement, food shortages, disease outbreaks, economic hardship and cuts to humanitarian funding.

"These pressures compound one another, so more families are pushed to the edge each year," she said.

The rising number of children requiring treatment also raises questions about whether humanitarian resources are keeping pace with the need. MSF supports the state Ministries of Health in Zamfara, Katsina, Kebbi, Borno, Bauchi, Sokoto and Kano.

Abba Adamu Musa/MSF Inside a ward of MSFâs facility, Nilefa Kiji, in Maiduguri, Borno State, northeast Nigeria. Here, MSF provides care for children suffering from malnutrition.

Supporting caregivers as part of treatment

Genya said that the emotional burden carried by caregivers is often overlooked in discussions about child malnutrition, where attention tends to focus on medical treatment, admissions and recovery rates.

"Medical statistics capture admissions and recovery rates, but they cannot measure the emotional burden carried by the person at the bedside, who is most often the mother," she said. Caregivers endure fear, anxiety, guilt, uncertainty and emotional exhaustion, and some develop symptoms of depression."

The consequences extend beyond their own wellbeing. This matters for the child's recovery too. A caregiver's emotional wellbeing influences how engaged they stay in treatment, whether they follow medical advice and how well they can care for the child after discharge.

"Caring for the caregiver is part of caring for the child," she said.

The competing demands on caregivers are evident in the experiences MSF counsellors encounter at its nutrition facilities in northern Nigeria. "Caregivers are pulled in two directions," said Genya. "Many arrive with a critically ill child while having left other children at home, sometimes with no one to look after them and little to eat."

Their worry does not stop when treatment begins. Genya recalled the experience of a mother in Maiduguri.

"One mother in Maiduguri told us she had left eight children at home, and when she heard one had a fever and there was no money for treatment, she cried and could not eat. Another was asked by her eldest son when she was coming home, because the children were hungry without her," she said. In another case, counsellors met a mother of six who had to leave the hospital because her husband had left the children with neighbours and she could not bear to stay.

"These stories show how guilt, worry and separation can put a child's treatment at risk, which is why we listen and respond," she said.

Recognising the emotional toll of malnutrition, MSF incorporates mental health and psychosocial support into its nutrition programmes.

At Nilefa Kiji, caregivers receive psychological first aid on arrival, followed by individual counselling and group sessions where they can share experiences, express their fears and learn coping strategies. Caregiver education helps families understand and manage the emotional and behavioural challenges that can arise during and after treatment. Children take part in structured play activities that help restore a sense of normalcy during recovery.

"The support is also practical," she said.

Counsellors help distressed caregivers reach relatives by phone, and in some cases supervised home visits let a caregiver briefly check on their family before returning to finish their child's treatment. She said that this helps caregivers cope, builds their confidence, supports treatment adherence and contributes to better recovery. "Many regain hope as they watch their children get better, and some come back after discharge just to show how healthy their children have become," said Genya.

Beyond treating malnutrition

For MSF, addressing the crisis requires more than treating children after they have become severely malnourished. Families must also be reached earlier, before food insecurity and other pressures push children into life-threatening conditions.

Abba Adamu Musa/MSF MSF counsellor-educator Keturah John engages Adamaâs daughter, Fatima, in a play therapy session at MSFâs facility, Nilefa Kiji, in Maiduguri, Borno State, northeast Nigeria. Fatima is an inpatient and has been receiving treatment for malnutrition.

"Treating children once they are already severely malnourished saves lives, but we also need to reach families before they get to that point," she said.

Insecurity and displacement, disease outbreaks and economic hardship continue to undermine families' ability to provide adequate food and care. Genya said prevention and treatment must go hand in hand, alongside support for caregivers who bear much of the responsibility for children's recovery.

She added that the pressures pushing children into malnutrition, including insecurity and displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks and the economic crisis, are not easing. Sustained funding is needed not only for nutrition services but also for mental health and psychosocial support, she said. Governments and humanitarian organisations must work to ensure families can access essential assistance before children reach the point of severe malnutrition.

"This is why MSF's work focuses on both prevention and treatment, and why we care for the whole family, including the caregivers at the bedside, through counselling and psychosocial support. This work depends on public support," she said. "Donating to MSF's humanitarian efforts helps our teams keep reaching children across northern Nigeria, treating them early and supporting the families who care for them."

With over 5.4 million children acutely malnourished this year, every contribution makes a difference, she said.

As the world marks World Food Day, the experiences of families in northern Nigeria underline the need to recognise the human cost of food insecurity beyond the physical effects of hunger.

Genya said that addressing the crisis requires supporting caregivers alongside treating children. She said that there is a need to support caregivers through mental health and psychosocial services. She said that behind every child in our facilities is a caregiver, most often a mother, living with fear, anxiety, guilt and exhaustion. Many are worried sick about children left at home without enough food. Their emotional wellbeing shapes whether they can stay engaged in treatment, follow medical advice and keep caring for their child after discharge.

"Recognising and supporting caregivers is therefore key to ending this crisis, not a side issue," she said.

She urged donors to reconsider humanitarian funding cuts and sustain investment in nutrition care, including mental health and psychosocial support, to ensure children and their caregivers receive the help they need. "Behind every statistic is a caregiver's mental health impacted by malnutrition," said Genya.

The fear of losing a sick child, combined with guilt over being separated from other family members, can take a significant toll on their mental well-being. "A mother sits at a hospital bedside, grateful that her child is improving, while worrying that her other children at home have nothing to eat. She is afraid of losing the child in front of her, and guilty about those she can't be with," she said. "These are people showing extraordinary resilience under immense strain, and their stories rarely get told."

"Healing is not only about restoring a child's weight," said Genya. "It is also about restoring hope and resilience to the person who sits at the bedside every day."

World.title: Nigeria: Aircraft Loses Door Mid-Air, Makes Emergency Landing in Abuja
World.content:
The aircraft, a CL60 with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was departing Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred.

An aircraft operated by Triton Aviation made an emergency landing at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on Thursday after its crew reported that a door had opened mid-air shortly after take-off.

The aircraft, a CL60 with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was departing Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred.

According to a serious incident report, the aircraft took off from Runway 22 at 4:17 p.m. Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and, about three nautical miles from the airport, was climbing at 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call at 4:20 p.m.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The crew reported an open door in flight, prompting air traffic controllers to direct the aircraft back to Abuja for an emergency landing.

Airport fire and rescue personnel and the medical team were subsequently alerted and placed on standby in preparation for the aircraft's return.

The incident report stated that at about 4:29 p.m. UTC, the crew asked the Abuja control tower to confirm whether the door was open.

The duty air traffic controller attempted to observe the aircraft with binoculars but could not establish the door's condition because of the aircraft's position.

The crew was informed that the controller could not visually confirm the situation.

The aircraft landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 4:34 p.m. UTC, about 14 minutes after the Mayday call.

After landing, the controller observed that the aircraft's door was missing from the fuselage.

The aircraft was subsequently taxied to the international apron extension, where it was parked with the assistance of a marshaller.

Meanwhile, a video circulating on social media appears to show the aircraft's missing door. In the footage, an unidentified man said some farmers found the door while returning from their farm in the Abuja area.

He suggested that it had fallen from an aircraft but did not provide further details about the discovery. The circumstances surrounding the reported discovery have not been independently verified as of the time of filing this report.

The cause of the incident and the circumstances surrounding the door's detachment have not been established.

The number of people on board is also not immediately available.

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) confirmed that the incident occurred and said investigators have been deployed.

"Yes, it happened. The investigators are there. We will be releasing an official statement shortly," the bureau's media team said.

Close 

The Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Michael Achimugu, also confirmed the incident but said the NSIB has jurisdiction.

However, Triton Aviation could not be reached for comment when this report was filed.

World.title: South Africa: Lions Player Dies From Suspected Cardiac Arrest in French Hotel
World.content:
A Lions player has apparently died in a hotel room in France, where the South African team has been preparing for the Champions Cup debut against La Rochelle.

French media are reporting that a Lions player has died in a hotel room on the Île de Ré, where the South African team has been preparing for the Champions Cup debut against La Rochelle.

Île de Ré is an island off the western coast of France, and connected via a bridge to the mainland city of La Rochelle.

According to media reports in France, the player was found unresponsive in a shower cubicle.

Paramedics attempted to resuscitate him but were unsuccessful. He was pronounced dead. The player, in his thirties, was in cardiac arrest when emergency services arrived shortly before 10.30am.

Sources have independently confirmed the news to Daily Maverick, but the player's family have yet to be informed, so his name cannot be released.

It is unclear at this stage whether the Champions Cup match against two-time champions La Rochelle will go ahead, originally scheduled for Saturday, 17 October 2026. DM

World.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Establishes Six-Month Caretaker Administration in Tigray
World.content:
New admin tasked with restoring security, rebuilding institutions and preparing for elections

Ethiopia's federal government has established a six-month caretaker administration for the Tigray region, assigning it responsibility for restoring security, rebuilding damaged infrastructure and organizing elections intended to return the region to an elected government.

The Council of Ministers established the administration under a regulation following a decision by the House of Federation, which cited Article 62(9) of the Constitution and Article 14(2)(b) of Proclamation No. 359/1995 as the legal basis for establishing an interim administration in the region.



The government said repeated efforts to resolve the conflict in Tigray under the Pretoria peace agreement had failed, blaming the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) for obstructing implementation. It also accused the TPLF leadership of initiating renewed fighting, which it described as the group's fourth failed attempt to wage war.

The government said the new administration was intended to help Tigray emerge from prolonged conflict, restore peace and enable residents to exercise self-government and benefit from development.

From The Reporter Magazine

Drought Emergency or Seasonal Deficit ? Published on 2026-09-02 By The Reporter Magazine

What the Old Developmental State Got Wrong Published on 2026-10-02 By Samson Berhane

25-Year Sentences & Retroactive Laws: Controversial Draft Law Sparks Fears of Growing Authoritarianism in Tigray Published on 2026-06-21 By Yared Nigussie

Red Sea Rivalries: What a Shifting Geopolitical Landscape Means for Ethiopia and The Horn Published on 2026-08-31 By Yared Nigussie

Under its mandate, the caretaker administration will work to restore stability, rebuild government institutions and damaged infrastructure, resume interrupted social services and facilitate the return of displaced residents to their homes.

It will also coordinate with federal defense, police and security institutions, as well as regional security forces, to establish stability across the region, including at the local administrative level. Its responsibilities include facilitating the disarmament and reintegration of armed groups and restructuring the region's security apparatus.

A central objective is to establish conditions for free and transparent elections within six months, allowing Tigray to resume its place as a regular component of Ethiopia's federal system under an elected government.

The administration will also coordinate media activities, organize public forums and undertake measures intended to promote reconciliation, rebuild public confidence and prepare residents for reconstruction and development.

The government said the caretaker administration must base its activities on Ethiopia's national interests and territorial integrity, as well as the fundamental interests of the people of Tigray.

Its authority will be limited to providing routine regional services and creating conditions for the next election. It will not undertake matters with longer-term strategic implications, the government said, and will operate under the direction and supervision of the federal government.

The administration's senior officials are Asefa Abraha Hagos, chief executive for administration and public services; Tewodros Aregay Woldeselassie (PhD), chief executive for the economy and reconstruction; Gebre Egziabher Beyene Hailu (Brig. Gen.), chief executive for security and peace; and Redae Hailuom Woldeselassie, chief executive for political affairs and public organization.

Shishay Amare (PhD) was appointed mayor of Mekele, the regional capital.

The federal government will provide direction, support and oversight for the officials' activities, according to the announcement.

World.title: Malawi: Gold Rush or Gold Bust? Malawi's Smuggling Crackdown Faces Credibility Test
World.content:
Malawi's latest bid to turn gold into a lifeline for its struggling economy is facing uncomfortable questions about the evidence on which it has been built.

A state-backed scheme designed to intercept gold before it is smuggled out of the country rests on a headline-grabbing claim that $100 million worth of the precious metal is lost annually through illegal trade. Yet, according to an analysis by Collins Mtika for the Mail & Guardian and the Centre for Investigative Journalism Malawi, the figure has never been publicly explained.

The programme, spearheaded by the Malawi Mining Investment Company (Mamico), aims to buy gold from artisanal miners operating at roughly 100 sites nationwide, funnel it through buying centres in Lilongwe, Kasungu and Nkhotakota, and ultimately sell it to the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM).

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

But a closer examination of the numbers reveals a troubling inconsistency.

Earlier this year, Mamico reported findings from a month-long assessment which estimated that more than $700 million worth of gold was being lost each year through illicit activity and identified 81 illegal mining sites.

The latest estimate is seven times lower. At the same time, the number of mining locations linked to the programme has increased to around 100.

The analysis asks a simple question: which number is accurate?

Without a published methodology, there is no way to test either claim. For a project requiring hundreds of billions of kwacha in public and private financing, that gap matters.

Mamico says it will need K85 billion to fund its first three months of operations and around K300 billion annually thereafter. The company has enlisted FDH Bank and NBS Bank as partners, but key parts of the commercial framework are still unresolved.

Most notably, the arrangement depends on an offtake agreement with the RBM that has yet to be concluded.

The uncertainty extends beyond the figures.

The analysis points to potential duplication between Mamico's planned operations and an existing RBM gold-purchasing initiative run through the Export Development Fund.

By September, that programme had already acquired about 1.63 tonnes of gold, raising questions about whether the government is creating parallel structures within the same market.

There is also a more fundamental challenge. Artisanal miners will only sell through official channels if they can secure competitive prices and prompt payment.

If unofficial traders offer better deals, the incentive to bypass the formal system remains intact, regardless of how many buying centres are established.

Close 

Yet the pressure to make the project work is immense.

Malawi's foreign exchange position remains fragile. Official reserves stood at $600.6 million in September, enough to cover just 2.4 months of imports, below the internationally recognised three-month benchmark.

Gold has emerged as one of the few commodities capable of generating substantial foreign currency earnings. In April alone, the RBM exported 589.95 kilogrammes of locally purchased gold valued at $75.09 million.

For ministers and policymakers, the allure is obvious: bring more gold into formal channels and bolster dwindling reserves.

But as Mtika's analysis suggests, the success of the strategy may hinge less on ambition than on transparency.

Until Mamico discloses how it calculated its smuggling estimates, clarifies how it will coexist with existing state-run gold programmes, and produces verifiable data on production, purchases and exports, the initiative will continue to face a credibility problem.

For now, the government's gold rush is asking the public to trust numbers it has yet to prove.

World.title: Somalia: Somalia's Govt Welcomes Election Timetable and Urges Political Dialogue
World.content:
Mogadishu — Somalia's federal government on Thursday welcomed an election timetable announced by the Independent National Electoral and Boundaries Commission, covering elections for both houses of parliament and the president.

In a statement dated October 15, 2026, the government described the timetable as an important step towards implementing the electoral process and strengthening democracy in the country.

The government said it had spent the past 18 months offering opportunities for consultation and negotiations aimed at helping Somali political stakeholders reach agreement on key national issues, particularly the electoral process.

It said the consultations would continue, adding that it remained committed to securing a broad-based understanding among the country's political actors.

The government described its support for the election timetable and its continued commitment to dialogue as complementary efforts that would help preserve stability, strengthen national unity and safeguard citizens' constitutional rights.

It called on all political stakeholders to engage in consultations in good faith and with a sense of national responsibility, urging them to work together to ensure peaceful elections that strengthen public confidence and Somalia's state institutions.

The statement comes amid political differences over Somalia's electoral process, including disagreements over the proposed arrangements and calls for an inclusive political agreement.

World.title: South Africa: Masemola Back As Police Commissioner After Ramaphosa Lifts Suspension
World.content:
Masemola was placed on precautionary suspension in April 2026 after appearing in court on charges linked to a R360-million police health services tender.

Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane has served as acting National Police Commissioner, and Ramaphosa says she served with distinction.

President Cyril Ramaphosa has lifted the suspension of National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola, who will resume his full duties on Monday, 19 October.

The Presidency made the announcement on Friday.

Ramaphosa and Masemola agreed in April 2026 that Masemola would be deemed to be on precautionary suspension. This followed his appearance in the Pretoria Magistrate's Court on charges of contravening the Public Finance Management Act. The charges were linked to a R360-million police health services tender awarded to Medicare24.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi ordered the charges to be withdrawn after a review found no reasonable prospects of a successful prosecution on 15 September. The Pretoria Magistrate's Court formally withdrew the charges on 22 September.

Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, the police's chief financial officer, was appointed acting National Police Commissioner when Masemola was suspended.

Ramaphosa thanked her and said she served with distinction in the interim.

"The President welcomes the National Police Commissioner on his return to his full duties," presidential spokesperson Vincent Magwenya said.

The South African Policing Union had urged Ramaphosa to lift the suspension after the charges were withdrawn. After the withdrawal, Masemola told the media that he had not heard from the president.

The National Prosecuting Authority has also referred the case to the oversight judge of the Investigating Directorate Against Corruption, to look into whether there was any malice behind the original charges.

World.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Nominates Four New INEC National Commissioners, Two Resident Electoral Commissioners
World.content:
press release

President Tinubu urged the Senate to expedite the nominees' confirmation in view of the forthcoming general elections next January.

President Bola Tinubu has nominated four new national commissioners and two new resident electoral commissioners to fill vacancies at the Independent National Electoral Commission created by expiring tenures.

The Senate will scrutinise all the nominees.

However, the president reappointed Bala Bila, the national commissioner representing the North East.

The new national commissioners are Mustapha Aliu, who will replace Abdullahi Zuru as the North West representative; and Bashir Muhammed Umar, who will replace Muhammad Adamu as the North Central representative.

President Tinubu recommended Oluwatoyin Babalola, the resident electoral commissioner in Osun, as the new South West national commissioner. She will replace Cornelius Ajayi, whose tenure expires on 24 October.

The two new resident electoral commissioners are retired permanent secretary Samuel Akinleye, to represent Ekiti State, and Zahradden Sanusi, from Jigawa, who will replace Saidu Babura.

President Tinubu urged the Senate to expedite the nominees' confirmation in view of the forthcoming general elections next January.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information and Strategy)

16 October 2026

World.title: Homan says Ilhan Omar could be stripped of naturalization, deported if immigration fraud is proven

Border czar Tom Homan said Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., could be denaturalized and deported if investigators find that she committed immigration fraud, repeating his assertion that no one is above the law after her home was raided and cellphone seized.

"Of course, if you lie during the naturalization process, there is a process to denaturalize somebody. We've done it before... And certainly, if the evidence points that way, that could happen," Homan told "The Big Weekend Show" on Saturday.

Omar is under federal investigation over allegations that she or her father lied about her birth year on immigration paperwork to obtain her citizenship when her family fled Somalia in the late 1990s.

DEMOCRATS' FURY OVER ILHAN OMAR RAID DRAWS STINGING GOP REMINDER ABOUT RAID FROM THE PAST: ‘SET THE PRECEDENT’

Her father became a U.S. citizen in 2000. Omar was believed to be 17 at the time, and, as a minor, automatically qualified for citizenship under U.S. law along with him. But, recently, it’s been alleged she was actually 18 and would have needed to go through the process herself at that point.

Omar and other Democrats, including House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., have denounced the probe as political persecution of one of President Donald Trump's detractors weeks before a critical election.

OBAMA BACKS ILHAN OMAR AMID PROBE, ACCUSES TRUMP ADMIN OF 'APPALLING' TARGETING IN LENGTHY STATEMENT

World.title: 'The Chosen' actor endorses James Talarico, claims candidate reflects real 'Christian values'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

'The Chosen' actor Jordan Walker Ross endorsed Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on Thursday, helping launch a faith-based voter coalition ahead of November's election while drawing criticism from a Republican state lawmaker over taxpayer-funded Hollywood subsidies.

Ross, who portrays the apostle Little James in the popular faith-based television series, announced his endorsement in a campaign video promoting "Faithful Texans for Talarico," an initiative intended to attract religious voters.

"A lot of politicians like to talk about Christian values, but you don’t really see that reflected in their legislation or the way that they live, but you do see that in the way that James lives. He loves his neighbor; he takes care of the needy, the sick, the immigrant," Ross said.

A spokesperson for Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton's campaign slammed Talarico's appeals to Christian voters in a statement to Fox News Digital, accusing the Democrat of using his religious beliefs to justify progressive positions on social issues.

'OFFICE' STAR SAYS JAMES TALARICO'S RELIGIOUS BELIEFS 'ACHINGLY CLOSE' TO JESUS CHRIST

"Everything about James Talarico is fake," the spokesperson said. "He uses his beliefs to justify his most radical positions, all while calling himself ‘a Christian who hates Christianity.’ In Talarico’s twisted version of Christianity, a follower of Christ is required to bend the knee at thealtar of the radical trans agenda, disavow the oil and gas industry, support late-term abortion, and open the door to every criminal illegal immigrant seeking asylum. I’m still looking through the Bible to find those passages, but I wouldn’t call it Christian."

Texas state Rep. Brian Harrison, R-Texas, also criticized the endorsement on X, accusing state lawmakers of subsidizing actors who support Democrats.

"Your money is being used to help elect Democrats like James Talarico," he said.

Harrison also took aim at Texas Senate Bill 22, which expanded Texas' film incentive program. Texas Film Commission records show that The Chosen Texas LLC received approximately $862,527 for its second season in 2022 and another $1.995 million for its fourth season in March 2025, totaling near $2.86 million. Both payments preceded the new legislation's September 2025 effective date.

In a follow-up statement to Fox News Digital, Harrison slammed the film program as a "socialist scheme to give billions of tax dollars to rich, woke, Hollywood leftists." He argued that production offsets "directly or indirectly" subsidize actor salaries, pledging to introduce legislation next session to repeal the "indefensible" Hollywood subsidies.

NETFLIX CHIEF ADMITS TRUMP IS HELPING SHOWBIZ INDUSTRY AS FEDERAL TAX CREDIT BILL AIMS TO FUEL HOLLYWOOD JOBS

Ross defended the film incentives and rejected the suggestion that actors' political endorsements should affect production opportunities.

"The growing film industry in TX creates thousands of jobs for Texans who fall on both sides of the aisle," Ross said, in a statement Sunday to Fox News Digital. "For Harrison to suggest that those opportunities should be taken away simply because some actors — like myself — endorse Democratic candidates is unconstitutional. One of the beautiful things about our country is the right to voice our opinions and I encourage my fellow actors/filmmakers (on the right AND left) to do the same."

"I believe it’s time for a change and that James Talarico offers a clear vision for how to create those changes," he continued.

COWBOYS LEGEND RANDY WHITE ENDORSES KEN PAXTON, WARNS JAMES TALARICO ‘CAN’T BE TRUSTED’

Brittany Hughes, a video host at the Media Research Center, criticized Ross' endorsement in a statement to Fox News Digital, arguing that his role as an apostle on "The Chosen" did not make him an authority on Christian teachings.

"As is any American, Ross is free to vote for whatever candidate he chooses," she said. "But American voters aren’t obligated to take a theological lesson from an actor simply because he plays an apostle on TV."

"It’s a simple fact that many of Talarico’s public positions are in total opposition to basic Christian principles — his support for so-called gender transitioning, for example, which is completely at odds with the biblical description of God having created us male and female separately and for separate purposes," she added.

TALARICO DISMISSES PAST COMMENTS ABOUT GOD AND GENDER AS 'PROVOCATIVE' WHILE INVOKING CHARLIE KIRK

Lisa Cusack, president of the Don't L.A. My Burbank PAC, criticized the endorsement in a statement to Fox News Digital, questioning whether Hollywood actors could influence Texas voters.

"I highly doubt this will help Talarico with voters, but Ross’ outspoken progressive politics could alienate Christian audiences from The Chosen. Christians and Texas voters can see through this kind of set piece Christianity," she said. "Theater kids generally make terrible political pundits."

Ross rejected the idea that political differences necessarily alienate fans, saying he welcomes conversations with viewers who disagree with him.

"As a progressive actor on a TV show with a largely conservative audience, I’ve had so many wonderful opportunities to engage in challenging conversations with my fans and I also do so from a place of compassion and curiosity. When we do that, we can learn so much from one another."

Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian, faces Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who announced his own "Pastors for Paxton" coalition with 27 faith leaders the same week.

World.title: Canadian PM Carney says 4 service members killed, dozens injured in military base fire
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Sunday that four service members were killed and dozens more seriously injured after a fire broke out during military training at a base in Alberta, calling it one of the country's worst peacetime military tragedies on domestic soil.

The deadly fire erupted Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where fierce winds fueled flames that spread beyond the installation and into surrounding rural areas. Canadian military officials said there were no indications of terrorism, though the cause remained under investigation.

Carney said in a televised address that the families of the four service members killed had been notified and that the situation was still evolving.

AT LEAST 1 KILLED, 34 FIREFIGHTERS AND EMS WORKERS INJURED IN 'MAJOR' STATEN ISLAND SHIPYARD EXPLOSION: FDNY

The prime minister said those affected included reservists and soldiers from Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry, one of Canada's oldest military regiments. Personnel had traveled from bases across the country to participate in training exercises at Wainwright.

Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty initially confirmed fatalities and injuries but did not provide a casualty count, Fox News Digital previously reported.

"I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister, but I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory," McGuinty told reporters.

The exact number of injured service members remained unclear Sunday, with victims receiving treatment at hospitals in Wainwright, Edmonton, Red Deer and Calgary.

Several hospitals across Alberta activated a "Code Orange," an emergency designation for mass-casualty incidents, as medical personnel scrambled to treat the wounded.

"This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton," Dr. Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at Royal Alexandra Hospital, told CBC News. "It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster."

MARINE CORPS OSPREY CATCHES FIRE DURING EXERCISE IN NORTH CAROLINA; 4 INJURED

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers responded to reports of a fire in a training area at the base shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday. Firefighters battled intense winds, with gusts reaching up to 62 mph, as flames spread beyond the installation.

By late Saturday, local officials said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order had been issued for nearby residents.

McGuinty said the RCMP was involved in investigating the incident, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate."

Carney announced that flags would fly at half-staff on federal buildings nationwide in honor of those killed and injured. He also praised emergency crews who battled the flames through the night.

Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

World.title: Poll: Americans are anxious, pessimistic and deeply unhappy with Trump ahead of the midterms
World.content:
Weeks ahead of Election Day, 71% of U.S. adults think the country is on the “wrong track.” It’s the highest share yet in President Donald Trump’s second term, illustrating the grim national mood his party faces in the midterm elections, according to a new NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey.

Poll respondents expressed deep unhappiness over economic conditions and widespread distrust toward both major political parties, but Trump and Republicans bore the brunt. For the first time in Trump’s second term, the poll has found the “right track” sinking into the 20s. A majority of Americans view the president’s administration as uniquely corrupt, even as they look skeptically at corruption in both parties. And they say Trump is failing to improve their material financial conditions.

Trump’s approval rating slipped to 34% among U.S. adults, a second-term low in this poll, while his disapproval rating rose to 66%. In another warning sign, the poll found a majority (51%) of respondents “strongly disapprove” of his performance, a second-term high.

Trump’s approval rating is slightly better among registered voters, 39%-61%. Registered voters said they prefer Democrats over Republicans to control Congress by a 55%-45% spread, another sign that the GOP’s House and Senate majorities are in danger in the Nov. 3 election.

Yet despite the sinking ratings for the party in power, Americans continue to hold a negative view of Democrats, too. Among adults, just 43% view the Democratic Party favorably, while 57% hold an unfavorable view.

The survey found that 37% have a favorable opinion of the Republican Party, while 63% view it unfavorably.

The president’s approval rating is 76% with Republican adults. That represents a drop from his previous numbers among members of his own party, fueled by a decline among Republicans who consider themselves more a supporter of the party than a supporter of the MAGA movement. Meanwhile, Trump’s approval rating sits at 21% with independents.

Among men under 30 — a group Trump won by 1 point in 2024 exit polling — his approval rating sits at 28%. And among Latinos, who also shifted toward Trump in 2024, his approval rating is 31%.

The poll highlights the tricky balancing act facing Republican candidates in competitive states and districts as they simultaneously try to energize GOP voters who continue to support Trump without alienating Americans who disapprove of the administration.

Among adults, 58% said Trump’s policies are hurting the country, while 28% said they are helping the country. Another 14% said they aren’t making a difference.

When broken down by issues, Trump’s approval rating is 27% on handling the cost of living, 29% on handling the war with Iran and 33% on his handling of AI. On his best issue, border security and immigration, 43% of adults approve.

Economic concerns are at the center of the sour national mood, with the economy once again topping the list of most important issues at 31%. While 18% of Americans said their financial situation is better off today than a year ago, 38% said it’s about the same and 44% said it’s worse now.

The results provided detail on how rising inflation, which last month rose to 3.7% year over year, has weighed on Americans’ daily lives.

Gas prices were described as a “very serious” or “somewhat serious” problem by 67% of respondents. Majorities said economic conditions have caused them to change what groceries they buy to live within their means, and to cut back on spending to afford necessities.

Pluralities also said they’ve cut back on electricity use, changed or canceled travel plans or delayed a major purchase as a result, according to the poll.

Trump has sought to appeal to voters by promising $5,000 payments if Republicans win the 2026 midterms. But the new poll showed that most U.S. adults aren’t buying it: Just 14% said they “definitely” or “probably” expect to receive such a check if the GOP keeps control of Congress, while 71% think they “definitely” or “probably” won’t.

Self-identified Republicans are among those who don’t appear to buy the president’s pledge, with 47% saying they don’t expect to receive the $5,000 payment Trump promised, while 28% do.

Corruption also registered as a major concern, with Americans harboring skepticism about both parties.

More than half (52%) of U.S. adults said in the poll that they find his administration “more corrupt” than previous administrations, while about 1 in 4 said it’s less corrupt and another 1 in 4 said the current administration is about as corrupt as predecessors.

A 56% majority also said corruption is equally bad in both parties, while another 25% said it’s a bigger problem inside the GOP and 17% said it’s worse among Democrats.

The dissatisfaction may be reshaping what Americans want in a politician. In another edition of this poll one year ago, Americans said by a 16-point margin they prefer an insider with the experience to get things done over an outsider who shakes up the system. That margin narrowed to 4 points in the new poll.

Among Democrats, the survey also found indicators of diminishing trust in the party’s establishment and an openness to different kinds of candidates.

When asked to pick one or the other, 52% of self-identified Democrats said they’re more of a supporter of progressive causes and the progressive movement, while 48% said they’re more of a supporter of the Democratic Party.

Among Democratic-aligned adults, 42% said they consider themselves to be democratic socialists, while 58% said they do not.

And despite Trump’s unpopularity, the country was split almost evenly on whether a potential Democratic-led House should begin impeachment proceedings: 52% said it should, while 48% said it should not go down that path.

The NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey surveyed 19,135 adults online from Sept. 28 to Oct. 12 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 2.6 percentage points.

World.title: Trump announces plans to renovate D.C. golf course amid legal battle
World.content:
President Donald Trump announced in a Truth Social post on Sunday that the administration has developed a plan to redevelop the East Potomac Golf Links course in Washington, D.C., which has been at the center of a legal battle over his renovation plans.

Trump said that the Interior Department worked with golf course architect Tom Fazio to develop “a plan to build a World Class Championship Golf Course on the site of the current East Potomac Golf Links, located in Washington, D.C.”

“When completed, it will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments such as the U.S. Open, the PGA Championship, the Ryder Cup, and the Presidents Cup,” Trump said in the post.

He said that the renovations would begin on Nov. 15 and take about 15 months.

The proposed renovation, though, has already been challenged in court by a preservation group and two D.C. residents.

Following Trump’s Truth Social post, U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes ordered the administration to inform her whether they still plan to argue that there remains no “final agency action” and that Trump’s plan to rebuild the East Potomac Golf Course is purely “preliminary.”

Justice Department attorneys have long argued that any plans to turn East Potomac into a championship-style golf course were simply hypothetical and not rooted in any formal plan.

National Park Service officials also told Reyes last week that they were aware of no formal plan to renovate East Potomac beyond what they saw from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Trump’s previous social media posts.

Last week, Reyes forbade the administration from cutting down more trees at the course through Oct. 26. The administration had cut down hundreds of trees from the course, causing Reyes to hit back, saying she was “furious.”

Log sections cut from trees at the East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C., on Monday. Mark Schiefelbein / Getty

“I was hearing from everyone on plaintiffs’ side this was going to happen. I said repeatedly, ‘No, I trust the government.’ I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done,” Reyes responded at the time.

She also said that incident “cost the government all of its credibility.”

Reyes said that the administration must provide her and the plaintiffs three business days’ written advance notice before making any “irreparable modification” to the golf course. The judge previously rejected the plaintiffs’ request for a restraining order because lawyers for the Trump administration said they would provide ample notice of large-scale work.

On Friday, the administration asked Reyes to recuse herself from the case, arguing that her “histrionics in prior hearings have clearly demonstrated she is no longer impartial.”

The judge will hold a hearing Monday in which she has called on the acting director of the National Park Service and the Interior Department’s chief of staff to testify under oath. Reyes on Sunday also required Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward to attend the hearing.

In Sunday’s Truth Social post, Trump said that the “current Course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect.”

The golf course renovation is the latest in a string of major changes the president has tried to make to the D.C. landscape. He is continuing to build the White House ballroom and has pushed forward on plans to build a “triumphal arch.” His handpicked Kennedy Center board also voted to close the renowned arts center for renovations, and the administration moved to renovate the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, though the lining ended up peeling.
